docs.title: The Essence of Truth
docs.text:
and its Relation to Story

You have entered a realm whose birth succeeds its existence. No, we didn't mean to say precedes, we indeed mean to tell you that the period of time that this realm has existed is shorter than the length of its entire history. To understand this, we will need to strip ourselves of our preconceptions, toss out what we knew before reading this, and come to the table with a fresh set of eyes (ideally your own).

truth /tro͞oTH/ noun:

A story we tell ourselves to make sense of the world around us. Oftentimes in terms of relativity to other known concepts.

docs.title: Yes and NoThe Art of Storycraft
docs.text:
Imagine. An individual, a regal one at that, has a craving. We do not need to know who this individual is, just that they are royalty and therefore are accustomed to receiving that which they request, and that which they are requesting is an apple.

"Bring me an apple! I must have one at once!"

The regent waits, not for an uncomfortable amount of time. The regent is particular, but is aware of the expected amount of time that must pass before the regent's request may be fulfilled. After this not uncomfortable amount of time passes, a subject presents the regent with an item.

"An apple for you, high regent, as you requested."

Presenting it in a white linen wrapping, the subject displays in their hands a round, red fruit, with a rounded hexagonal form and a crown-like growth where it was plucked by the stem. Presented in a white linen wrapping before the high regent, who had requested an apple, is a plump pomegranate.

"What is the meaning of this? I had requested an apple! Not some bitter excuse of an approximation of one..."

...is how you might have expected this interaction to proceed. But, as storytellers, we can blur the lines between truth and falsehood, yes and no, right and wrong. And we do this by adding dimensions of truth. Consider: if ALL of the facts of the world were placed on a straight line, where the coordinate of a fact represented one unique statement, and each had a value of either "true" or "false."

If we found the coordinate point for "The regent requested an apple" in the context of this story, its statement value would be "true," because we have established it to be just so. We have also established "The subject brought the regent a pomegranate" to be true. Now, in the world as we know it, if we traveled further down the line, the phrase "The regent is satisfied with the knowledge that his request has been fulfilled" would be marked as false. But this is assuming that what we've been trained to know still applies.

At some point, "A pomegranate is not an apple" has been deemed as true. But what if it also wasn't? What if "A pomegranate is not an apple" could also be false? But narrator, then we would have two contradicting truth values for the same point on our line! Correct! Which is where we propose that truth has dimension. It is possible for truth to also be falsehood, as long as the proper dimensions and context are built around it. The only time two dots share a coordinate on a line yet have two different values is when there is an underlying umpteenth dimension that would give them separate identities.

Before we make this sound too complicated, thankfully this story has a simple solution. The term "apple," at its origin of use, was not used to solely refer to the fruit that comes from the tree known as Malus domestica, or whichever cousin of the apple tree existed at the time of the creation of the word "apple." "Apple" was used to refer to ALL fruits, and slowly after some linguistic prototype mumbo jumbo and a really long period of civilizational social development yadda yadda, "apple" evolved to refer to the fruit it evokes in your mind today. So, giving this story a linguistic dimension and flexibility to consider that a word you understand today may not mean what you think it means (just ask Inigo Montoya), we can end our short story with:

"This is much appreciated, dear subject. If you would be so kind as to bring me my paring knife?"

As storytellers, we must become experts in holding contradictive truths simultaneously. This may be easier said than done, though fictional genres like fantasy and science fiction would not have been able to be developed without this technique: they tell of protagonists who make possible the impossible, they describe incomprehensible horrors who only pose a threat when witnessed and comprehended, and they speak of the unreal made real.

Take for example the following hypothetical facts:

  1. "I killed them."
  2. "I saved their life."

While keeping the Agent and Theme constant (the actor and "actee", per se), there are several ways to add dimensions of truth to make these contradicting phrases simultaneously hold true.

We could, for example, add some specificity. Maybe the definition of "kill" in this circumstance, was entirely technical. A doctor who saves a patient during open-heart surgery must stop the heart and use a bypass machine. If one's definition of "killing" included stopping their heart, this may allow these two phrases to be true simultaneously.

We could instead add a dimension of relative time. One could feasibly save someone's life, and then also kill the same person. However, is it possible to switch the time relation? Perhaps the previous example could be stretched to be considered killing someone and then saving their life immediately afterwards, but narratively the two actions were part of the same process. We begin to see how fictional genres are born when we start to stretch the boundaries of our own understandings of the world. For one to kill another person through one act or process, and then save their life after some time has passed, we need to create a dimension of truth of our own. The power to bring back the long dead, though impossible in our world, is precisely the product of the practice we are proposing for transcendent fantasy storytelling: nothing is impossible so long as you extrapolate farther for new dimensions of truth.

docs.title: An Entire World's Truth
docs.text:
Umbrea is not the world you'll be playing in. This preface is just a fancy way of preparing you for this fact. This world is a convergence of truths, where the pivotal contradictions were given new dimensions of truth to reach an equilibrium. "Umbrea" is just one of the two superimposed existences that now exist within the same dimensional sphere in the cosmos.

In the broad strokes of things, Umbrea exists within a larger cosmos, whose essence comprises the space between stars, the supposedly insurmountable space between different existences. These existences reside in places called spheres: spheres of influence, spheres of truth; these spheres contain within them a unique set of rules and defined truths that its contents must follow. Because of this, the setting of Umbrea is inclusive to other campaign settings that may not exactly follow the lore of the main campaign setting detailed in this guide.

In our sphere, the planet of Tsindwr (/'sin-dur/) is circled by a set of twelve moons of varying sizes, orbits, and compositions. Without a local sun to light the land of Umbrea, these moons and their backdrop of stars are the best way for scholars to keep track of the days and passing time.

These moons are some of the last remaining proof of the existence of the gods. Some say they first came to Tsindwr on these moons, some believe they built them when they arrived as their personal domains, and some suspect that the moons are the corpses of the dead gods themselves. What we do know of our world's first visitors, can be found in the mythos of an ancient elven civilization who later left Tsindwr to travel the stars.

The astral elves, or Shimylv, were the first to settle Tsindwr. What has been recovered of their history has either been restored from artistic reliefs, inferred from their arcane artifacts, or passed through word of mouth by their descendants. Their advancement in the mystic arts and astromancy suggests the possibility of other records of their civilization, though these methods of storing histories have yet to be discovered or decoded.

Their more base methods of records were oft reserved for their mythology, which is why we have record of the gods' few stories. This includes the events leading to their downfall: the conclusion to a war between the Divines and the Primordials. Originating from the adjacent planes of elemental chaos, the Primordials wanted Tsindwr for themselves: a playground of their destruction and constant rebirth. The Divines had other plans: a world of creation and evolution, something new to be perceived and discovered by its inhabitants.

However, a group of the Divines wanted to explore their destructive capabilities alongside the Primordials, and thus the Pantheon was split in two. Though a trickster god called Nlyoz-a, or The Light, knew a way to resolve this conflict, though at no one's benefit in particular. She had overheard Tbedw-na, or The Spider, speak of a ritual that could empower Tsindwr with the Divine souls, protecting it from further encroachment from the Primordials. Confident in her ability to finish the ritual, Nlyoz-a snuck into Tbedw-na's domain and stole the ritual texts.

The ritual required the cooperation of all of the Divines, and great sacrifice too, so Nlyoz-a devised a ruse. She added a clause to the ritual's final revision, and told both the Divines of Creation and the Divines of Destruction that this clause would protect them from the sacrifice needed by the ritual. Consulting with both groups at once, Nlyoz-a coordinated the ritual to be conducted contemporaneously from opposite sides of the world. What the rest of the Divines did not know, was that Nlyoz-a was conducting a third ritual, the final clause, in another location, and meant to only spare herself from the toll required by Tbedw-na's magic. She only intended to have Tsindwr for herself for a few decades before releasing her siblings, but her clause was flawed, and she ultimately needed to join her brethren in sacrifice to stabilize the final spell. In the end, all souls of the Divine were separated from their avatars, and imbued within the land of the Material Plane, imbuing it with a newfound planar boundary more stable and protective.

Scholars theorize that the gods now imbue the latent planar permanence of nature and its forces, though some theorize that they slumber in ancient tombs, dispersing their divine influence in radial areas around them. Skeptics are convinced they have been dead for a long time, and there's no use in waiting for their return.

docs.title: Elfin Legacy
docs.text:
The Shimylv were the first to harness the dichotomic essences of Gloam and Faerie that permeate the world of Tsindwr. In most other spheres, the planes of the Feywild and the Shadowfell have been separated from the primary or Material Plane, however this is always done through the will of the gods. In Tsindwr, where the Divines are absent, the Material Plane still has its brightest and darkest aspects, giving its environment a polarizing and diverse level of magical infusion. Because of this, it is common for the innate nature of the land to imbue the living with consciousness and the dead with life. Much like the Feywild, one's environment can be influenced by one's mood, and much like the Shadowfell, the environment itself can influence its inhabitant's emotions. This made the land of Umbrea very volatile, and nearly uninhabitable, until the Shimylv introduced the Obelisks.

Great stone pillars with tapered tops were inscribed with constellations of arcane sigils and names, anchoring the nature of its surroundings to become stable enough to hold a single form, a single identity. The Shimylv were the first mortals to assign True Names to the land, quite literally setting them in stone to allow for stationary settlements and safe throughways. Without them, Umbrea was a roiling mass of whim and terror, where incorporeal presences haunted every shadow and mesmerizing swirls of enchanting spirits led wandering souls to their eternal entrapment.

For the most part, the evidence of the astral elves and their mystically-advanced civilization lives on in ancient abandoned cities carved of a singular stone structure. None have yet been able to reproduce the grandeur of their architecture, but there are those that search their ruins for enlightenment. Many of the names taken by large cities and assigned to major land formations are also influenced by the psychic presence of the True Names assigned to them by the Shimylv, though the passing of time has allowed them to shift and evolve with language. The last chapter of Shimylv civilization that we know of is their encounter with an intradimensional horror that leaked into Tsindwr, in the vast network of caves below the surface called the Kagecombs.

The entity was only ever pictured as a kaleidoscope of blank eyes, writhing tendrils, and dendritic mineral growths. It was never named or recorded in writing, so we will refrain from doing so in this recounting. What we can tell you is that the remains of this defeated entity were what fed the mineral growths in the depths below, and created a unique resource to be studied and harnessed by an elfin outpost that later became the dominion of Sauztein Geb. After sundering this entity, the Shimylv seem to all have left this plane for the stars; very rarely do these elves return to Umbrea but it has been known to happen occasionally.

docs.title: Beneath the Footfalls of Titans
docs.text:
Millenia passed between the visitations of the Shimylv and the evolution of sentient anthropoid species, the first of which being the Mulburrows. The faerie essence of Tsindwr allowed for an advanced rate of evolution and change amongst its organic inhabitants, and was often influenced by the wills in its vicinity. This is likely why Mulburrows came to be during the Age of Titans. Lesser elementals from the Primordial Sea had found entryways into the Material Plane that were too small to allow Primordials to pass through but gave Titans such as giants and dragons a backdoor to explore a realm previously void of civilization. The presence of intelligent life was quite possibly the final piece required for the birth of the first unique race of Tsindwr.

The Mulburrow people were brought into the world while the elemental Titans attempted to shape and colonize the land. These fleet-footed smallfolk became quickly accustomed to using the nature around them to create camouflaged and portable shelters; they were always on the move. They began relying on the innate magics of the flora and imitating the practices of the fauna around them, slowly discovering a pattern to their formation and rituals. The Mulburrow civilization was the first to diverge from elemental magics and construct artificial spellcraft, through mimicry of nature's knowledge. They called the practice Weaving, and today they have perfected the craft of sewing arcane sequences into apparel, carving enchantments into materials, and coaxing plants into braided wards.

But it would be a long time before the Mulburrows could settle down in a haven of their own. Irachron was nigh and the elemental factions were on the brink of coups. In the beginning of the Titan's conquest of the Material Plane, each element found their own corner of the world. Giants and dragons of their respective factions lived in harmony for a period, building grand castles to house the planar crossings from where they came. Though over time, the essential Dichotomy of Tsindwr slowly sewed dissent between the two species; giants became obsessed with harnessing Gloam and dragons fell to Faerie's temptation to hoard the boons of the land. Both groups of Titans believed the other to be an obstacle to their goals; the giants would not part with their constructed keeps and dragons would not part with their understanding of the arcane. They were divided by their jealousy and ambition, thus beginning the Era of Rage and Storm: the Irachron.

War between giants and dragons ensued, lesser elementals were summoned as infantry and colossi called Wardens were built as harbingers of destruction. Giants became pioneers in the harnessing of Gloam's mutational properties; the phenomenon of enhancing natural fauna into colossal beasts of rending and craze was called Seep: the moment when a creature accepts the influence of Gloam to overtake their physical form and transmute into something more. Dragons took the first steps into golemic magicks and material alchemy, creating semi-autonomous constructs of inanimate material made animate through arcane sigiling and element-powered movement: as the dragons discovered new materials and methods of transmutation, they were able to optimize the composition of these golems for specialized purposes.

It was the discovery of Petrolune that turned the tides. Golems made from this material found in the ocean depths were observed to have unpredictable behavior, having disruptive and dampening interactions with arcane magic but would sometimes take unprompted autonomous action. Dragons who hoarded this material slowly became more and more seclusive, focusing on the understanding of this strange material. Petrolune golems seemed to learn, which was previously unheard of. Eventually, these golems started to go missing. Mulburrow legend, however, tells of voiceless visitors made of armor and barbs who showed no signs of life except for two glowing green eyes. These beings became historically known as The Heralds, and were the same beings that caused the end of the Era of Rage and Storm. Leading Mulburrow tribes across the world, these Heralds infiltrated giant strongholds and disrupted their protected portals, cutting them off from their elemental allies and leaving them vulnerable to the dragons' tyranny. The Mulburrows were essential for the downfall of the giants, providing the Heralds the necessary concealment and navigation through the strongholds, then slipping away unseen to leave the Heralds to complete the destruction of the portals.

After the strongholds were stripped of their wealth by the dragons and giants were driven into exile, the Mulburrows inherited the empty ruins and built multi-leveled communities and shelters from artificially-enforced wooden structures with a heavy incorporation of natural materials and high degrees of craftsmanship. Today, these strongholds are little-known, partially due to their strategic placement in the landscape, but also partially due to the Mulburrows' expertise in Weaving: they've had more than enough time to imbue a misdirection enchantment around their borders to protect from feral monstrosities.

docs.title: If Umbrea were a single state, Drakonia would be its capitol.
docs.text:
The story of the Irachron coming to its end gave way to the beginning of the Gnosichron, the Era of Known History. This was an era of draconic reign, arcane innovation, and the birth of the first true civilizations. The Empir Drakoni, or Empire of Dragons, was a sovereignty that spanned the entire northern half of the continent of Umbrea, and its capitol, Drakonia, was an island province in the center of an inland sea.

But 500 years before the end of the Era of Rage and Storm, the legacy of the Drakoni and its empire would begin in a single egg, shared by two brothers: Owalid and Oshik. Twin wyrms, they hatched to the warmth of their mother's hoard being melted down by the elemental glyphs of attacking giants. Bound by blood and fueled by revenge for their slain mother, Owalid and Oshik were the first of the dragon Titans to brush away their pride and work together. It was their final attack on the giants that drove home the nail that cemented the Gnosichron into stability.

It was these brothers who established the first settlement of what would become the great Empir Drakoni. This was a haven to conscious reptilians of all sorts, including humanoid Faerfolk (awakened anthropomorphic beastfolk), as well as even a slow trickle of minor dragons who let go of their independence in favor of communal benefits. As the settlements grew, leading proud Titans such as dragons became an increasingly difficult group to manage, let alone lead. They needed direction, a common goal. So Owalid and Oshik decided to give them one.

Drakkonia would become the greatest arcane hub of knowledge and innovation that Umbrea has ever seen. The pursuit of understanding the fabric of magic, The Arras, and the extrapolation of its patterns through implemented equation became the focus of dragonkin all over. Moving beyond golemic magic, the Empir Draconi became notorious for its infrastructural enchantments, the most notable being the aeropolises. The first aeropolis, or city of the sky, was made from the summit of the island's volcanic peak, rotated upside down and fueled by its elemental connection to the plane of fire. Later iterations of the aeropolises would no longer have such a reliance on the elemental planes, but Drakonia's sister city of Dwoemer's name would go on to represent all artificial arcane enchantments: a herald of esoteric accomplishment.

docs.title: The Fall of an Empire
docs.text:
The first public signs of civil restlessness arrived with the establishment of the Drakonic Arena. Gladiators throughout the realm were called upon to provide entertainment with the prospects of earning a place in Empir Draconi's high militia. In an attempt to quell internal dissent and desire for new leadership, Owalid and Oshik, alongside their council, designed the battle arenas as a way to recruit the strongest among the populace while offering the common folk regular entertainment.

Seeds of doubt were sewn in the public opinion when the brother emperors, who until now had been known to be immortal, became one emperor: Oshik had disappeared from public view. With little explanation to the reason behind his stepping down from the throne, there was now concerns about both the longevity of their rulers, as well as the question of their successors.

There were many who believed the next line of emperors should be chosen, but there were many differing claims. The most notable candidate was a shimylf by the name of Valen Searcher, who dubbed himself The Sapphire King. A leader in his own right, The Sapphire King was the face of a large astral colony of elves and ingratiated himself to the Drakoni people through the Drakonic Arena. He rose through the ranks and graduated to a senior officer of the crown's guard. By then he had amassed a following and now had the numbers to challenge the throne.

Disaster struck before reform could even take a breath. Valen Searcher, The Sapphire King, quickly pivoted to exodus by sea, speaking of a great calamity on the horizon. "The sun would take a final breath and give way to an age of darkness and terror." Some believe his proximity to the emperor gave him insight to a dangerous arcane experiment whose repercussions would wrack the realm to its core. Some thought it was an attempt to bring his brother back from the dead. Some posited it was the last throes of a ruler desperate for ensured immortality. Some claimed it was not Valen, but his wife, only ever referred to as Nonna Rossa, who foretold the coming of a doomsday.

Drakonia sunk into the bowels of the earth. The Viridian Sea drained into the writhing trails of caves below. The fingers of magmatic vessels steamed and hardened. Steam clouds burst forth from cracks in the ground. Smoke clouds filled the sky, blotting out the light. The wards and siphons of elemental planar crossings became unstable, sending their tethered sister cities plummeting whence they came.

Dwoemer itself was never reported to crash. In fact, no evidence of its residents survived the fall of Empir Drakoni. What was left behind was a black sun that drained the heat of the entire north, leaving a frigid desert where the empire once stood proud. Most survivors of the fall were those who heeded The Sapphire King's warning, and took Llewyr Fenest and the western ocean beyond to cultivate a fresh start.

docs.title: The Forewarned Slumber of the Surface World
docs.text:
The Arras was torn and frayed the day the empire fell. Magic was turbulent, and planar crossings became naturally unstable. Soothsayers and seers alike predicted a time of storm and prepared their communities for shelter. The chaos and spirits of the primordial planes burst forth and brought storms upon Umbrea.

Columns of fire raged under searing eyes glaring just behind the clouds.

Hungry vortexes swallowed boats and Colossi then whipped their remains ashore.

Wind bore through the mountains and landscape at dizzying speeds, carving through the land and shaping it to its image.

The world cracked and strained and shifted, digging deeper and deeper into the earth, crushing paths to make way for more who harbored the whispered breathing of titanic and lurking presences.

During the Tenechron, escaping to the Kagecombs below was the only path to survival. The faerfolk, Shimylv, titanblood, mulburrows, and what little Drakoni there were left retreated to the cave system below the surface, where most storms could not reach them. Lifetimes spent in the dark confines of the underworld gave rise to a shared language, and a generation of new races to claim this world as their own. The ever-moving progression of Faerie created a lineage of cave-dwellers adapted to their new home. Gnomes, dwarves, dark elves, and kobolds quickly made a home of their circumstances, carving dwellings from the host rock itself and giving birth to the first sparks of now prosperous civilizations.

docs.title: "Upon an Ark does she come, and in her hand the blazing starlight of The Lord"
docs.text:
Humans are visitors to this world, immigrants from a foreign land. Just like us. In Umbrea, they came on an Ark, following the steps of a brilliant arcanist. She who transported a people in search of refuge from a dying world: a prophet of possibility and a future. With them she brought the word of The Lord, a pioneer in a godless world.

With their advanced understanding of magic and its schools, the wizards of the Ark brought structure to those communities they touched, and most miraculous of all, their resolution of planar instability that paved the way into the Divine Age, the Luxichron.

Granted, the people of Umbrea never wanted for a god, and had spirits aplenty to rely on and deities of their own to organize around. The introduction of new god was no great ordeal, though one who could bring mass miracles was indeed. The Lord's devotees took residence in the Kagekunan city of Gellhapfen, and made significant contributions to the establishment of its surface world city. Here, the Concordat of Chains was formed, bringing order to a fresh haven from the hellscape of storm and cold destruction.

Not much is recorded of the specifics of The Lord, its origins, or its magic.

docs.title: The Dread
docs.text:
This sphere is in flux. That which has been recounted here is no different. A collision of existences has brought the world into an equilibrium ever so slightly different from its original.

Very few are those who are aware of the changes made during The Dread, The Convergence, whatever you like to call it. Those who do are the ones with potential to lessen this world of its grievances. The Luxichron is yet to be defined by its events, nor those who live in its era. An equilibrium benefits those who settle for constance, yet it neglects that which still plagues its roots. Agents of change: those willing to step back and reconsider their world are those who we must rely on now.

The outlook is grim, but perhaps you are enough to change that.

docs.title: Legacy of the Stars
docs.text:
Cost Budget: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Abyssal Tiefling/Astral Elf (-2 Strings)

Long Rest Action (1 String)

Direct Flipside (Spell):

(Budget: 2.5 Strings)

You may cast a divinatory spell to read the omens surrounding a Near (+5 Beats) creature. On a successful Sense Test, you gain insight into their fortune in the upcoming tenday: whether it brings Weal or Woe, any symbolic visions that may accompany it, and any visual effects. (Utility, +1 String)

Consequence: On a failed Test, your mind is flooded with visions of your own possible fortunes within the next year; you are Dazed until the end of your next turn and you cannot use this spell again until you take a Short Rest.  (Minor Fallout, -1 String)

(Spell, +2 Strings)

Indirect Focus (Long Rest):

Spend a Seep Resistance (-1 Enhancement) to gain these effects during the current scene (+2 Strings):

  • Once you activate this ability, recover a number of Mental Resistances equal to your Tier. (+2 Strings)

  • Once per turn, you may take a reaction to transfer an incoming Physical Stress point to a Mental Stress track. 

  • You are Proficient in unarmed attacks (+1 String). On a hit, they do Finesse damage equal to a number of Seep Volatility Dice equal to your Tier (+1 String).

  • You may add "Move Near" to each of your Movement Actions.

  • You cannot Concentrate. (Major Fallout, -2 Strings)

  • On each turn, you must make a melee attack against another creature. If there are none within range, you must spend your Movement Action to move towards the nearest creature, and then take your Attack Action. If there are no adversaries within range, this ability targets your allies. Allies within Here range may use a reaction to spend 1 Flavor Token to narrate how they calm your rage. This ends your rage, and avoids expending your Attack Action. (Severe narrative consequence, -2 Strings)

(^Interpretable, +4 Strings 1 Enhancement)

docs.title: Alert - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 4 Strings 5 Beats

Prerequisite: Control/Tiefling (-2 Strings)

Upgrade Base Cost (5 Strings)

Trait (+1 String, +1 Enhancement)

You are proficient in Reflex (included in Upgrade). When a Scene begins (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may take a reaction to spend an Instinct Resistance (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) to immediately activate a Movement Action from one of your Action cards. (Special Narrative Weight: +1.5 Strings)

docs.title: Menial Magick
docs.text:
Cost: 1 String, 9 Beats

Prerequisite: Control | Face (-2 Strings)

Spell Action (3 Strings)

Direct Focus (Spell):

You may ask a collection of materials and tools Close (+1 String) to you to complete a task that would otherwise take a minute to complete manually. On a successful Reason Test, these materials become animated and complete the task in the span of a turn, granted the action can take place in a 5-foot radius sphere. You must have a relevant Knack to perform crafts with a set of tools.

Consequence: On a Failure, the spirits of menial magick are offended at your request and may intervene in your activities before your next Long Rest. (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat)

(^Primarily narrative ability, -1 String)

(^Utility Narrative Weight, +1 String)

Indirect Flipside (Spell):

(Budget: 9 Beats)

Decide on a specific trigger before casting this spell. On a successful Recall Test, one Close object of your choosing becomes monitored by a minor spirit, who you instruct to perform one simple movement (e.g. push, pull, squeeze) once the trigger is satisfied.

Consequence: On a Failure, the minor spirit you summoned may continue to enact this instruction on objects around you until you spend a Resistance to banish them back to their homeplane or until you finish a Short Rest. (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat)

(^Utility Narrative Weight, +1 String)

docs.title: Familiar (Instinct) - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Trait:

You have summoned a tressym spirit as an adventuring companion: Evangeline. Your Instinct score represents your bond with this Companion. Companions granted by this Trait are able to contribute in the following ways:

  • Aid: Grant you Advantage on a Test while within Here.

  • Buffer: Once per scene, as a reaction to you being subject to an external effect that applies Stress, you may reduce it by a roll of your chosen Potential's Volatility Die.

  • Connect: The bond between you and your Companion allows you to understand each other even if you do not share a language. You may also use a Surge to perceive through your Companion's senses. While perceiving in this way, you are insensate to your own body's senses.

docs.title: Presence - Stat
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings

Prerequisite: Familiar

Assign Potential Scores to your Companion (1d6 each).

Evan - Angel Kittyyy

Marks: 4

MIGHT: 1

FINESSE: 4

NERVE: 3

SEEP: 3

INSTINCT: 6

WIT: 3

Evan's Volatility Dice are the same as yours, with the natural limit of her Potential Scores. When you level up, you may apply chosen Stat bonuses to your Companion instead.

docs.title: Humanoid’s Best Friend
docs.text:
Cost: 2 Strings

Prerequisite: Presence/Support

Specialization Base (2 Strings w/ prereq)

Traces of the summoner’s magic have been infused into Evan, and she embodies both a magical charm and the draws of a furry companion. Evan gains Proficiency in Hope and Squirm, and a Knack called "ESA".

docs.title: Dexterity - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 1 String (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Frontliner (-2 strings)

Trait:

The Dexterity Ability allows a character to use their Finesse Potential instead of their Might Potential when making Tests with melee weapons. This does not apply to any weapon with the Heavy or Unwieldy properties.

docs.title: Redirect - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Trait:

The Redirect Ability allows you to move incoming Stress from Wit to Heart. To do so, you must make a reaction when receiving Stress in Wit.

Cost: 6 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Control/Legacy of the Stars

You have a number of Stardust Points (a special kind of Wit Resistance) equal to your level in Control. You may create Abilities that expend Stardust Points instead of Resistances, but still have the discount to cost of spending a Resistance (-1 String) and having a prerequisite (-2 Strings). Your number of Stardust Points is considered a permanent Stat (can be Upgraded). Spent Points are refreshed in the same way as Resistances.

Total: 9

docs.title: Cosmic Lens - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 3 Strings

Prerequisite: Stardust Pool (-2 Strings)

Long Rest Trait (2 Strings 1 Enhancement):

When an ally within There (+1.5 Strings) fails a Test, you may take a reaction to increase that Test's success level by 1 (+5 Beats). If there are no uses of this Trait left, you may spend a Stardust Point (Amplify, -1 Enhancement) to activate it again (Utility, +1 String).

docs.title: Wildshape
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Support/Frontliner/Familiar (-2 Strings)

Long Rest Action (1 String)

Direct Flipside (Spell, +2 Strings)

(Budget: 2.5 Strings)

Once per scene (-5 Beats), a successful Instinct (Grasp) Test, an ally you touch within Here is granted a layer of natural bark-like armor for the current Scene (+2 Strings), giving them the Armored condition (+1 String) and granting them a Nerve Shield.

Consequence: On a failure, your target becomes Petrified until the end of their next turn (Major Condition, -2 Strings).

Indirect Focus (Long Rest):

You may activate this Ability a number of times equal to your Tier* per Long Rest. When you activate this Ability, you assume the form of a beast you remember seeing*. For the current scene (+2 Strings), you temporarily adopt the Potentials of the chosen beast*. While you are able to Concentrate (not specifically Concentrating) you retain your mental Potentials*, and may end this Ability’s effect as a reaction. If you suffer Fallout while in Wildshape form, make a Grit Test, becoming Distracted (Major Fallout, -2 Strings) while in Wildshape form on a failure.

(*Interpretable, 4 Strings 1 Enhancement)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Avatar of the Cosmos
docs.text:
Cost: 2.5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Stardust Pool/Humanoid’s Best Friend (-2 Strings)

Short Rest Action (2 Strings)

Direct Focus: 

Once per Long Rest, you may to attune to one of the many Constellations in the cosmos. In order to attune to a Constellation, you must learn a facet of its True Name; this involves conducting a ceremony requiring ingredients made from rare living residents (whether flora or fauna) of the Domain corresponding to the god related to the Constellation (Material Components, -1 String). This ritual must be conducted under the divine light of the respective god’s moon (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), and, in order to ground the memory of comprehending a True Name, requires the caster to resolve an important social conflict, confess a deep emotion, or other narrative disclosure that connects with the target Domain (Narrative Consequence, -5 Beats).

Attuning to a Constellation allows you to purchase an Option for the Flipside of this Action*. It also gives you a fleeting understanding of the Constellation’s Essence, allowing you to expend a use of this ability to instead apply the target Domain to a single Test*. When you make a Test in this way, you may improvise a Utility-level magical effect as part of the Test’s intent*. You may choose to let your Familiar activate this Ability in this way instead of you (Agency, +1 String). Using this Ability in this way does not prevent you from using the Flipside, it just uses up a charge for the Focus side*.

(^Interpretable, 4 Strings 1 Enhancement).

Each Option generated by this Ability produces an effect that lasts for the current Scene (+2 Strings). Options made by this ability can only be activated if you possess the spellbook in which the Constellation was recorded (Narrow Trigger, -1 String).

(Option Base Cost: 3 Strings)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

Indirect Flipside: 

(Budget: 2 Strings 2 Beats)

Activate one of the Options created under this Ability (Trigger, +1 Beat). Whenever you activate this Ability, your Familiar may activate it as well (+1 Enhancement). 

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Shooting Star - Option
docs.text:
Cost: 8 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Avatar of the Cosmos

Avatar of the Cosmos Base (3 Strings) [Glare]

While this Constellation is active, you may make an Indirect action to shoot a bolt of radiant cosmic energy from a starry manifestation of a bow and arrows. An arc of starlight strikes a point within There (+1.5 Strings), causing a burst of energy within Near of the target point (Near AOE, +1.5 Strings +1 Enhancement). Creatures within the Near of the target point must make a Frame Test or take 1IDV damage to Seep.

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Horologium - Option
docs.text:
Cost: 6 Strings

Prerequisite: Avatar of the Cosmos

Avatar of the Cosmos Base (3 Strings) [Flow]

As a part of activating this Constellation, spend a Finesse Resistance (-1 Enhancement). While this Constellation is active, you are Frenzied (Major Condition, 3 Strings 1 Enhancement).

docs.title: Krath́r - Option
docs.text:
Cost: 5.5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Avatar of the Cosmos/Support

Avatar of the Cosmos Base (3 Strings) [Root]

Scene -> Sequence Die (I) (+1 Enhancement)

Any time you start your turn while an ally is Here, you may take a reaction and make a Read Test (Test Required, -5 Beats) to heal them 1IDV in Instinct (Initial Healing, +1 String).

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Upgrade - Stat
docs.text:
Cost: 16 Strings

Prerequisite: N/A

Upgrade Base (4 Strings)

Increment: Spell Limits, Marks, Stardust Pool (2 + 3 + 1 Strings)

Increase your Stored Spells limit by your Tier*. Increase your Mark Pool by your Tier*. Increase your Stardust Pool by your Tier*.

(*Utility, +3 Strings)

docs.title: Battlemage - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 6 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Spellslinger | Control | Support | Frontliner (-2 Strings)

General Trait (5 Strings 1 Enhancement)

You have a Knack for casting spells and maintaining Concentration on them while under the pressure of combat (Knack, +2 Strings). 

Additionally, whenever you take Fallout while Concentrating (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may make a Risky Grit Test (Risky Test Required, -1 String) to maintain Concentration (Utility, +1 String). On a Failure, you may still choose to spend a Resistance and maintain Concentration.

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Starry-Eyed Child, Full of Wonder
docs.text:
Cost: 7 Strings

Prerequisite: Legacy of the Stars/Control/Familiar (-2 Strings)

Spell Action (3 Strings)

Direct Focus:

On a successful Esoterica Test, for the next minute (+2 Strings), you can see the auras of magical effects* within Close (Close AOE, +2 Strings +1 Enhancement) of you. For each magical effect, you may determine what Tradition it came from, any plane of origin of Warp associated with the effect, and the exact extent of the effect’s reach*. In addition, regain a Wit Resistance (+2 Strings).

(^Utility*, +1 String)

(Primarily Narrative Ability, -1 String)

Consequence: On a failure, you lose an Instinct Resistance (GM ruling, -1 Enhancement).

Indirect Flipside:

(Budget: 3.5 Strings)

Long Rest Action (-2 Strings)

A number of times equal to your Tier (Utility, +1 String), you may teleport (Utility, +1 String) within Close (+1 String). Consider a target Here to be Surprised (Aesthetic, +1 Beat) until the beginning of your next turn. You may choose to, instead of activating this Ability yourself, allow your Familiar to activate this Ability (Agency, +1 String).

docs.title: Know Thy Enemy
docs.text:
Cost: 1.5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Frontliner/Starry-Eyed Child, Full of Wonder/Infernal Viper/Driven (-2 Strings)

Conditional Trait (5 Beats 1 Enhancement)

You may describe how you spend an hour observing the actions of a quarry and otherwise preparing for a fight to come. After doing so, gain a Flavor Token (+5 Beats).

You may spend a Flavor Token when you are within There (+1.5 Strings) of a Surprised (Narrow Trigger, -1 String) adversary to make an attack against them (Initial, +1 String). Once you have resolved the attack, the target is no longer Surprised (Mechanical Consequence, -1 String).

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Snake in the Grass - Surge
docs.text:
Cost: 6.5 Strings

Prerequisite: Know Thy Enemy (-2 Strings)

General Surge (4 Strings, 1 Enhancement)

When you succeed on a Test (Test Required, -5 Beats) using an Ability against an enemy who is Surprised (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may activate this Surge to clear your Stress Track (+4 Strings) in the same Potential used for the Test*. In addition, add 1WDV (Initial Damage, +1 String) to the total amount of damage dealt by the Ability.

Amplified (-1 Enhancement): Upon spending 1 Resistance in the same Potential used for the Test*, you may choose to instead clear Stress in Instinct or Seep.

(*Utility, +1 String)

docs.title: You Die, I Die
docs.text:
Cost: 8.5 Strings (1 Enhancement, +2 Strings)

Prerequisite: Support

Short Rest Ritual (-1 String)

As a ritual, a creature may spiritually bond itself to a target creature. The bonding ritual may present in any way the creature chooses, but must involve the names of each creature written on each other (Narrow Trigger -1 String). The recipient of the bond is considered Empowered (F) (Minor Condition, +1 String) until a Long Rest (Until Long Rest +4 Strings +1 Enhancement). While bonded, both the caster and the target receive the following benefits for the duration:

  • You have a sense of the other’s vitals and can listen to each other’s heartbeats at will.

  • You can communicate telepathically over a distance of Far (+2 Strings).

The caster may also benefit from the following effects:

  • You may take a reaction when the target is subject to stress from an external source to absorb one of the incoming Stress points in the correlating Potential (Recover Stress +1 String, Spend Stress -5 Beats).

  • You may cast spells with a range of Here on the recipient while they are Far.

(^^Utility +1 String)

docs.title: Eclipse the Arcane
docs.text:
Cost: 7 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Control | Spellslinger | Halfcaster (-2 Strings)

General Trait (5 Strings 1 Enhancement)

As a reaction to a creature casting a Spell that you have seen before (Narrow Trigger, -1 String) within There (+1.5 Strings), you may shift the stars in your favor and suppress their magical talents for a moment and make a Reflex Test (-5 Beats), preventing the spell from manifesting on a success (Utility, +1 String).

If the triggering Spell is Tier 1 Scrivening (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you have Advantage (+1 String) on this Reflex Test.

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Written in the Stars - Spell
docs.text:
Cost: 6 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Support/Legacy of the Stars (-2 Strings)

Long Rest Action (1 String)

Direct Flipside:

(Budget: 3 Strings)

Long Rest -> Short Rest (+1 String)

On a successful Weave Test (-5 Beats), you are enveloped by the essence of possibility as starry projections of your appearance flank you from many sides. For the next Hour (+2 Strings +1 Enhancement) while you Concentrate (-1 Enhancement), you may take a reaction when you are targeted by an attack to make a Reflex Test (-5 Beats): on a success, one of your starry projections to take the effect of the attack instead (Utility, +1 String).

Indirect Focus:

Once per Long Rest, within 1 minute after an ally has died (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may risk your own safety to bring them back to life by infusing them with your own magick and life force (Interpretable, +3 Strings +1 Enhancement). On a successful Anchor Test (-5 Beats), you successfully bring an ally Here back to life by transferring one of your own Marks (-4) to them (+4). In addition, your ally is Fortified (+3 Strings +1 Enhancement) for the rest of the Scene (+2).

You may spend a Heart Resistance (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) to reduce the Riskiness by 2 (+1 String) on this Anchor Test.

Consequence: On a failure, you fail to bring your ally back to life and they remain dead. You become Vulnerable until you finish a Short Rest (Major Fallout, -2 Strings). Any attempts to revive this target using this Ability or narratively similar magic of this magnitude automatically fail (Narrative Consequence, -5 Beats).

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Nebulous Convergence
docs.text:
Cost: 11.1 Strings

Prerequisite: Cosmic Lens (-2 Strings)

Spell Action (3 Strings)

Direct Focus:

On a successful Wit (Weave) Test, cause all creatures to become Disentangled (Aesthetic, +1 Beat) within Far (+3 Strings +2 Enhancements). Spend a Tether and Wit Resistance (Amplified x2, -2 Enhancements) as you conceptualize the interposition between realities, dictating the physical position of each target to be a new position because in another reality it is already true. You may teleport each Disentangled creature to a space within Yonder of you. Once you have done so, you may also teleport within Yonder.

In addition, you may choose to affect each Disentangled creature affected by this Spell with one of the following effects (Utility, +1 String):

  • The Disentangled target takes 1TDV damage to Seep.

  • The Disentangled target recovers 1 Instinct Stress.

(^Initial Damage or Stress Recover, +1 String)

(^Utility, +1 String)

(^Yonder Movement, +5 Strings)

(^Damage and Movement, +1 String)

Consequence: On a failure, roll 1TDV. Ask your GM what happens whenever you roll a 1 (Severe Narrative Fallout, -2 Strings).

Indirect Flipside:

(Budget: 5.5 Strings)

On a successful Wit (Anchor) Test, you may attune yourself to a reality where you and your friends are safe, spending a Tether Resistance (Amplified, -1 Enhancement). Begin a Tether Sequence Die (Sequence (TDV), +2 Strings +1 Enhancement) (Add Experience Slot x2, +2 Strings). You may expend a use of your Sequence Die to grant an ally within Close (+1 String) a number of Stress points to recover (+1 String) equal to your Sequence Die’s current value.

Consequence: On a failure, you are plagued with visions of all the possible ways things could end for your allies, and you become Afraid of your friends until the end of your next turn (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats).

docs.title: Hellhound’s Eye
docs.text:
Cost Budget: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Infernal Tiefling (-2 Strings)

Long Rest Action (1 String)

Direct Flipside:

(Budget: 2.5 Strings)

Long Rest -> Spell (+2 Strings)

On a successful Esoterica Test, you may deal 1WDV of damage to Finesse (Initial, +1 String) as you hurl a bolt of fire at a target within There (+1.5 Strings).

Consequence: On a failure, you become Cursed until the end of your next turn (Major Fallout, -2 Strings).

Indirect Focus: 

Spend a Wit Resistance (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) and name a specific piece of information you are looking for (Narrow Trigger, -1 String) at the end of a Long Rest. During this time (Until Long Rest, +4 Strings +1 Enhancement)

  • You have Advantage on Tests related to finding this information*

  • You may see fingerprints and footsteps relating to this piece of information within Close (+1 String) of you.*

(^Utility*, +2 Strings)

docs.title: Dexterity - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 1 String (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Bard by Many Names

The Dexterity Ability allows a character to use their Finesse Potential instead of their Might Potential when making Tests with melee weapons. This does not apply to any weapon with the Heavy or Unwieldy properties. This ability can be assigned a prerequisite of any of the following archetypes, reducing its cost by 2 Strings: Saboteur, Frontliner, or Summoner.

docs.title: Notes - Stat
docs.text:
Cost: 7.5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Face

Discipline Pool Base (6 Strings)

You have a number of Notes (a special kind of Heart Resistance) equal to your level in Face. You may now create Abilities that expend Notes instead of Resistances, but still have the discount to cost of spending a Resistance (-1 String) and having a prerequisite (-2 Strings). Your number of Notes is considered a permanent Stat.

You may expend a Note (-1 String) as a reaction (+1 Enhancement) to switch a Prepared Spell with one of your Stored Spells (GM ruling, +5 Beats).

1 Enhancement (+2 String)

docs.title: Driven - Stat
docs.text:
Cost: 1.5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Driven Base (1 String (1 Enhancement))

Flavor Token Trigger (5 Beats): 

Describe a tale portrayed by a song, dance, or other performance.

docs.title: Signature Study - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 8 Strings 1 Beat (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Face/Bard

General Trait (5 Strings 1 Enhancement)

Your years of education and practice have granted you understanding over the True Name to your signature study: the art form you have specialized in, through which you may cast magic.

You may create Option Abilities by defining different performances from this Parent Ability (Utility, +1 String). Each Option is called a Craft*. The Option requires a Test (-5 Beats) and will not activate unless the performance is executed (Narrative Consequence, -5 Beats).

(Option Base = General Trait, -1 String)

(*Aesthetic, +1 Beat)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Soothesong - Surge
docs.text:
Cost: 2 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Signature Study/Support

Signature Study Option Base (General Trait, -1 String) [Flavor Required]

General -> Short Rest (-2 Strings)

Trait -> Surge (-1 String)

Activate a Surge to start a Sequence Die  (+2 Strings +1 Enhancement) using your Heart Volatility Die. You may use your reaction when you cast a Craft while within Close (+1 String) of an ally to expend one use of the Sequence Die to heal that ally 1HDV (Initial, +1 String) in Heart.

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Healing Tale
docs.text:
Cost: 4 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Healing Hands | Soothesong (-2 Strings)

Spell Action (3 Strings)

Direct Flipside:

(Budget: 2 Strings)

On a successful Hope Test, heal one target ally within Close (+1 String) 1HDV (Initial Healing, +1 String) in Nerve.

Consequence: Your voice cracks each time you fail this Ability’s Hope Test. After failing a number of times equal to your Tier before you take a Short Rest, you cannot activate this Ability until you take a Short Rest (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat).

Indirect Focus [Flavor Required, -1 String]:

Spell -> Short Rest (-1 String)

Represent a story through an artistic medium or historical mythos: choose a Potential (P) (Utility, +1 String) encapsulated by the agents in the story. Any ally, including yourself, (AOE GM ruling, +2 String +1 Enhancement) that is paying close attention to your performance may receive 1HDV (Initial Healing, +1 String) healing to the chosen Potential (P).

(*Narrative Consequence, -1 String)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Spinster - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Face

General Trait (6 Strings, 1 Enhancement)

You draw power from the lessons that art portrays: an expert in spinning story and song together to grasp the intricacies of our reality. You may spend a Heart Resistance (-1 String) to automatically succeed on a Test (+1 String) made to cast a spell, but you must choose to do this before rolling the Test (Narrow Trigger, -1 String).

docs.title: Proverbial Improvisation
docs.text:
Cost: 4 Strings

Prerequisite: Spinster/Notes/Driven (-2 Strings)

General Action (4 Strings)

Direct Flipside (Ritual):

(Budget: 2 Strings)

When you spend 10 minutes performing for others, you may regain a Resistance (+2 Strings) of your choice (Utility, +1 String). Willing creatures in the audience become Enraptured (+1 String).

(Ritual, -2 Strings)

Indirect Focus:

Give a creature within There (+1.5 Strings) a Note (Spend Resistance, -1 String), allowing them to use it to succeed on a Spell Test as per the Spinster Ability (Utility, +1 String). Gain a Spirit Token when you do (+5 Beats).

docs.title: Wings of Whiteflower - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 8 Strings 5 Beats

Prerequisite: Frontliner/Bard by Many Names (-2 Strings)

General Trait (6 Strings, 1 Enhancement)

When you first activate this Ability, spend a Note (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) to be given access to the following reaction while you Concentrate (-1 Enhancement) until the end of the current Scene (+2 Strings):

Whenever you make a weapon or unarmed attack you may add one roll of your Volatility Die to the damage roll (Volatility damage, +1 String) (Increasing damage, +1 Enhancement). 

You may increase the number of Volatility Dice added to the damage roll by taking Stress in Heart. 1 Volatility Die (+1 String) is added per (Utility, +1 String) Stress spent (-5 Beats).

If your target comes from the planes of Faerie or Fiends (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may add an additional roll of your Volatility Die (Additional damage die, +1 String).

docs.title: Manifest Morale
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings

Prerequisite: Signature Study

Craft Base (General Trait, -1 String) [Flavor Required]

Trait -> Action (-1 String -1 Enhancement)

Direct Flipside

(Budget: 2.5 Strings)

On a successful Sway Test, a target within There (+2 Strings) is Muddled (+1 String) until the beginning of your next turn. 

Consequence: On a failure, the target is Empowered until the beginning of your next turn (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats).

Indirect Focus

On a successful Sway Test (-5 Beats), a target within There (+1.5 Strings) is Inspired (Aesthetic, 1 Beat) for the current Scene (+2 Strings). The first time a creature makes a Test while Inspired, you may roll XHDV where X is your Tier (Proficiency/Primed/Utility, +2 Strings +1 Enhancement), treating them as a Volatility Pool and resolving any relevant Perk. If your value is higher than the Inspired ally’s Volatility Pool result, they may use your value instead (GM ruling, +2 Strings).

Consequence: On a failure, the target canonically did not enjoy your performance (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat).

docs.title: Essential Miming - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Manifest Morale (-2 Strings)

General Trait (5 Strings 1 Enhancement)

You may call upon your understanding of the Essence of Performance, channeling its ability to convince an audience in believing your performance to be true and alive. Make a Heart (Read) Test: on a success, you may mime the existence of any mundane object (Interpretable, +3 Strings +1 Enhancement) no larger than Here. Weapons are not considered to be mundane. This object can be interacted with, and otherwise acts as if it were present in the Real, but it cannot be perceived visually. This summoned object will be referred to as your Mime.

On a failed Test, you cannot use this ability again until you take a Long Rest (Major Fallout, -2 Strings). Your Mime ceases to exist automatically if there is no one to witness your performance (Narrative Consequence, -1 String).

You may spend a Note (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) to expand the effects of your Mime. One Note is required per effect applied*:

  • Your Mime may be a nonmagical weapon.

  • Your Mime may be a barrier up to Near.

  • You may specify if only you are able to interact with your Mime or if only others are able to interact with your Mime.

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Manifest Ambience - Spell
docs.text:
Cost: 6 Strings

Prerequisite: Manifest Morale/Signature Study

Craft Base (-1 String) [Flavor Required]

General -> Spell (-1 String)

Trait -> Action (-1 String -1 Enhancement)

Direct Flipside:

(Budget: 3 Strings)

Make a Sway Test. On a success, a creature that can hear you* within Close (+1 String) becomes Charmed (Minor Condition, +1 String) for 1 minute (+2 Strings) while you Concentrate (-1 String) and the creature can hear you. When the Charmed condition ends, the creature is not aware they were Charmed (Utility, +1 String).

(^Narrow Trigger, -1 String)

Consequence: The target is Empowered (I) until the beginning of your next turn (Minor Fallout, -1 String).

Indirect Focus:

Make an Aura Test. On a success, all adversaries that can hear you within Far (Far AOE, +3 Strings +2 Enhancements) must make a Read Test or become Enraptured by you (Minor Condition AOE, +3 Strings) for the next minute (+2 Strings) while you Concentrate (-1 Enhancement). Creatures that are Enraptured in this way have Disadvantage on attacks against you (+1 String) while they can hear you.

(Consequence = Test Required (no discount))

docs.title: Manifest Delusion
docs.text:
Cost: 7.5 Strings

Prerequisite: Manifest Ambience/Essential Miming/Signature Study

Craft Base (-1 String) [Flavor Required]

General -> Short Rest (-2 Strings)

Trait -> Action (-1 String -1 Enhancement)

Direct Focus:

On a successful Sway Test (-5 Beats), create a visible illusion of an object or creature* within Far (+2 Strings). During the current Scene (+2 Strings), you may spend Notes (-1 String) to modify the illusion in any of the following ways, spending the [Note cost] for each effect activated:

  • Increase the Range category by 1 (There -> Far, Far -> Yonder).* [1]

  • Add 1 sense that the illusion can be interacted with (touch, smell, sound, etc.).* [1]

  • Allow the illusion to be animate and capable of moving position.* [2]

  • Increase the number of cloned instances of the illusion by 1 within range.* [2]

  • Instead of manifesting a single illusion for all to see, you target a single target and manifest all they see.* [1]

  • Allow the illusion to deal 1HDV damage to Instinct as a reaction to interaction with and from the illusion (GM ruling, +3 Strings).* [3]

(^Interpretable*, +7 Strings +1 Enhancement)

Consequence: The illusion simply does not appear. The GM may choose to instead summon the illusion you described before your next Short Rest (Mechanical Consequence, -1 String).

Indirect Flipside:

(Budget: 3.7 Strings)

On a successful Heart (Sense) Test, target a creature within Close (+1 String). Your target is Silenced (Minor Condition, +1 String) for the next minute (+2 Strings).

Consequence: On a failure, you cannot be heard by your allies until the end of your next turn (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats).

docs.title: Manifest Pain - Spell
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings

Prerequisite: Manifest Ambience/Signature Study

Craft Base (-1 String) [Flavor Required]

General -> Spell (-1 String)

Trait -> Action (-1 String -1 Enhancement) 

Direct Focus:

On a successful Sway Test, target an ally within Yonder to heal 1HDV (Initial, +1 String) in Nerve, and receive +1 to the success level of their next Test (+5 Beats). Target an adversary within Yonder to then take the total amount of Stress (+1 String) (Primed & Utility, +1 String +1 Enhancement) recovered by your ally, including any Stress recovered from supplemental Traits activated (+1 Enhancement).

(^Yonder Range, +3 Strings)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

Consequence: On a failure, your ally heals half as much damage and you take the full damage rolled by your healing (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats).

Indirect Flipside: 

(Budget: 2.5 Strings)

On a successful Aura Test, target an adversary within Close (+1 String) that has been successfully affected by one of your Abilities since the beginning of your last turn (Narrow Trigger, -1 String). The Target is now Vulnerable (N) (Minor Condition +1 String) for 1 Minute (+2 Strings).

Consequence: On a failure, you become Afraid of the target until the end of your next turn (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats).

docs.title: Encyclopaedic Insight - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 1 String (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Signature Study (Option)

Signature Study Option Base (General Trait, -1 String)

General -> Long Rest (-3 Strings)

Nomic studies can take a lifetime to unlock the comprehension of a True Name, but even Apprentice Nomists can glean minor insights towards the more general definitions of the world. You may undergo a ritual that requires a Long Rest’s worth of uninterrupted meditation and a representation of the narrative target expressed through your art.

This Ability can be used to generate Options (Utility, +1 String). You may activate Options created by this Ability a number of times determined by a Sequence Die equal to your Instinct Volatility (Sequence DV, +2 Strings +1 Enhancement).

Each Option has a free and mandatory (-5 Beats, GM ruling) Utility Narrative Weight (+1 String) effect.

(Option Base = Long Rest Trait, 5 Beats)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Silverstem - Option
docs.text:
Cost: 1 String

Prerequisite: Encyclopaedic Insight

Encyclopaedic Insight Option Base (Long Rest Trait, 5 Beats)

Long Rest -> Short Rest (+1 String)

Trait -> Surge (-1 String)

Activating this Surge allows you to make a Heart (Read) Test to activate one of the following effects:

  • This object shifts to form a sword (Armed*)

  • This object becomes Invisible (Utility*)

You may expend a Stress (+5 Beats) to activate both effects at once (Utility, +1 String).

(*, +1 String)

Consequence: On a failure, one of the strings snap on your lute. Until repaired, Tests made with this instrument are made with +1 Riskiness (Major Fallout, -2 Strings).

docs.title: Fluten - Option
docs.text:
Cost: 6 Strings

Prerequisite: Encyclopaedic Insight

Encyclopaedic Insight Option Base (Long Rest Trait, 5 Beats)

Long Rest -> General (+3 Strings)

Trait -> Surge (-1 String)

For the next minute (+2 Strings) you may take a reaction whenever you activate a Craft or Spell through this instrument that provides healing to provide an extra 1HDV of healing (Initial, +1 String). Roll a D8; depending on the resulting value (GM ruling, -5 Beats), the extra healing targets a different Potential (Utility, +1 String):

D8 Potential 1 Might 2 Finesse 3 Nerve 4 Seep 5 Instinct 6 Wit 7 Heart 8 Tether

docs.title: Jasper’s Armada - Option
docs.text:
Cost: 8 Strings

Prerequisite: Encyclopaedic Insight/Bard by Many Names

Encyclopaedic Insight Option Base (Long Rest Trait, 5 Beats)

Presence (+5 Strings)

Specialization (+2 Strings)

Long Rest -> Short Rest (+1 String)

Trait -> Action (-1 String -1 Enhancement)

Direct Focus 

Activating this ability allows you to make a Read Test (-5 Beats) to cause the weapon to fly around on its own for one hour (+2 Strings +1 Enhancement) while you Concentrate (-1 String). While active, Jasper’s Armada has the following stats:

Name: Jasper’s Armada 

Marks: 3

Knack: Stick ‘em with the Pointy End

Skills: Force, Feat

Potentials:

MIGHT: 4

FINESSE: 4

NERVE: 4

SEEP: 3

INSTINCT: 2

WIT: 3

HEART: 2

TETHER: 2

Indirect Flipside 

(Budget: 4 Strings)

Short Rest -> Spell (+1 String)

On a successful Sway Test, choose a target in Close (+1 String) to throw Jasper's Armada dealing 1IDV of Finesse damage (+1 String) and recall the sword back to you (Utility, +1 String).

Consequence: On a failure,You whiff your throw and the sword tumbles onto the ground. The GM chooses where it ends up (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat).

docs.title: Bard by Many Names - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 7 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Face/Bard/Notes (-2 Strings)

Upgrade Base (4 Strings)

You may add the prerequisite “Bardic Versatility” to an Ability that would otherwise not be accessible to you via your Archetype. This can only be applied to Abilities that already have a prerequisite archetype (i.e. cannot affect Abilities that solely have Origin choices as a prerequisite). This creates a different prerequisite option tacked onto the existing prerequisites**. You may also replace any expenditure of Resistances to instead expend a Note*.

(^Interpretable, +3 Strings +1 Enhancement)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Menial Magick - Spell
docs.text:
Cost: 1 String, 9 Beats

Prerequisite: Control | Face (-2 Strings)

Spell Action (3 Strings)

Direct Focus (Spell):

You may ask a collection of materials and tools Close (+1 String) to you to complete a task that would otherwise take a minute to complete manually. On a successful Reason Test, these materials become animated and complete the task in the span of a turn, granted the action can take place in a 5-foot radius sphere. You must have a relevant Knack to perform crafts with a set of tools.

Consequence: On a Failure, the spirits of menial magick are offended at your request and may intervene in your activities before your next Long Rest. (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat)

(^Primarily narrative ability, -1 String)

(^Utility Narrative Weight, +1 String)

Indirect Flipside (Spell):

(Budget: 9 Beats)

Decide on a specific trigger before casting this spell. On a successful Recall Test, one Close object of your choosing becomes monitored by a minor spirit, who you instruct to perform one simple movement (e.g. push, pull, squeeze) once the trigger is satisfied.

Consequence: On a Failure, the minor spirit you summoned may continue to enact this instruction on objects around you until you spend a Resistance to banish them back to their homeplane or until you finish a Short Rest. (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat)

(^Utility Narrative Weight, +1 String)

docs.title: Starry-Eyed Child, Full of Wonder
docs.text:
Cost: 7 Strings

Prerequisite: Legacy of the Stars/Control/Familiar | Bard by Many Names (-2 Strings)

Spell Action (3 Strings)

Direct Focus:

On a successful Esoterica Test, for the next minute (+2 Strings), you can see the auras of magical effects within Close (Close AOE, +2 Strings +1 Enhancement) of you. For each magical effect, you may determine what Tradition it came from, any plane of origin of Warp associated with the effect, and the exact extent of the effect’s reach. In addition, regain a Wit Resistance (+2 Strings).

(^Utility*, +1 String)

(Primarily Narrative Ability, -1 String)

Consequence: On a failure, you lose an Instinct Resistance (GM ruling, -1 Enhancement).

Indirect Flipside:

(Budget: 3.5 Strings)

Long Rest Action (-2 Strings)

A number of times equal to your Tier (Utility, +1 String), you may teleport (Utility, +1 String) within Close (+1 String). Consider a target Here to be Surprised (Aesthetic, +1 Beat) until the beginning of your next turn. You may choose to, instead of activating this Ability yourself, allow your Familiar to activate this Ability (Agency, +1 String).

docs.title: Extra Attack - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 6 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Tier 2 (-2 Strings)

General Trait (5 Strings, 1 Enhancement)

Once per turn, when you take a weapon or unarmed attack, you may take a reaction and make one additional weapon or unarmed attack (Weapon damage, +1 String).

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Cleanse - Spell
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings

Prerequisite: Soothesong (-2 Strings)

Spell Action (3 Strings)

Direct Flipside:

(Budget: 2.5 Strings)

Make a Hope Test with Advantage (+1 String): on a success, you choose an ally within Here to recover from a Minor Condition (Recover, +2 Strings) you may expend a Resistance in Heart (-1 String) to remove a Major Condition (+1 String) instead. 

Consequence: On a failure, your target becomes Muddled (H) until the end of your next turn (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats).

Indirect Focus:

On a successful Read Test, choose a target within Close (+1 String) that has a Minor Condition that is positively affecting them. Remove the Minor Condition (Recover Condition, +2 Strings) and apply the corresponding condition across from it on the table below to one of your allies (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats) within Close. The duration is determined by the duration of the Condition taken from the adversary. You may choose to spend an Instinct Resistance (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) to do the same except with a Major Condition (Recover Condition, +1 String) (Major Fallout, -1.5 Strings).

Consequence:  On a failure you and your ally become Muddled (H) until the end of your next turn (Minor Fallout x2, -1 String).

(Interpretable ->, +3 Strings +1 Enhancement)

Positive Condition Negative Condition Minor Empowered (P) Vulnerable (P) Unseen Afraid Major Fortified Mentally Vulnerable Frenzied Slowed Invisible Blinded Retaliate Bleeding (H) Spirited Dazed Warded Physically Vulnerable

docs.title: Food For The Soul - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 9.5 Strings (1 Enhancement) 

Prequisiste: Signature Study/Notes

Craft Base (General Trait, -1 String)

When an Ally within Close (+1 String) is afflicted with a negative Minor Condition that you have inflicted onto them (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may make a Hope Test (Test Required, -5 Beats) to cancel the negative effects of the condition (Recover Minor Condition, +2 Strings) and replace them with the correlating positive effect listed in the table below (Minor Condition, +1 String). You may expend a Note (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) to cancel out the effects of a Major Condition (Recover Major Condition, +1 String) in the same way instead (Major Condition, +2 Strings +1 Enhancement).

(Interpretable ->, +3 Strings +1 Enhancement)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

Negative Condition Positive Condition Minor Afraid Unseen Bound Advantage on Feat Tests Charmed Advantage on Read Tests Deafened Advantage on Sense Tests Enraptured Advantage on Reason Tests Held Advantage on Squirm Tests Muddled, Vulnerable (P) Empowered (P) Rooted Advantage on Grace Tests Silenced Advantage on Sway Tests Major Bleeding Retaliate (H/T) Blinded Invisible Cursed Armored (Heart Shield X where X = Tier) Dazed Spirited Distracted Empowered (F, W, I) Petrified, Slowed Frenzied Vulnerable (Mentally) Fortified (1) Vulnerable (Physically) Warded (1)

docs.title: By Your Side
docs.text:
Cost: 3 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: (Support | Spellslinger)/Tank | Bard by Many Names (-2 Strings)

Long Rest Trait (-1 String, 1 Enhancement)

When a target ally within There (+1.5 Strings) takes any number of Marks (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may take a reaction to spend an Instinct Stress (-5 Beats) to teleport (Utility, +1 String) to within Here of the target (Movement: There, +2 Strings). You ally becomes Armored with an Instinct Shield until the beginning of your next turn (Minor Condition, +1 String).

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Battlefield Influencer - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 7 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Manifest Morale (-2 Strings)

General Trait (5 Strings 1 Enhancement)

You have a number of Ally Slots equal to your Tier (Utility, +1 String). Whenever you cause a creature to become Inspired (Narrow Trigger, -1 String), you may expend an Ally Slot to transfer the duration to this Ability instead (Utility, +1 String). While an Inspired creature is taking up an Ally Slot, they may take a Group Action (-2 Strings) with you, no matter how far away you are, and spend a Heart Resistance (-1 String) to recover from a Minor Condition (+2 Strings). Whenever a creature taking up an Ally Slot loses the Inspired tag, the Ally Slot is refreshed.

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Mote - Perk
docs.text:
Cost: 3 Beats

Prerequisite: Manifest Morale

When you activate this Perk outside of the jinx threshold, cause an ally that can perceive you within Close to become Inspired.

docs.title: Improvisation - Perk
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Beats

Prerequisite: Essential Miming

When you activate this Perk, you may spend a Flavor Token to create a Mime that assists you in your Test, allowing you to increase the success level by +1 after resolving the success level modification of the Volatility Die (e.g. within the Jinx Threshold would result in an overall +0 to the base success level, and outside of the Jinx Threshold would result in an overall +2 to the base success level).

docs.title: Nesting Flock - Trait
docs.text:
Cost Budget: 5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Leshen/Summoner (-2 Strings)

Companion Base (3 Strings 1 Enhancement) [Summoner]

General -> Short Rest (-2 Strings)

You may spend a Heart Resistance (Amplified, -1 Enhancement) to summon a Flock* of ravens that remain for the next Hour (+2 Strings +1 Enhancement).

This ability gives mechanical purpose to your summoned flock. Your Heart Potential represents your bond with your flock. The Flock granted by this Trait is able to contribute in the following ways:

  • Aid: Grant you Advantage on a Test while within Here.

  • Buffer: Once per Scene, as a reaction to you being subject to an external effect that applies Stress, your Flock may reduce the Stress taken by a roll of your Heart Volatility Die.

  • Connect: The bond between you and your Flock allows you to understand each other even if you do not share a language. You may also use a Surge to perceive through one bird from your Flock's senses. While perceiving in this way, you are insensate to your own body's senses.

  • Retaliate: Once per Scene, as a reaction to you being targeted by an attack by a target creature within Near, your Flock may deal 1HDV damage to the target’s Wit.*

(^Utility*, +2 String)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Redirect - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 3.5 Strings (1 Enhancement)

General Trait (5 Strings (1 Enhancement))

General -> Spell (-1 String)

On a successful Steel Test, move incoming Stress from Finesse to Nerve. To do so, you must make a reaction when receiving Stress in Finesse.

Consequence: On a failure, your target has Advantage on any Tests made against you to resist the Afraid Condition until the end of your next turn (Minor Fallout, -5 Beats).

docs.title: Channeling - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings 1 Beat (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Summoner (-2 String)

General Trait (5 Strings 1 Enhancement)

Your connection to the Warp of another plane has allowed you to Channel the Warp to create specific Manifestations (Ambience, +1 Beats). 

You may make Option Abilities for each distinct Manifestation your summoning magic assumes. Activating a Manifestation requires a Test (-5 Beats). Activating this Option will always fail if its appearance and effects of the Manifestation are not described (Narrow Trigger, -1 String).

(Option Base = General Trait (-1.5 Strings))

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: Spiritual Prescience - Minute
docs.text:
Cost: 2 Strings

Prerequisite: Summoner (-2 Strings)

Short Rest Minute (0 Strings)

You may take 1 minute to meditate on the guidance you can perceive as a spiritual medium: a living, breathing, thin space in the border between planes. 

When you activate this Ability, for the next Scene (+2 Strings), you have Advantage (+1 String) on Tests made to interact with an adversary during Initiative (Narrow Trigger, - 1 String). During this time you may also take the Pray Flavor Action without expending the required Flavor Tokens (Utility, +1 String).

docs.title: Energetic Retribution - Spell
docs.text:
Cost: 4.4 Strings

Prerequisite: Channeling (Option)

Channeling Option Base (General Trait, -1.5 Strings) [Narration Required*]

General Trait -> Spell Action (-2 Strings -1 Enhancement) 

Direct Flipside:

(Budget: 2.7 Strings)

On a successful Steel Test, mark a target There (+1.5 Strings) creature to become Hexxed (Aesthetic, +1 Beat) for the current Scene (+2 Strings). While a creature is Hexxed, you have Advantage (+1 String) on Tests made to attack or track the creature.

Consequence: On a failure, you are Enraptured for the next minute or until you take a Surge to make a successful Recall Test to end the condition (Major Fallout, -2 Strings).

Indirect Focus [*]:

On a successful Grasp Test, for the current Scene (+2 Strings), you have the Retaliate (N) condition (Major Condition, +3 Strings +1 Enhancement). The number of NDV dealt by this condition is equal to your Tier (Primed, +1 Enhancement) (Tier, +1 String).

Consequence: On a failure, during your next Long Rest, you are compelled to commune with the spirits you draw power from (Narrative Fallout, -1 Beat).

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: A Battlefield Instigator - Trait
docs.text:
Cost: 5 Strings 1 Beat (1 Enhancement)

Prerequisite: Control | Channeling (-2 Strings)

Short Rest Trait (5 Strings 1 Enhancement)

Your voice has become an integral tool in the heat of battle. Your own sense for strategy or the wisdom of the spirits you channel allow you to intervene during integral parts of a dire situation. You may activate this ability a number of times equal to your Tier (Utility, +1 String). For each use of this Ability, you have 1IDV (Initial, +1 String), creating a pool of dice called your Maneuver Pool*. You may create Option Abilities off of this one (Utility, +1 String).

Each Option requires a use of its Parent Ability in order to be activated (Baseless, -5 Beats). Each Option is called a Maneuver*. If you have the Channeling Ability, you may require a narrative description each time this Ability is activated, giving an extra -1 String discount [Narration Required, -1 String].

(Maneuver Base Cost = -1.5 Strings)

(^Aesthetic*, +1 Beat)

1 Enhancement (+2 Strings)

docs.title: “Shoot,” the Messenger - Option
docs.text:
Cost: 2 Strings

Prerequisite: A Battlefield Instigator/Summoner

Maneuver Base (-1.5 Strings) [Narration Required]

Short Rest -> Spell (+1 String)

On a successful Tether (Hope) Test, expend a Die from your Maneuver Pool to target a number of target allies equal the result of your Maneuver Die that you can visualize or otherwise recall conceptually to establish a telepathic connection with (Utility, +1 String) the targets while they are within Yonder (+3 Strings). If you are touching an item that is sentimentally important to your target, or has been prepared to be attuned to the specific target, you are not required to make the Test (Material Component, -1 String) (General, +1 String).
