docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Description

Empir Draconi was considered a [[Settlement Classification Chart#^bafa77|Metropolis]].

Residents

Demonym: Draconian

Species Contour History and Lore

docs.title: The Sunforged Coliseum
docs.text:
Location and Description

A large coliseum located in the heart of the city, with large archways allowing hoards of spectators to enter through. Detailed stone work can be found on every wall and column, evoking ancient draconic imagery. The arena itself hosts rows upon rows of seating, enough to host thousands of attendants. High up there are various guest boxes reserved for the most wealthy members of draconic society. An announcer's box is amongst these, magically equipped to allow the users voice to be heard amongst the roaring crowds.

At the center of this massive coliseum is a large circular arena with a sandy floor. Four bared entrances lead into the fighting pit, a large moat circling it, with draconic fountains jutting out of the walls. Small bridges with snake head railings allow the competitors passage to the center of the arena. Twelve fifty foot columns of rough stone topped with fire line up around the arena. Large stone crocodile statues, standing rearing on their hide quarters, provide platforms for competitors to take their starting positions on.

Bellow the arena hosts the competitors, and their rooms for preparation. A vast armory of magical weaponry and tools are available to them. Along with medics and staff on hand to attend to any injuries that befall them while in the arena.

Competitors

Champions - Ivyarre "Luat's Ivy" Estreau (Faye): 1W/0L - Celeste Glistenova (Faye): 1W/0L

19th - Steveil Wizard (Will): 0W/1L

18th - Taston Drakris (Theo): 0W/2L

16th - [[Valen Searcher]] (Theo): 1W/0L - Nonna Rossa (Faye): 1W/0L

14th - Gust (Levi): 0W/1L

3rd - Teon Boldhide (Theo): 1W/2L

2nd - Denis (Faye): 1W/1L

Eliminated - Joesph (Will): 0W/1L

History and Lore

The champion's arena was created to give a source of entertainment to the people of the city, and a allow a way for anyone within Tepholithe to work their way up to glory.

docs.title: Invention
docs.text: Empir Draconi was a hub of ingenuity, blending arcane mastery with practical engineering. The empire pioneered advancements in levitation technology, adaptive metallurgy, and elemental energy manipulation. Many of these innovations revolved around the needs of their floating cities, war efforts, and trade networks.

docs.title: Distribution
docs.text: The empire’s economy depended on a structured resource distribution network. Floating cities relied on docking settlements and ground-based provinces for raw materials, while centralized bureaucracies managed supply chains with magical oversight.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
Despite its self-sufficiency, Empir Draconi imported specialized resources, including:

  • Rare minerals from deep-earth mines and neighboring nations.
  • Exotic alchemical reagents traded from distant lands.
  • Luxury textiles woven from foreign arcane silks.

docs.title: Income
docs.text:
The empire's wealth flowed from multiple avenues, including:

  • Taxation of settlements and guilds.
  • Arcane trade in spellwork, artifacts, and energy refinement.
  • Military conquest and subjugation, seizing assets from lesser nations.
  • Guild monopolies over essential crafts, enforced through imperial decree.

docs.title: Key Industries
docs.text:
Aethercrafting

The refinement and shaping of aetherstone and other levitation materials, crucial for maintaining the floating cities.

Elemental Energy Harnessing

Extraction and containment of raw elemental forces for power sources and weaponry.

Artificing and Enchantment

The empire's skilled artificers infused weapons, armor, and tools with arcane properties, leading to a booming enchanted goods trade.

Draconic Alchemy

Harnessing dragon blood, scales, and essence for medicinal, magical, and military applications.

docs.title: Niche Professions
docs.text:
Fabric Engineers

Experts who studied and manipulated [[The Arras]] to stabilize floating cities and arcane structures.

Skybound Merchants

Traders specializing in high-altitude commerce, piloting wind-skiffs and aerial caravans between cities.

Rune-Scribes

Scholars and artisans who engraved arcane runes into tools, weapons, and architecture to enhance their properties.

Tidecallers

Mages who regulated water flow to prevent oceanic disasters before the empire’s fall.

docs.title: Mundane Professions
docs.text:
• Blacksmiths
  • Farmers
  • Dockworkers
  • Merchants
  • Scribes
  • Architects
  • Leatherworkers
  • Tailors
  • Street Performers

docs.title: Companies
docs.text:
Several powerful trade syndicates and noble-backed enterprises controlled different sectors of the economy:

  • The Gilded Wyrm Consortium – A merchant guild overseeing the trade of enchanted goods and arcane relics.
  • Draconis Aetherworks – The empire’s leading manufacturer of aetherstone-based technologies.
  • The Obsidian Exchange – A financial institution managing imperial wealth and high-value transactions.
  • The Talon Forges – A state-backed weapons manufacturer specializing in enchanted arms for the military.
  • The Azure Loom – A luxury textile company producing enchanted fabrics for nobility and spellcasters alike.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Empir Draconi was born from the unity of warring states upon a vast island kingdom, an expanse of fertile land and volcanic peaks surrounded by the temperamental sea. The empire’s heart lay in the capital, a city of towering basalt citadels and grand avenues paved with polished obsidian. From this center of power, emperors and the Magisterium ruled with calculated authority, their dominion stretching outward through fortified ports, sprawling agricultural terraces, and mining colonies rich with precious ores.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text: While the floating cities became the pride of the empire, the land itself remained its foundation. The empire's mainland domains, including its annexed territories and coastal fortresses, provided the resources necessary for its continued expansion. The grand roads, paved with arcane-reinforced stone, connected its provinces, ensuring the swift movement of legions, goods, and imperial decrees. These regions were governed by high lords and imperial magistrates, maintaining order and enforcing the will of the emperor.

docs.title: Districts
docs.text:
Empir Draconi’s dominion was vast, divided into distinct regions, each serving a crucial role:

  • The Imperial Heartland – The ruling seat of the empire, housing the Magisterium, the emperor’s palace, and the grand arenas of law and war.

  • The Celestial Bastions – The floating cities, each a self-sufficient entity hosting scholars, military garrisons, and the elite of society.

  • The Dock-Cities – The fortified mountain settlements that managed commerce and passage between the sky and the land.

  • The Outer Provinces – The agricultural and mining regions, sustaining the empire’s economy and supplying its war machine.

  • The Border Forts – Strongholds that marked the limits of the empire, guarding against both foreign invaders and internal dissent.

docs.title: Modes of Travel
docs.text:
• Sky-Galleons – Vast airships that connected floating cities to the land, powered by arcane propulsion.

  • Imperial Roads – Enchanted highways that allowed swift and efficient movement between the empire’s key holdings.

  • Drake-Carriages – Beasts of burden bred for speed and endurance, serving nobility and military officers alike.

docs.title: Travel in the Empire
docs.text: Imperial decree strictly controlled access to its floating cities. Entry required sanctioned writs, granted only to merchants, scholars, and officials. The dock-cities managed trade and migration, ensuring that only those deemed worthy ascended to the skies.

docs.title: Entry and Reentry
docs.text:
• The Gilded Arch – The grand entrance to the imperial capital, a gate of obsidian and gold, guarded by elite sentinels.

  • The Azure Gateways – The enchanted portals that linked the floating cities, accessible only by those who held the emperor’s favor.

  • The Iron Watch – The heavily fortified border gates, defending the empire’s most vulnerable frontiers.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
• Aetherstone – The foundation of the floating cities, an arcane mineral infused with levitational properties.

  • Blacksteel and Obsidian – The primary materials of imperial construction, resilient and imposing.

  • Glasscrete – A fusion of volcanic sand and enchanted binding agents, forming the empire’s transparent yet unyielding structures.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: The mastery of Empir Draconi’s arcanists and engineers saw the birth of an age of unparalleled innovation. In the later centuries of the Gnosichron Era, the empire undertook its most ambitious endeavor: the separation of mountaintops from their earthly roots, shaping them into great floating cities sustained by aetherstone and tethered to the arcane fabric of the world. These airborne bastions did not replace the island kingdom but instead served as mobile strongholds, centers of governance, and testaments to the empire’s command over both magic and nature. Below them, dock-cities emerged at the severed peaks, vital trade hubs linking the heavens and the land.

docs.title: Landmarks
docs.text:
• The Magisterium Spire – The seat of arcane governance, where scholars and artificers dictated the advancement of magical sciences.

  • Locations/Settlements/Draconic Empire/Establishments/The Sunforged Coliseum – A grand arena where warriors proved their worth before the emperor’s gaze.

  • The Riftvault Archives – A subterranean vault containing ancient knowledge, accessible only to the empire’s most trusted minds.

docs.title: Climate
docs.text:
Beneath the empire’s cities and fortresses, the land thrived under careful cultivation and arcane augmentation:

  • A temperate climate, stabilized through controlled weather manipulation.

  • Seismic activity harnessed for geothermal energy and volcanic glass production.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Flora

  • Aetherbloom – A luminous flower cultivated for its arcane-conductive properties.

  • Obsidian Vines – Hardy plants used in the reinforcement of imperial walls and terraces.

Fauna

  • Drakebeasts – Domesticated wyvern-like creatures serving as the empire’s primary aerial mounts.

  • Ember Stags – Flame-touched cervids revered as omens of imperial favor.

Pests

  • Void Moths – Insects that consume residual arcane energy, weakening enchantments over time.

  • Burrow Leeches – Subterranean parasites that infest the lower districts and outer provinces.

docs.title: Symbolism
docs.text:
(Emblem/Crest)

A dragon’s eye surrounded by an intricate, spiraling pattern, representing [[The Arras]]. The color of the eye shifts depending on the magical alignment of the ruler.

Mascot

The Argent Wyrm – A legendary silver dragon believed to have been The Weaver’s first emissary. Though its existence is debated, it remains a powerful symbol of legitimacy for any emperor.

docs.title: Settlement Leaders
docs.text:
Though Empir Draconi was an empire, governance was handled by a council of magisters and appointed officials under the emperor.

  • The Emperor – A dragon ruler believed to be the avatar of The Weaver. Their reign was marked by both reverence and political intrigue.
  • The Magisterium – A council of twelve arcane scholars and statesmen who oversaw the empire’s laws, research, and elemental affairs.
  • The Warden of [[The Arras]] – A single archmage dedicated to maintaining balance in magic and ensuring the stability of the empire’s leyline-based infrastructure.
  • The High Talon – The supreme commander of the empire’s military forces, often a dragon or draconic warlord.
Legislation

docs.title: The Mandates of Dominion
docs.text:
The Codex Imperius

A series of laws dictating the hierarchy of rule, the upkeep of magic, and the empire’s doctrine of expansion. Any challenge to the Codex was considered heresy, punishable by death or exile to the Kagecombs.

docs.title: Factions
docs.text:
Empir Draconi was rife with internal factions, each vying for control, knowledge, or survival in the empire’s tumultuous political landscape.

The Weaversworn (deceased)

A religious order dedicated to interpreting The Weaver’s will, often clashing with the Magisterium over the balance of faith and arcane study.

The Wyrmforged (deceased)

An elite group of enchanters and smiths who created Empir Draconi’s greatest magical artifacts, including the floating cities.

The Ashen Pact (deceased))

A secretive cabal of dragons and magisters who sought to break the empire’s rigid hierarchy and place magical prodigies in power, regardless of bloodline.

The Taloncloaks (survivors today)

An imperial intelligence network specializing in espionage, assassination, and political manipulation. Their true allegiance often shifted with the tides of power.

The Riftborne (active)

Individuals who were permanently altered by exposure to [[The Arras]]’s instability. Many of them escaped to the Kagecombs after the fall, forming splinter communities of warped mages and outcasts. These outcasts and exiles studied the unstable remnants of [[The Arras]] during the [[Tenechron]], believing that understanding its flaws could lead to a second age of floating cities.

docs.title: Crime
docs.text:
Empir Draconi’s society was highly regulated, with magic itself being one of the most controlled resources. However, many underground movements sought to subvert, steal, or weaponize arcane power.

  • Soulforging – The illegal practice of binding souls into magical objects, creating immensely powerful relics at a horrific cost.
  • Fabric Piracy – Smugglers who harnessed unstable leyline currents to transport goods and fugitives.
  • Blood Rituals – Forbidden dark magic involving dragon or draconic-blood sacrifices, rumored to enhance a sorcerer’s power.
  • Artifact Theft – The Magisterium heavily monitored magical artifacts, but rogue scholars and thieves often sought to claim lost relics for their own gain.
  • Coup Conspiracies – Political intrigue was a way of life, and entire networks existed to overthrow rulers or install puppet leaders.

docs.title: Adaptation to Threats
docs.text:
Empir Draconi stood as a bastion of power, yet it was not without its dangers. The empire’s survival relied on an intricate network of defenses, both mundane and arcane. To guard against external forces and internal subversion, the Magisterium commissioned legions of warding glyphs and arcane surveillance systems. Enchanted fortifications ensured that even the floating cities were protected from siege, with arcane storms conjured to repel aerial assaults.

The empire faced threats beyond mortal warfare, fabric rifts, incursions of eldritch entities, and rogue sorcery tested its resilience. The Warden of [[The Arras]], an imperial office charged with maintaining stability between the Material and Astral planes, was pivotal in preventing such disasters. Specialized orders, such as the Riftwardens and the Ashen Pact, were established to combat existential threats.

Natural disasters were no less perilous. The empire's island heartland was prone to tremors and seaquakes, leading to extensive research in seismic mitigation. Floating cities were engineered not merely for expansion, but as a safeguard against these cataclysms, ensuring that the ruling elite could govern unscathed even if the land below suffered.

docs.title: Arcane Integration
docs.text:
Magic was the lifeblood of Empir Draconi, interwoven into its culture, industry, and warfare. The empire’s architects employed geomancy and elemental binding to construct and sustain its great cities. Roads pulsed with leyline energy, ensuring swift travel, while archaic golems carried out labor alongside mortal craftsmen.

The state maintained strict oversight of arcane practice, with the Magisterium regulating the use of leyline tapping and to what extent. The Weaversworn, a prestigious sect of spellcasters, were entrusted with grand arcane endeavors, from stabilizing the floating metropolises to imbuing imperial relics with untold power. Meanwhile, the Wyrmforged, mage-smiths of unparalleled skill, crafted living metal constructs, automated sentinels that patrolled the empire's borders.

Even daily life bore the mark of magic. Farmers called upon weatherbinders to ensure bountiful harvests, while healers infused their remedies with restorative enchantments. Those of noble blood often bore sigils of protection, their ancestral lines marked by contracts with spirits or celestial patrons.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
The empire was deeply spiritual, its doctrine a fusion of ancestor veneration and celestial worship. The Weaver, an enigmatic cosmic entity believed to shape fate itself, was revered above all. Temples of the Grand Loom stood as places of worship and divination, where oracles deciphered the threads of destiny.

Imperial cults flourished, dedicated to revered emperors who had ascended beyond mortality. Pilgrims sought blessings at the tombs of past rulers, believing that their spirits guided the empire from beyond the veil. In contrast, the Riftborne, esoteric sects that communed with the chaotic forces beyond [[The Arras]], were viewed with suspicion, their practices teetering on the edge of heresy.

docs.title: Holidays
docs.text:
• Aeternis Reckoning – The new year’s celebration, marking the passage of another cycle within the empire’s grand chronicle. Rituals of renewal were performed, and the emperor’s decree for the coming year was unveiled.

  • The Celestial Weave – A holy festival honoring the divine tapestry of fate. Oracles presented prophecies, and citizens wove symbolic threads into grand murals representing their aspirations.

  • Titanfall Remembrance – A solemn day of reverence for the empire’s victories over the primordial giants in the Titanfall Conflict. Military parades and historical reenactments honored the legacy of those who fought.

  • The Night of Shattered Veils – A time of caution, marking the anniversary of a near-catastrophic planar breach. Protective wards were reinforced, and offerings were made to the Warden of [[The Arras]] to maintain balance between realms.

docs.title: The Magisterium of Empir Draconi (Pre-1354)
docs.text:
• Archmagister Thalvorius the Adamant - A revered scholar and master of elemental transmutation, Thalvorius was one of the last voices of caution before Vethiskaar's Folly. He sought to stabilize [[The Arras]] but was ultimately silenced by the emperor's decree.
  • Magister Iridessa Vhalar - A brilliant artificer who specialized in aetherstone technology. Some of her surviving blueprints hint at undiscovered secrets of levitation magic.
  • Magister Rylthorne the Vexed - Known for his controversial research into the fusion of draconic essence with mortals, Rylthorne's experiments were outlawed, but rumors suggest his work continued in secret enclaves.

docs.title: The Riftborne Survivors (Post-1354)
docs.text:
• Veylin "Ashcloak" Draevan - A former sky-noble turned warlord, Veylin commands one of the strongest enclaves within the Docking Rings, leading scavengers in reclaiming lost arcana from the fallen empire.
  • Orvessa the Hollow-Eyed - A mystic who wandered into the Kagecombs and returned with cryptic knowledge. She claims to hear the whispers of the empire’s lost souls.
  • Jaspar Flintwing - A courier and wind-skiff pilot who specializes in navigating the Wastes of Draconi, offering passage and illicit trade between scattered enclaves.

docs.title: The Chain of the Rift (Cult of the Fallen Empire)
docs.text:
• High Seer Kaelith Morryn - Leader of the Chain, a sect that believes the empire's destruction was divine punishment for their hubris and seeks to bind the shattered world in servitude to a higher order.
  • Inquisitor Zareth Vox - A ruthless enforcer of the Chain’s doctrine, known for hunting down rogue arcanists and apostates in the ruins.
  • Elder Drenmar Thalvos - An ex-Magister who repurposed his knowledge of [[The Arras]] to serve the Chain, creating rituals designed to suppress the lingering magical anomalies of the empire.

docs.title: Historical Figures
docs.text:
Empress Vorrashka the Skyborne (r. 512-588)

One of the few non-draconic rulers in the empire’s history, Vorrashka was a storm genasi whose command of elemental magic earned her a throne among the empire’s elite. Her rule is remembered as a golden age of interplanar diplomacy.

Emperor Kael’Zyrrith the Gilded (r. 764-829)

Known for his economic and territorial expansion, Kael’Zyrrith transformed Empir Draconi into a center of elemental commerce. His reign saw the construction of the first floating cities.

Magister Ulthara the Everbound (r. 899-955)

A scholar of immense renown, Ulthara uncovered a means of stabilizing floating cities using Aetherstone resonance, but mysteriously disappeared in a diplomatic mission to the elemental planes.

High Talon Serevaal the Blackened (d. 1021)

A legendary warleader who waged campaigns against rogue giant enclaves in the southwestern mountains. His tactics in aerial warfare became the foundation of Empir Draconi’s military doctrine.

Vethiskaar the Last (d. 1354)

The final emperor of the Arcane Draconic Empire, Vethiskaar attempted to extend his dominion by manipulating [[The Arras]] to control elemental forces. This catastrophic experiment led to the collapse of his empire and the onset of the elemental storms that defined the Tenechron. His name is now synonymous with hubris among arcane scholars.

docs.title: Trade Partners
docs.text:
• The Aetherbound Consortium – A powerful mercantile network that specialized in the trade of arcane materials, rare metals, and enchanted textiles. Their airships frequently docked at Empir Draconi’s floating cities, exchanging resources for exclusive access to the empire’s aetherstone reserves.
  • The Myrmidic Holds – A collection of fortified enclaves along the empire’s eastern frontier, known for their exceptional craftsmanship in weapons and armor. Empir Draconi relied on their metallurgy and, in return, provided protective enchantments and air transport.
  • The Pearl Cities of the Azure Coast – A federation of seafaring city-states that engaged in the trade of exotic spices, aquatic alchemy components, and luxury goods. The empire exchanged enchanted constructs and navigational artifacts for their maritime expertise.
  • The Obsidian League – A shadowy yet influential trade network that dealt in rare artifacts, alchemical reagents, and contraband. Though officially denounced by the empire, many within its nobility relied on their smuggling operations to circumvent trade restrictions.

docs.title: Allies
docs.text:
• The Skyward Compact – A coalition of floating city-states that aligned with Empir Draconi in mutual defense, technological exchange, and cultural collaboration. Their bond ensured shared advancements in aerial navigation and levitation magic.
  • The Covenant of Dawn – A religious order devoted to celestial phenomena, whose healers and diviners worked closely with the empire’s magisters. Their alliance bolstered the empire’s spiritual legitimacy and access to divine magic.
  • The Argent Dominion – A knightly order dedicated to preserving ancient relics and protecting arcane knowledge. Their warriors often served as elite guards in Empir Draconi’s highest courts and arcane academies.
  • The Ember Pact – A diplomatic agreement between fire-wielding elemental clans and the empire, ensuring cooperation in energy production, warfare, and trade of rare volcanic minerals.

docs.title: 1. Vorthessar & Vorthasdral
docs.text:
• Vorthessar (Floating) – Known as the “Crown of the Magisters,” this city was home to the most prestigious arcane academies and research sanctums. It housed the Magisterium’s grand council chambers, where laws were debated and the empire’s magical advancements were overseen.
  • Vordral (Docking) – A fortified settlement built into the mountain base, Vordral served as the gateway to Vorthessar, hosting alchemical markets, smithies specializing in arcane-infused weaponry, and diplomatic lodges for emissaries.

docs.title: 2. Xiranthessar & Xirandral
docs.text:
• Xiranthessar (Floating) – A stronghold of the empire’s military elite, Xiranthessar functioned as a mobile command center, allowing rapid deployment of imperial forces. Its sky-docks were lined with drake-rider garrisons and warforged constructs, ready for battle at a moment’s notice.
  • Xirandral (Docking) – A rugged outpost carved into the cliffs below, Xirandral was a recruitment hub, prison complex, and proving ground for warriors. Its infamous gladiatorial pits tested potential conscripts in brutal combat trials.

docs.title: 3. Zevorithessar & Zevoridral
docs.text:
• Zevorithessar (Floating) – The heart of commerce and trade, Zevorithessar’s shimmering marketplaces were famed across the empire, dealing in rare goods, magical artifacts, and luxury wares. Merchant princes wielded immense influence here, competing for imperial favor.
  • Zevoridral (Docking) – A heavily defended checkpoint ensuring only authorized traders could access Zevorithessar. It was also a haven for spies and clandestine dealings, as ambitious merchants often sought to undercut rivals through underhanded means.

docs.title: 4. Aerynthessar & Aeryndral
docs.text:
• Aerynthessar (Floating) – Revered as the “City of Saints,” Aerynthessar was the spiritual center of Empir Draconi, where high priests communed with celestial forces and the doctrine of the empire’s divine mandate was solidified.
  • Aeryndral (Docking) – A sprawling sanctuary and pilgrimage site, Aeryndral housed shrines, temples, and healing wards where both the faithful and the desperate sought solace or divine intervention.

docs.title: 5. Dravethessar & Dravedral
docs.text:
• Dravethessar (Floating) – An industrial and technological marvel, Dravethessar was home to the empire’s most advanced forges and artificer workshops. The city pioneered soulforging techniques and produced enchanted armaments of unparalleled craftsmanship.
  • Dravedral (Docking) – A mining and labor settlement that supplied raw materials to Dravethessar’s forges. Populated largely by skilled laborers and bound artisans, Dravedral was the backbone of the empire’s weapon production and infrastructure.

docs.title: Enemies
docs.text:
• The Titansworn Clans – The remnants of the giants who waged the Titanfall Conflict, seeking vengeance against the draconic rulers for their ancient war crimes. They frequently raided imperial territories and disrupted trade routes.
  • The Gloamborn Rebellion – A secretive insurgency that opposed the empire’s expansionist policies and arcane exploitation. Their agents worked from the shadows, sabotaging imperial projects and inciting uprisings among the oppressed.
  • The House of Ash – A rogue faction of exiled Draconi nobles and arcane dissidents who sought to reclaim lost power through subterfuge and assassination. They maintained hidden enclaves in distant lands, plotting their return.
  • The Umbral Dominion – A rival empire that vied for control over arcane ley lines and forbidden knowledge. Their necromantic overlords viewed Empir Draconi as both a threat and a prize to be conquered.

docs.title: Neighbours
docs.text:
• The Verdant Principalities – A loose confederation of forested kingdoms to the west, known for their deep druidic traditions and reluctance to engage with Empir Draconi’s arcane pursuits. Trade existed, but tensions over deforestation and resource exploitation remained high.
  • The Sunken Halls of Nythra – An ancient subterranean civilization dwelling within the Kagecombs, whose relationship with the empire was one of cautious diplomacy. Their expertise in abyssal magic and underground navigation made them valuable allies and dangerous foes.
  • The Stormforged Bastions – Mountain strongholds inhabited by tempest-wielding warrior clans, some of whom served as mercenaries while others actively resisted imperial expansion.
  • The Whispering Sands Confederacy – A desert-dwelling network of nomadic tribes that controlled key trade routes across the former seabed. Their neutrality made them indispensable as guides, but their loyalty was never guaranteed.

docs.title: Language
docs.text: Empir Draconi boasted a rich linguistic tradition, with Draconic serving as the official language of governance, magic, and high culture. However, regional dialects and influences from trade partners and vassal states contributed to a diverse linguistic landscape.

docs.title: Dialects and Accents
docs.text:
• High Draconic – The formal dialect spoken by the ruling elite, scholars, and magisters. This version was infused with arcane phrasing and complex grammatical structures.
  • Imperial Common – The lingua franca of the empire, derived from Draconic but simplified for ease of use among traders, artisans, and commoners.
  • Dockside Creole – A blend of Imperial Common, regional tongues, and foreign influences, spoken in trade hubs and docking settlements.
  • Deep Cant – The dialect of those who fled to the Kagecombs, heavily influenced by underground survivalist slang and cryptic phrasing meant to conceal meaning from outsiders.

docs.title: Developmental Impacts
docs.text:
The expansion of floating cities and subterranean enclaves influenced every aspect of Empir Draconi’s social structure. The wealthy and powerful resided in elevated cities, looking down, both literally and figuratively, on those in the docking settlements below. Meanwhile, the island kingdom, which served as the heart of the empire, became a highly stratified society where proximity to the emperor often dictated political influence.

With the fall of the empire, the survivors’ adaptations led to further divergence in culture and daily life. Those in the wastes maintained vestiges of imperial grandeur, while the Kagecombs’ denizens developed a pragmatic and secretive society, valuing adaptability and communal survival over status and tradition.

docs.title: Cuisine
docs.text:
• Skyborne Feasts – Lavish meals consisting of rare meats, exotic fruits, and spiced wines, reserved for the floating city elites.
  • Seafarer’s Fare – Fresh seafood, preserved kelp, and fermented delicacies were staples for those on the island kingdom before its sinking.
  • Dockside Stews – Hearty meals made from accessible ingredients like root vegetables, dried meats, and sea salt.
  • Wasteland Rations – In the post-collapse world, foragers rely on roasted drakegrass, ember vine fruit, and smoked storm drake meat.
  • Kagecombs Brews – Distilled from underground fungi and bioluminescent algae, these potent drinks are both nourishment and ritual offering.

docs.title: Rich/Poor Gap
docs.text: Wealth disparity in Empir Draconi was pronounced. The aristocracy resided in floating palaces of aetherstone, removed from the struggles of common laborers. The merchant class, while influential, still relied on imperial favor to maintain their status. Below them, dock workers, farmers, and artisans lived under strict economic hierarchies. Following the empire’s fall, the survivors saw a forced equalization, those who retained knowledge of imperial technology or arcane secrets held an advantage, while former elites struggled to adjust to the new world order.

docs.title: Outsiders
docs.text:
Empir Draconi maintained a wary stance toward outsiders, balancing diplomacy with displays of strength.

  • Allied Traders – Merchant guilds from neighboring regions were permitted controlled access to docking settlements but rarely allowed into floating cities.
  • Vassal Tribes – Some indigenous peoples were assimilated into the empire, while others resisted, leading to ongoing conflicts.
  • Arcane Scholars – Foreign mages sought entry to study the empire’s advances in magic, though few were granted permission without proving loyalty.
  • Post-Fall Relations – In the wake of the empire’s collapse, survivors in the wastes and Kagecombs remain suspicious of newcomers, viewing them as potential threats or resources to exploit.

docs.title: Pirate Lords
docs.text: • [[Captain Soren Drakkar]] – A pirate lord who leads one of the most infamous holds in The Enclaves of Istrecce. Drakkar has clashed with Locations/Settlements/Haven of Hale/Hellhaven’s naval forces on several occasions but continues to evade capture through his knowledge of the region's currents and arcane weather manipulation.

docs.title: Historical Figures
docs.text:
at least 5

(Historical Figure Name) Harven Norrick (fl. 1960s)

A former pirate captain who rose to prominence after the Mist Veil disaster, Harven Norrick was instrumental in organizing the The Free Enclaves of Istrecce. His initial involvement in Locations/Settlements/Haven of Hale/Hellhaven's early mercantile agreements saw him broker several under-the-table deals with the clergy, providing essential supplies during the city’s rebuild. Norrick’s fortunes changed after a failed attempt to seize power during a factional civil war. His escape into the outer gulf marked the beginning of his infamous pirate career. Though labeled a traitor by the clergy, Norrick’s name is still whispered in the taverns of Locations/Settlements/Haven of Hale/Hellhaven as a symbol of rebellion and freedom.

docs.text:

docs.text:
Location and Description

The largest island located in Locations/Settlements/Gulf of the Fallen Moon/Fallen Waters, home to many of the Fallen and their trades.

Notable Residents

History and Lore

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Description

Hellhaven is a sprawling city located at the eastern edge of Locations/Regions/Loierr Fenest, where the fjord meets the Locations/Regions/Windbor Coast. Founded in 1933, it became the epicenter of human theocracy, built upon the arrival of both humans and their god. The city serves as both a seat of power and a beacon of divine influence, with towering temples and dark spires dominating the skyline. Hellhaven’s streets are a mix of industrialization, religious fervor, and societal control, reflecting both the power of [[The Lord]] and the struggles of those living under his rule. Despite its oppressive atmosphere, Hellhaven remains a thriving hub of political and religious activity, drawing citizens and refugees alike seeking to live under the strict doctrine of [[The Lord]].

Hellhaven’s history is one of divine governance, military dominance, and a slow shift from the natural to the imposed. Once, the land was fertile and lush, but now it bears the scars of overuse and divine exertion. The city's buildings rise tall, made from black stone and wrought iron, often shrouded in a perpetual haze from residual Tenechronian magic that permeates the air.

Hellhaven is considered a [[Settlement Classification Chart#^bafa77|Metropolis]].

Residents

Hellhaven is a city of devout followers and those desperate enough to seek refuge within its walls. Its population is primarily composed of humans, with a significant number of military personnel, clergy, and administrative officials. [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]] holds the most power, serving as both enforcers of divine law and elite military agents. The lower classes often live in fear, working in the factories or serving the clergy in menial ways.

Some come to Hellhaven out of necessity, many by birth, others by the will of [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat]], and some seeking salvation or answers from [[The Lord]]. However, dissent is brewing beneath the surface. Underground movements and secret alliances work to resist the city’s divine control, though they are largely unsuccessful due to the ever-watchful eye of the [[Creosmagi]].

While Hellhaven is a city of faith, it is also a place of secrecy, danger, and political intrigue, where the line between devotion and manipulation is often blurred.

Demonym: Hellian

Species Contour
  • Humans (50%)
    • Standard, Fey-Descended Humans, Half-Elves, Shifters
  • Kagefolk (15%)
    • Dwarves, Gnomes, Drow
  • Fae (10%)
    • Fairfolk, Fairies, Elves, Goblins
  • Hybrids (10%)
    • Genasi, Tieflings, Aasimar, Goliaths
  • Draconians (5%)
    • Dragonborn, Yuan-Ti, Lizardfolk, Tortles
  • Minority Groups (10%)
    • [[Mulburrow|Mullburrows]], Orcs, Wights, Revenants, Vampires, Disembodied
History and Lore

The history of Hellhaven is closely tied to the city’s foundation being built on a newfound gift of calming storms; Gellhafn. Over time, Gellhafn became a mercantile giant, but its power base later shifted from a port town to a sprawling city-state ruled by the clergy and military.

During the later years of the city’s formation, tensions arose between the mercantile elites and the [[Concordat of Chains]], both seeking to claim authority of Gellhafn. These tensions came to a head during after The Dread, when Gellhafn’s political climate shifted to give credit to the Creed of Blinding Light, now willing to believe that a higher power was communicating through global catastrophe to express dissent about magical regulation.

Despite these challenges, Gellhafn become Hellhaven, who still survives, though city life is constricted through both religious fervor and mercantile control. The city’s infrastructure became more complex, with the creation of the [[Creosmagi]] as both a religious police force and a military arm of [[The Lord]]’s divine will. Today, Hellhaven stands as a symbol of divine rule and unwavering order, although beneath its holy exterior lies a web of political intrigue and hidden rebellion.

docs.title: Atmosphere
docs.text: Dark and Heavy: The air is thick with a sense of saltwater and incense, accompanied by the constant hum of religious rituals. The scent of burning offerings lingers in every corner, and the oppressive weight of divine oversight hangs over the city like a perpetual storm cloud.

docs.title: Populace
docs.text: Devout and Subjugated: The citizens of Hellhaven live under a strict theocracy, their lives governed by [[The Lord]]’s will. Religion and governance are inseparable, and almost every aspect of daily life is influenced by the city’s devout clergy. Despite this, there are murmurs of dissent among the more oppressed and disenfranchised groups, though open rebellion is rare due to the constant surveillance and control of the Inquisitors. Resilient but Fearful: The people of Hellhaven have learned to live with fear and reverence, constantly watching their actions, thoughts, and words. The deep piety instilled by the church is a double-edged sword, while it provides a sense of purpose and unity, it also stifles any attempts at self-expression or deviation from the divine law. Class Divisions: The city is deeply divided into classes, with the clergy and military occupying the highest echelons, while the common folk serve in subjugation to [[The Lord]]'s divine will. The lower classes are relegated to menial tasks, working the factories and serving the wealthy, while the elite enjoy the privileges of power and influence.

docs.title: Rapport
docs.text: Enforced Piety: Hellhaven is renowned for its unwavering dedication to [[The Lord]]. Its citizens are constantly reminded of their place within the divine order, with the clergy acting as the primary enforcers of religious law. The Inquisitors, a military and religious police force, patrol the city, ensuring that no one deviates from the prescribed teachings and practices. Cultural Repression: Hellhaven’s culture is one of strict obedience to [[The Lord]]’s will. Festivals and celebrations are rare, often occurring only during holy days or the anniversaries of significant religious events. Even then, they are imbued with solemnity and reverence, lacking the joy or exuberance found in other cities. Secretive underground movements occasionally attempt to overthrow the established order, but they are always stamped out swiftly by the ruling authorities. Power Struggles: While outwardly Hellhaven appears unified under the rule of [[The Lord]], there are political struggles between various factions of the clergy and military. These factions vie for influence and power, and while they may outwardly present a united front, there are deep fractures within the system that often lead to covert power struggles. Religious Sanctity: Despite its oppressive nature, Hellhaven is a pilgrimage site for those seeking divine enlightenment or wishing to prove their devotion to [[The Lord]]. Pilgrims travel from across the land to pay homage to [[The Lord]]’s temples, seeking blessings or guidance, often unaware of the city’s darker underbelly.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text:
• Front: A reputable tinkering and repair shop specializing in ship components, automaton parts, and fine clockwork mechanisms. The sign outside reads: “Brighton’s Fix & Fiddle – Precision Repairs & Custom Craftwork.”
Overview
  • Location: Nestled in a dimly lit alley of the Chainmoor Brine Yards, squeezed between a rotting sailmaker’s loft and a derelict spice warehouse. The constant clatter of gears and hissing steam conceal hushed conversations.
  • Access: Customers seeking more than mechanical repairs must use the coded phrase: “I need a tune-up for my arcane conductor.”, only then will Brighton lead them into the hidden chamber below the shop.
  • Hidden Chamber: A vaulted, sea-sprayed cavern beneath the shop, where arcane trinkets float weightlessly in lantern-lit glass cases. Some items still hum with residual magic, while others seem eager to be held.
NPCs History and Lore
  • True Business: A black-market magic emporium dealing in stolen and cursed magical items, often plundered from merchant caravans.

docs.title: Brighton the Proprietor
docs.text: Brighton, an Archfey warlock with an unsettling grin, runs the shop. Always impeccably dressed, with clockwork jewelry that shifts on its own, he speaks in riddles and deflects questions with humor. Those who cross him tend to vanish into the dark tides of the Chainmoor.

docs.title: Quick Facts
docs.text:
Legitimate mundane steel and mithral armor and weaponry distributor in The Ironclad Sprawl

Overview NPCs

Proprietor: Horace Warsledge

History and Lore

docs.title: Invention
docs.text: Hellhaven thrives on arcano-mechanical advancements, blending etheric technology, imported Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig engineering, and its own unique resources, such as [[petrolune]], a volatile, semi-organic mineral that can store and release arcane power in controlled bursts.

docs.title: Creosmark Tokens – The Soulbound Permits
docs.text:
^3c24dc

One of Hellhaven’s most controversial and omnipresent inventions is the Creosmark Token, issued to all citizens. These tokens are:

  • Forged from [[petrolune]], infused with a drop of the bearer’s blood, and soul-bound upon activation.
  • Essential for movement, as [[Creosmagi]] (clergy enforcers) scan them to ensure individuals are where they belong.
  • While enforced by the [[Creosmagi]], they are handled and governed by the Creosmark Administration.
  • Personalized, containing a record of employment, permissions, and any legal infractions.
  • Temporarily deactivated as punishment, preventing access to workplaces or barring movement beyond certain districts.
  • Illegally forged or stolen tokens are worthless, as they are inert to anyone except their bound owner.

These tokens are administered and maintained by Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Lord’s Tithe Commission, which enforces their distribution, renewal, and revocation.

docs.title: Petrolune Firelances – The "Lawgiver" Weapons
docs.text:
• [[Petrolune]]'s explosive properties have been harnessed into firelances, carried by elite [[Creosmagi]].
  • These weapons function as arcane muskets, launching controlled etheric bursts at criminals and dissenters.
  • The higher-ranking enforcers wield Lawgiver variants, which have multiple firing modes, including:
    • Judgment Shot – A concussive blast to incapacitate.
    • Retribution Arc – A burning bolt of searing energy.
    • Atonement Lance – A restraining etheric tether.

docs.title: Petrolune-Powered Pneumatic Rails
docs.text:
Due to the winding, steep, and uneven terrain of Hellhaven, traditional carts struggle to navigate the streets. Instead, the city has developed:

  • Pneumatic rail carts that use controlled petrolune combustion to propel passenger lifts, cargo trams, and supply trolleys.
  • These systems operate on sealed pressure channels, reducing the risk of uncontrolled explosions.
  • Stations exist at various altitude points, allowing easier movement for workers and goods**.

docs.title: Etheric Power Harnessing
docs.text: Instead of petrolune, the city utilizes arcane energy similar to electricity, imported from Vergrenzig’s research. This fuels lamplights, lifts, and industrial machines.

docs.title: Self-Winding Automata
docs.text: Gnome- and dwarf-crafted mechanical constructs assist in shipbuilding, mining, and clerical duties.

docs.title: Sealock Mechanisms
docs.text: Engineering advancements in docking technology allow ships to be elevated between sea levels using arcane hydraulics.

docs.title: Distribution
docs.text:
• Clergy-Controlled Markets – All trade, production, and sales are regulated by the Concordat, requiring permits and tithes.
  • Guild Monopolies – Skilled industries like shipbuilding and etheric engineering are controlled by official guilds, ensuring only licensed artisans can work.
  • Black Market in the Chainmoor Brine Yards – A hidden trade network dealing in stolen magical artifacts, illegal technology, and outlawed arcane services.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
• Advanced Arcano-Tech – Vergrenzig supplies etheric batteries, automaton components, and steam-driven engines.
  • Exotic Metals – Required for precision mechanics and high-grade shipbuilding.
  • Luxury Goods – Silk, wines, and rare spices for the merchant elite.

docs.title: Income
docs.text:
• Shipbuilding and Naval Engineering – The city thrives on maritime industry, producing warships, trading vessels, and steam-powered submersibles.
  • Legal Tithes and Fines – Citizens are taxed for nearly everything, from travel permits to business licenses.
  • Industrial Manufacturing – Factories churn out machine parts, processed fuel, and enchanted tools for export.
  • Religious Pilgrimage – The faithful travel from afar to seek judgment, redemption, or penance, contributing to the economy through lodging and service fees.

docs.title: Key Industries
docs.text:
Arcano-Industrial Engineering

Combining mechanical engineering with arcane-infused energy, this industry is responsible for: - Hellhaven’s power grid, lighting, and heating. - Arcane lifts and transportation systems. - Etheric-powered ship components and industrial machines.

Naval Construction

A powerful shipbuilding industry producing:

  • Warships for Hellhaven’s navy.
  • Merchant vessels for trade across the Gulf.
  • Privateer ships used in anti-piracy efforts.
The Bureaucratic Machine

Hellhaven’s government is an industry of its own, sustaining:

  • Clerical scribes who maintain extensive legal records.
  • Judicial enforcers who oversee trials and executions.
  • Tax officials and auditors responsible for financial regulation.
Creosmark Administration

A bureaucratic industry focused on creating, tracking, and issuing Creosmark Tokens. This administration is headed and supervised by the Archprelate of Gates.

Professions: - Blood Scribes

^ed5799

Petrolune Refinement & Engineering

An industry focused on processing raw petrolune into usable energy sources for Hellhaven.

Etheric Constructs & Automata

Hellhaven imports Vergrenzig’s automata designs, but it has developed its own unique variations, powered by etheric cells and petrolune fuel reserves.

docs.title: Niche Professions
docs.text:
Etheric Tinker

Specialists in arcano-mechanical fusion, crafting ether-powered devices, enchanted constructs, and automated machinery.

^6142b3

Scrivener-Judicator

A legal scribe and investigator, assigned to document legal cases, oversee trials, and deliver edicts in [[The Lord]]’s name.

^b03051

Tithe Inspectors

Clerics who audit businesses and homes to ensure proper tribute is paid.

Judicial Lectors

Officers who review and interpret [[the Lord]]’s edicts for sentencing.

^e1eeb1

Memory Scriveners

Scribes who record public trials, punishments, and proclamations, ensuring historical accuracy.

^b29577

Sealock Engineer

Designers of hydraulic lifts, floodgates, and canal systems, crucial for managing Hellhaven’s altitude shifts and ship movement.

^d24a88

Combustion Artificers

Engineers who refine petrolune for controlled etheric discharge in weapons, tools, and transport.

^f9cd00

Stabilization Alchemists

Scientists dedicated to making petrolune less volatile, ensuring it doesn’t self-detonate.

^8c4801

Volatility Testers

Workers who test batches of refined [[petrolune]], often at great personal risk.

^706f96

Token Smiths

Specialists in forging new Creosmarks, using precise arcane etching techniques.

Blood Scribes

Officials who bind tokens to their owners, ensuring their compliance.

^47387e

Revokers

The agents responsible for confiscating and deactivating tokens from criminals or exiles.

^51214a

Clockwork Surgeons

Specialists who repair and enhance arcano-mechanical constructs.

^78e794

Binding Technicians

Experts who link automata to control scripts, ensuring their compliance.

Scrap Harvesters

Salvagers who scavenge broken automata for reusable components.

^d2a4a8

docs.title: Mundane Professions
docs.text:
• Dockworkers and Shipwrights – Essential for maritime trade and naval production. Essential for unloading cargo and ferrying goods across the city’s waterways. ^ec9281
  • Lampwrights and Gutterflames – Maintain the city’s etheric streetlamps and energy grid. Maintenance workers who ensure the etheric streetlights remain active.
  • Legal Archivists – Manage the endless scrolls of contracts, permits, and decrees.
  • Tax Assessors – Travel through districts collecting dues, issuing penalties, and ensuring compliance.
  • Soot-Chimneys – Specially trained workers who maintain steam vents and etheric exhaust systems, preventing deadly build-up.
  • Launderers and Sutlers - Provide clothing, daily essentials, and fresh provisions for both commoners and officials.
  • District Sweepers – Assigned to clean and maintain public areas based on their Creosmark status.

docs.title: Vergrenzig-Hellhaven Trade Syndicate
docs.text: Handles high-level commerce, ensuring regulated trade with Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig’s industrial firms. Logo: A steampunk gear surrounding a stylized globe, representing technological progress and economic reach.

docs.title: Brineyard Naval Works
docs.text: The largest shipyard, producing military vessels and private merchant fleets. Located in the Chainmoor Brine Yards. Professions: Sealock Engineer, Dockhand, Shipwright Logo: A mechanical anchor intertwined with chains, representing both maritime dominance and control.

docs.title: Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Lord’s Tithe Commission
docs.text: Oversees tax collection, legal fines, and financial audits under direct oversight of the Concordat. Logo: A black coin marked with a single drop of blood, signifying the binding nature of tribute and sacrifice.

docs.title: [[Chainmoor Guild|The Chainmoor Guild]]
docs.text: A covert network laundering illegal goods, bribing officials, and funding black-market enterprises. Logo: A shattered manacle, symbolizing the defiance of authority and the hidden underground economy.

docs.title: [[Creosmagi]] Enforcement Office
docs.text: A group of throat-slit, mute clergy who patrol and enforce the laws of [[The Lord]] in the streets of Hellhaven. They are also responsible for the guarding and transportation of imprisoned individuals. Logo: A pair of scales, with one side holding a gilded token and the other a blade, signifying law and retribution.

docs.title: Planning
docs.text: Hellhaven is a meticulously planned city, structured around strict principles of order and efficiency dictated by [[The Lord]]’s adjudicators. Streets follow a rigid grid pattern, with major roads radiating outward from Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Vault of Penance, ensuring that all paths symbolically lead back to the center of divine and legal authority. Walls and barriers segment the city into carefully controlled districts, each serving a distinct purpose. Watchtowers, checkpoints, and observation posts are positioned to monitor movement, ensuring that no illicit activity escapes the gaze of [[The Lord]]’s enforcers.

docs.title: Districts
docs.text: Hellhaven, also known in ancient records as Gellhafn, has grown into a sprawling metropolis of industry, faith, and maritime power. The city is a crucial trade hub, thanks to its strategic position at the mouth of a fjord-lined gulf, and its culture has absorbed steampunk innovations from Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig, blending them with strict religious oversight.

docs.title: The Adjudicary
docs.text:
(Government & Religious Quarter)

  • Seat of [[The Lord]]’s clergy, including Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Vault of Penance and Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Codexorium, where divine law is dictated and transcribed. The city’s ruling sect, [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]], enforces unwavering obedience.

docs.title: The Tribunal Forum
docs.text:
(Commerce & Civil Affairs)

  • Bustling with trade halls, judicial squares, and regulated markets. Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/Arbiter’s Call, a bureaucratic stronghold, ensures that all transactions remain under the watchful eyes of the clergy.

docs.title: Chainmoor Brine Yards
docs.text:
(Docks & Industrial Shipping)

  • A vast shipyard, famed for producing steam-powered vessels using Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig-imported innovations. The district is dense with warehouses, repair docks, and smuggling rings hiding within the labyrinthine canals.

docs.title: The Ironclad Sprawl
docs.text:
(Tinker’s & Artificer’s Quarter)

  • A newer district, filled with mechanists, artificers, and alchemists, many of whom are immigrants from Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig. Gas-lit signs flicker above shopfronts, advertising arcane-electric engines, clockwork contraptions, and mechanized limbs.

docs.title: The Aegis Quarter
docs.text:
(Military Quarter)

  • A fortified garrison, where the Archprelate of Binds maintains an iron grip on security. The [[Creosmagi]] train here, and ship docks service military patrol vessels.

docs.title: Penitent’s Rise
docs.text:
(Residential & Clerical Housing)

  • A dense multi-tiered district stacked along the city’s steepest inclines, where the city’s middle class and clerical administrators reside. Golemic lifts, powered by arcane electricity, ferry people between levels.

docs.title: The Chainstock Wards
docs.text:
(Industrial Slums & Low-Class Housing)

  • A smog-choked, overcrowded district where factory workers, dock laborers, and debt-bound "Redemptives" toil beneath the looming spires of the wealthier districts above.

docs.title: The Wraithmire Quarter
docs.text:
(Shrouded & Haunted Ruins)

  • The oldest part of the city, a ghostly, mist-covered ruin from the elemental storm’s fallout centuries ago. Few dare to live here, but some black-market traders, fugitives, and heretics hide in the mist-choked alleyways.

docs.title: Modes of Travel
docs.text:
Due to Hellhaven’s steep and winding streets, traditional carts struggle to traverse the city. Instead, the following alternative transportation methods have developed:

  • Treadwalkers – Clockwork exoskeletal frames, resembling steam-powered stilts, allow couriers and enforcers to ascend steep roads with ease.
  • Golemic Lifts – Towering arcane-powered elevators assist movement between altitude levels, commonly found in Penitent’s Rise and The Tribunal Forum.
  • Skyferries – Suspended tram-like gondolas, powered by arcane-electric current, ferry goods and passengers across the city’s highest districts.
  • Canal Ferries – Many of Hellhaven’s lower districts have waterways, where flat-bottomed steam skiffs operate as taxi services.

docs.title: Travel in the City
docs.text:
• Checkpoint System – Each district has controlled entry points where movement is monitored. Travel papers are required for restricted areas, such as The Adjudicary.
  • Curfew Enforcement – At sundown, non-essential movement is forbidden unless sanctioned.

docs.title: Entry and Reentry
docs.text:
• The Gate of Submission – The main landward entry into Hellhaven, where newcomers are interrogated and documented.
  • Brineyard Inspection Docks – All ships must register cargo and passengers upon arrival. Unregistered arrivals face severe punishment. Located in [[Chainmoor Brine Yards (Docks & Industrial Shipping)|Chainmoor Brine Yards]].
  • The Inner Gates – Sections of the city are separated by gated corridors, restricting access to sensitive areas.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
Hellhaven’s architecture is built with a mix of local stone, imported steel, and arcane-powered lighting:

  • Obsidian-Grey Brick & Ironwood Reinforcement – The foundational material for most buildings, durable enough to withstand the coastal gales.
  • Arcane-Electric Streetlights – Imported from Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig, these tesla-like lamps harness engineered magic, emitting a steady white-blue glow.
  • Copper-Inscribed Sigils – Many official buildings feature etched symbols of [[The Lord]]’s decree, warding glyphs, and reinforcement runes.

docs.title: 1st Era: The Refuge of the Mist (Founding of Gellhafn, 1354)
docs.text:
• Hellhaven, originally Gellhafn, was founded as a sanctuary for refugees fleeing the devastation of the elemental storms of the [[Tenechron]], a catastrophic event that left arcane-laden mist lingering along the coastline.
  • The city’s first settlers were survivors, building atop the ruins of a preexisting civilization, remnants of which still exist in Wraithmire Quarter.

docs.title: 2nd Era: The Industrial Reform (Trade with Vergrenzig, 1970s)
docs.text:
• Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig’s steampunk innovations reached Hellhaven, revolutionizing shipbuilding, arcane-electric power, and mechanical craftsmanship.
  • The Chainmoor Brine Yards and Ironclad Sprawl expanded, turning the city into a technological and maritime powerhouse.
  • However, industrialization brought new tensions, with Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig’s free-market ideals clashing against the strict theocratic rule of [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat]].

docs.title: 3rd Era: The Rise of the Concordat (Religious Takeover, 2021)
docs.text:
• [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]], a powerful group of [[The Lord]]’s clergy, arrived and seized control of Gellhafn, proclaiming the mist a divine trial to test mortal will.
  • Under their rule, Gellhafn was renamed Hellhaven, a "bastion of order in a world of chaos."
  • The great edicts were established: law, obedience, and industry above all else.

docs.title: 4th Era: The Era of Iron and Chains (Present Day)
docs.text:
• Hellhaven is at a crossroads, torn between its theocratic law and the technological advancements reshaping society.
  • [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat]] fears losing control over the population as innovation challenges their monopoly on power.
  • The Wraithmire Quarter’s mist has begun to shift unpredictably, with reports of strange figures emerging from its depths, an omen of past forces stirring once more…

docs.title: Landmarks
docs.text:
• Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Bastion of Judgment – A towering, fortress-like structure where criminals are sentenced and divine law is upheld. Public trials are held in the Forum of Redress before being carried out here.
  • Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Codexorium – A grand, heavily fortified archive where [[The Lord]]’s decrees are recorded. Some say the deepest vaults contain knowledge of [[The Lord]]’s true origins, though access is near impossible.
  • The Gallows of the Weighing Night – Located in the Tribunal Forum, this raised platform is where heretics and criminals are "weighed" and judged beyond redemption.
  • Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Vault of Penance -
  • Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/Aegis Bastion -

docs.title: Climate
docs.text: Hellhaven sits along the Locations/Regions/Windbor Coast, a cold, wind-lashed fjord known for harsh storms and sudden changes in temperature. The sea is treacherous, with jagged cliffs and unpredictable currents making it difficult for unskilled sailors to navigate safely.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Flora
  • Ironwood Trees – Hardy, slow-growing trees with dense bark, often used for shipbuilding.
  • Bitter Fen Moss – Found in the city's lower, damp areas; used in alchemical treatments.
  • Petrolune Bloom – A bioluminescent plant found in the coastal caves, its resin refined for Hellhaven’s fuel industry.
Fauna
  • Tide Hounds – Aquatic canines used to patrol the docks, trained to sniff out contraband.
  • Fjord Gulls – Opportunistic scavengers with eerie, almost human-like cries.
  • Drift Crabs – Large, aggressive crustaceans that sometimes invade the docks and attack unwary laborers.
Pests
  • Gutter Crows – Dark-feathered, intelligent birds that seem to whisper unsettling phrases. Some claim they are cursed spies of [[The Lord]]’s enforcers.
  • Chain Rats – A species of rodent with unnervingly strong teeth, known to chew through ship moorings and sabotage goods.
  • Mire Mites – Blood-draining insects that thrive in damp alleyways and basements.

docs.title: Symbolism
docs.text:
The Hellhapfen Emblem

A black sunburst behind a gilded balance scale, encircled by a ring of broken chains.

  • The sunburst represents [[The Lord]]’s divine authority shining upon the city.
  • The scales signify justice, law, and balance, the foundation of Hellhaven’s governance.
  • The chains, once whole, symbolize the city’s past as a refuge before it was brought under control.
Mascot: The Everbound Stag

A bronze-plated stag with chains woven into its antlers, eternally stepping forward but never breaking free.

  • Represents both order and sacrifice, the necessary burden of civilization under [[The Lord]]’s will.
  • The stag's bronze plating symbolizes the fusion of the arcane and industrial in Hellhaven’s rule.
  • A commonly used motif in official banners, statues, and clergy robes.

docs.title: Settlement Leaders
docs.text: Hellhaven is ruled through divine law, upheld by a structured theocratic hierarchy. Power is centralized within [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]], a ruling body that dictates legislation, military actions, trade policies, and spiritual doctrine.

docs.title: The Concordat of Chains
docs.text: A grand clergy led by tribunal of seven archprelates, each overseeing different aspects of law and governance.

docs.title: **The Seven Archprelates
docs.text:
1. Archprelate of Binds – Oversees law enforcement, punishment, and judiciary matters. ^c5ef99
    • Currently [[Rhaeven Marciel|Archprelate of Binds Rhaeven Marciel]]
  2. Archprelate of Tithes – Ensures tax collection, resource distribution, and trade oversight. ^8f3fff
    • Currently [[Archprelate of Tithes Orielle Vossin]]
  3. Archprelate of Flame – Manages industry, infrastructure, and arcane energy harnessing. ^9cb211
    • Currently [[Archprelate of Flame Tessa Durnford]]
  4. Archprelate of Ledgers – Controls historical record-keeping, bureaucracy, and census data. ^dac724
    • Currently [[Archprelate of Ledgers Valeria Silvershade]]
  5. Archprelate of Godspel – Directs religious doctrine, conversion efforts, and temple affairs. ^5f573b
    • Currently [[Archprelate of Godspel Solana Vokov]]
  6. Archprelate of Brine – Regulates naval defense, maritime trade, and sea-based industries. ^871683
    • Currently [[Archprelate of Brine Abena Khatari]]
  7. Archprelate of Gates – Handles immigration, border security, and internal travel permissions. ^d5db4e
    • Currently [[Archprelate of Gates Harland Dorne]]
Legislation

^abc6e7

docs.title: The Creed of Binding Light
docs.text:
(Foundational legal doctrines of Hellhaven)

The Unerring Edict

"A city without law is a body without a spine. Obedience brings order, and order brings salvation."

  • The core document that codifies governance, labor divisions, and citizen obligations.
The Creed of Tribute

"To each, their station; to each, their due. That which is given in sacrifice is repaid in divine favor."

  • Governs tithes, taxation, and labor servitude.
The Concord of Balance

"Punishment must be just, mercy must be measured, and order must be absolute."

  • The legal standard for crime, sentencing, and civic discipline.

docs.title: The Gellhafn Codex
docs.text:
A remnant from Hellhaven’s past as Gellhafn, before the rise of the clergy, this body of law governs the foundational civic structures of the city, property rights, inheritance, and the classification of citizens. Though much of it has been rewritten to fit [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]]' doctrine, some old maritime and trade laws remain in effect.

The Charter of Harbormasters

An ancient decree that regulates docking fees, ship registrations, and the division of waterfront properties. It is one of the few pre-theocracy laws still honored by both secular traders and the clergy.

docs.title: The Gulf Concords
docs.text:
A maritime legal framework developed in agreement with the other major coastal powers of Locations/Regions/Loierr Fenest to regulate trade routes, naval engagements, and piracy control. Hellhaven plays an outsized role in its enforcement.

The Treaty of Salt and Iron

A trade and naval defense agreement between Hellhaven, the Republic of Rellavoss, and the Tidecourt of Vethmar. It details mutual protection pacts, the exchange of naval technology, and taxation rights over key waterways.

docs.title: Factions
docs.text:
[[Creosmagi|The Creosmagi]]

Role: Hellhaven’s paramilitary force, law enforcement, and inquisitorial body.

  • Tasked with maintaining order, hunting criminals, and ensuring compliance with The Creed of Binding Light.
  • Enforcers carry petrolune-powered "Lawgiver" firelances, capable of non-lethal or deadly force.
  • Their ranks include interrogators, penal overseers, and corruption hunters.
Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Lord’s Tithe Commission

Role: Regulates taxation, Creosmark Token issuing, and financial oversight.

  • Responsible for issuing Creosmark Tokens and ensuring that citizens fulfill their labor obligations.
  • Wealthy merchants and artisans owe their permits to the Commission and must pay tithes to maintain status.
  • Led by the Archprelate of Ledgers.

^172ce7

[[Hellhaven Concord|The Hellhaven Concord]]

Role: The dominant maritime trade and naval defense organization.

  • Balances Hellhaven’s dependence on Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig’s technology with its own naval sovereignty.
  • Its privateer armada patrols the gulf, warding off pirates, smugglers, and illegal traffickers.
  • Known for its strict hierarchy and loyalty to the Archprelate of Brine.
[[Chainmoor Guild]]

Role: The hidden underbelly of Hellhaven’s economy, operating outside official trade channels.

  • Smuggles unregistered arcane goods, stolen Creosmark Tokens, and restricted Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig tech.
  • Provides alternate employment for those seeking to escape [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]]'s rigid caste system.
  • Hunted relentlessly by the [[Creosmagi]], but never fully eradicated.
The Sanctum of Ingress

Role: The highest theological authority, dictating worship practices and religious law. Professions: Judicial Lector

  • Houses the most powerful clerics and scholars, who interpret [[The Lord]]’s will.
  • Directly oversees rites of redemption, atonement rituals, and sacrificial doctrines.
  • Controls the historical record, determining what truths are spoken and what are erased.
  • Led by the Archprelate of Godspel and Archprelate of Ledgers.

^ab2ae3

docs.title: Crime
docs.text: Crime in Hellhaven exists in the shadows, as overt defiance is swiftly crushed. However, the strict legal structure itself breeds subversion, leading to a thriving underground economy, black markets, and rebellion.

docs.title: Common Crimes & Punishments
docs.text: Crime Punishment Possession of an unregistered arcane artifact Confiscation, fine, or exile Forgery of a Creosmark Token Public branding and lifetime servitude Smuggling goods through Chainmoor Brine Yards Labor in the Deep Mines Unauthorized movement beyond assigned district Loss of work privileges (starvation risk) Blasphemy against The Creed of Binding Light Penal servitude or execution Association with the [[Chainmoor Guild]] Permanent Creosmark revocation (exile or death)

docs.title: Criminal Organizations
docs.text:
Despite the [[Creosmagi]]’s brutal efficiency, Hellhaven’s oppressed lower classes have fueled the rise of secret societies and insurgent groups:

  • [[Concordat of Chains#^151c8a|The Hooded Covenant]] – A hidden sect within the clergy itself, questioning [[The Lord]]’s divinity.
  • The Hollowed – A group of former citizens stripped of their Creosmarks, surviving in the city’s ruins.
  • The Gilded Knives – An elite guild of assassins and spies, operating under noble patronage. ^dcfae3

docs.title: Adaptation to Threats
docs.text: Hellhaven has endured centuries of external assaults and internal upheaval, shaping its strict security measures and defensive innovations. The city’s position at the fjord’s mouth provides a natural barrier against naval incursions, but the treacherous currents and sudden storms have also forced the development of specialized ship designs and navigational tools. - Creosmagi Enforcement – The clergy’s militant enforcers, the [[Creosmagi]], use sangromantic runes and blood-bound Creosmark Tokens to monitor movement within the city. Any unregistered individual attempting to pass through major checkpoints is quickly detained. - The Fogwardens – A special division of Hellhaven’s navy dedicated to navigating the Mist Veil, the lingering arcane phenomenon left behind by the elemental storm fallout. The Veil obscures portions of the coastline, harboring dangerous entities and lost ships. - Storm-Bound Bastions – Fortified watchtowers, empowered by Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig-engineered stormcatchers, draw and disperse ambient magical energy, preventing unnatural tempests from overwhelming the city. These bastions also serve as waystations for trained Galewrights, navigators who specialize in reading and mitigating the unpredictable weather. - The Ever-Closed Gates – Hellhaven’s inner sanctum, Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/Aegis Sancta, remains sealed behind reinforced walls that have never been breached. Only those carrying the Seal of Oaths, a relic imbued with layers of divine and arcane protections, may enter. - Fugue Wardings – Due to historical conflicts with necromantic forces, all bodies within the city are ritually marked with protective sigils to prevent their reanimation. Unauthorized burial outside consecrated grounds is strictly forbidden.

docs.title: Arcane Integration
docs.text:
While magic is heavily regulated under the Concordat’s rule, it remains deeply embedded in Hellhaven’s infrastructure, industries, and daily life.

  • Petrolune Refinement – Though too unstable for construction, [[petrolune]] is refined into controlled arcane conductors that power Hellhaven’s ether-lamps, heating systems, and automated machinery.
  • Bound Constructs – Sentient golems are outlawed, but restricted automata, arcane-powered machines bound to predefined tasks, are commonly used in industry and enforcement. The [[Creosmagi]] employ Chain-Sentinels, armored constructs designed to apprehend criminals and suppress uprisings.
  • Blood-Bound Tokens – Each citizen carries a Creosmark, imbued with their blood sacrifice and ensuring their movement through the city remains traceable. Unauthorized modification or tampering with these sigils is punishable by exile or execution.
  • The Sigil Veil – A massive, citywide ward system created in collaboration with Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig’s artificers. This etheric lattice prevents large-scale teleportation within Hellhaven and detects unregistered magical activity.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
Hellhaven’s spiritual framework is deeply entwined with the [[Concordat of Chains]], enforcing strict theological doctrine and ensuring worship remains centralized under the ruling clergy. The faithful believe that law and order are divinely mandated, and heretical deviations are swiftly punished.

  • The Creed of the Binding Lightlocations/Settlements/Haven of Hale/Subpages/Hellhapfen Governance and Power#^abc6e7|* – The central religious doctrine, which asserts that mortal existence is meant to be disciplined and guided under divine law, lest chaos consume all.
  • Oath-Keepers of the Chain – An elite sect of clergy responsible for interpreting divine will and ensuring all contracts, laws, and social structures align with holy scripture. ^df513d
  • Pilgrimage of the Condemned – A grim tradition where those accused of high treason may attempt a dangerous journey across the Mist Veil to seek absolution. Few return, and those who do are forever marked by their trial.

docs.title: Holidays
docs.text:
• The Day of Supplication – A solemn day of fasting and prayer where the citizens reaffirm their devotion to the Concordat’s laws. It is customary to publicly confess minor transgressions and seek absolution from the clergy.
  • The Binding Oath – A citywide festival marking the renewal of Hellhaven’s foundational contracts, where new guild members, citizens, and officials formally swear allegiance to the city. Arcane sigils are ritually inscribed upon public monuments to reinforce the sanctity of the oaths.
  • The Vigil of Chains – A night-long ritual where the faithful carry lanterns through the streets, symbolizing their commitment to order and vigilance against corruption. [[Creosmagi]] use this event to investigate suspected dissidents under the cover of religious observance.
  • The Tithe of Remembrance – A day of offering where citizens donate portions of their wealth or labor to the city’s central authority. It commemorates the sacrifices of those who perished during the early years of Hellhaven’s establishment.
  • The Exultation of the Storm’s End – A rare celebration held only once per generation when a particularly dangerous arcane storm is successfully dispelled. It serves as a reminder of Hellhaven’s resilience and technological advancements.

docs.title: The Creosmagi[[Creosmagi|*]]
docs.text:
A subsect of the Concordat responsible for regulating and policing magic users within Hellhaven.

  • [[Magnus Forscythe]] – The current High Executor of the [[Creosmagi]], responsible for the enforcement of Hellhaven’s laws and overseeing the Creosmark distribution system. Forscythe’s background in arcane martial arts and blood-binding rituals makes him a fearsome figure. His operations ensure total control over the city’s populace.
  • [[Marshal Seraphine Vexis]] (b. 2095) - Relentless enforcer of magic restrictions
    • A rising star in the [[Creosmagi]], Seraphine was raised in the system and has absolute faith in its necessity. She sees magic as a force that must be controlled for society’s survival. However, she has a complicated respect for rogue casters who manage to elude her.
  • [[Interrogator Orlen Vesk]] (b. 2088) - Master of arcane extraction techniques
    • A specialist in forced memory extraction, Vesk is a cold pragmatist who sees people as puzzles to be solved. He thrives in the shadows, knowing secrets no one else should know.
  • [[Scribe Elion Faeth]] (b. 2100) - Young scholar assigned to classify restricted spells
    • Once a curious and ambitious magic user, Faeth was forcibly recruited into the Adjudicators after an unauthorized spell incident. Now he files confiscated spell formulas while secretly copying some for his own research.

docs.title: The Concordat of Chains[[Concordat of Chains|*]]
docs.text:
The ruling body enforcing the worship of [[The Lord]], maintaining control through strict laws, religious doctrine, and the Creosmark system.

  • [[Archprelate of Godspel Solana Vokov]] – A primary theological leaders of [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]]
    • Vokov is renowned for her piety and unwavering commitment to [[The Lord]]. Her decision-making often steers Hellhaven’s policies toward more restrictive, authoritarian measures in the name of divine order.
  • [[High Arbiter Lucenna Draeven]] (b. 2078) - Chief Judge of Hellhaven's Theocratic Courts
    • An unyielding and calculating judge responsible for overseeing major trials. She is particularly infamous for using memory extractions as legal evidence. Privately, she’s weary of the Concordat’s corruption but believes order must be preserved above all else. Works under [[Archprelate of Ledgers Valeria Silvershade]].
  • [[Purifier Yevan Horne]] (b. 2093) - Leader of the [[Creosmagi]]
    • A ruthless inquisitor who also leads [[Creosmagi#^1d695d|The Burning Veil]], a secret order hunting heretics and rogue arcanists. He views any deviation from the The Creed of Binding Light as a disease to be excised. His reputation for unforgiving judgment and arcane tortures precedes him. Works under [[Rhaeven Marciel|Archprelate of Binds Rhaeven Marciel]].
  • [[Scribe Maelis Rhell]] (b. 2085) - Head of the Codexorium
    • A scholar tasked with curating and censoring the city’s pre-Dread knowledge. She secretly hoards banned texts and believes some arcane relics should not be destroyed but repurposed for Hellhaven’s protection.
  • [[Archprelate of Gates Harland Dorne]] (b. 2091) - Organizer of the Creosmark and city defense
    • Oversees the arcane branding process that binds Hellhaven citizens to their assigned roles. While outwardly a devoted Concordat official, Dorne has begun questioning the ethics of the system after seeing the long-term toll it takes on families. Works under [[Purifier Yevan Horne]] and [[Archprelate of Ledgers Valeria Silvershade]].
  • [[Rhaeven Marciel|Archprelate of Binds Rhaeven Marciel]]
    • Archprelate of Binds Rhaeven Marciel is the ruthless and unyielding overseer of Locations/Landmarks/Establishments/The Vault of Penance. A figure draped in both reverence and terror, he is the ultimate enforcer of divine law in Hellhaven, personally ensuring that heretics confess, that dangerous artifacts remain under the [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat]]’s control, and that [[The Lord]]’s will is never questioned. Marciel embodies theocratic absolutism, unyielding, methodical, and utterly convinced of his righteous purpose.

docs.title: Hellhaven Concord[[Hellhaven Concord|*]]
docs.text:
• [[Archprelate of Brine Abena Khatari]]
    • A formidable woman of unwavering conviction, Abena Khatari presides over the maritime faith and governance of the Hellhaven Concord.
