She enforces the Creed of Binding Light with a zeal that both inspires and terrifies, ensuring that all seafaring peoples remain loyal to the Concord’s doctrine. Her word is law upon the waves, and her influence extends from temple halls to warships. Though she presents herself as a pious steward of order, whispers circulate of her more pragmatic alliances, ensuring that faith and power remain intertwined.
  • [[Grand Admiral Nathaniel Dlamini]]
    • Nathaniel Dlamini is a veteran of countless naval conflicts, his leadership in the Tempest Watch making him both feared and respected. Born into a family of sailors, his rise through the ranks was swift, driven by tactical brilliance and ruthless efficiency. He views the Concord’s enemies, both external and internal, as threats to be crushed beneath the might of his fleet. While he remains publicly loyal to Abena Khatari, there are those who wonder if his ambitions stretch beyond mere command, his fleet a power unto itself.
  • [[Eoghan Frosttide]] - Tidecourt of Vethmar Diplomat
    • A proud and imposing triton, Eoghan Frosttide represents the Tidecourt of Vethmar, the ancient and once-dominant rulers of the sea. Though bound by the Concord’s rule, they do not hide their disdain for Hellhaven’s control, seeing it as an insult to their people’s legacy. In secret, they stir the embers of Vethmar’s old ambitions, fostering alliances among discontented factions. They walk a fine line, keeping their court relevant within the Concord while waiting for the moment to reclaim the seas for their kin.
  • [[Sifhild Brandtdottir]] - The Caedrith Accord Diplomat
    • A staunch advocate for the rights of mages and scholars, Sifhild Brandtdottir stands against the Concord’s draconian punishments for magical misuse. As a half-orc raised among the arcane scholars of the Caedrith Accord, she sees knowledge as a force to be guided, not shackled by religious dogma. Her clashes with the Archprelate of Brine are frequent, and her growing frustration with the Concord’s brutality may soon push her towards open defiance.
  • [[Lethabo Masego]] - The Argent Bastion Diplomat
    • Lethabo Masego is a skilled negotiator and seasoned military commander, entrusted with protecting the Argent Bastion’s interests within the Concord. The Bastion’s elite forces serve as the shield against outside threats, and Lethabo ensures they remain a dominant power within the coalition. A pragmatist, he understands that stability must be maintained, but he also knows that the Bastion must never be seen as a mere pawn of Hellhaven’s rulers.
  • [[Zuberi Adewale]] - The Sable Warden Conclave Diplomat
    • A calculating and enigmatic figure, Zuberi Adewale speaks for the Sable Warden Conclave, the shadowy enforcers of the Concord’s will. While she outwardly supports the Archprelate’s mission, her true motives remain elusive. Some suspect that she works to expand the Conclave’s power beyond Hellhaven, while others believe she is playing a deeper game, perhaps even setting the stage for a shift in control. Regardless, her mere presence is enough to make even the most hardened politicians uneasy.
  • [[Elise von Rheinhardt]] - Republic of Rellavoss Diplomat
    • Elise von Rheinhardt embodies the diplomatic finesse and cunning required to represent Rellavoss, a republic caught between the demands of its trade interests and the ambitions of its neighbors. She carefully maneuvers the political landscape, ensuring that Rellavoss remains prosperous without falling too deeply under the Concord’s control. However, her patience with Aexithis’s growing calls for independence is running thin, and she may soon have to choose between diplomacy and action.
  • [[Baldur Falkenstein]] - The Commonwealth of Aexithis Diplomat
    • Baldur Falkenstein is the quiet architect of Aexithis’s growing independence movement. A shrewd and charismatic leader, he plays the long game, gathering allies, securing resources, and subtly pushing the Commonwealth toward self-rule. He publicly maintains the façade of loyalty to the Concord, but in the shadows, he ensures that Aexithis’s innovations remain firmly under its own control. If the moment comes to break free, he will be ready.
  • [[Gerhard Eisenrauch]] - The Ironwreath Syndicate Diplomat
    • Gerhard Eisenrauch is a blunt, ambitious representative of the Ironwreath Syndicate, a criminal network struggling for legitimacy. Coming from the shadowed depths of the Kagecombs, he fights to elevate his people’s status within the Concord, demanding the respect and influence that has long been denied to them. While some dismiss him as a glorified smuggler, others recognize the growing reach of the Syndicate’s operations. Gerhard knows that true power is not given, it is taken.

docs.title: Hellhaven Mercenary Company[[Hellhaven Mercenary Company|*]]
docs.text:
• [[Fenric of the Chain]] – The enigmatic leader of a highly-skilled group of mercenaries loyal to Hellhaven’s ruling elite. Known for his cold pragmatism, Fenric takes on missions that require absolute discretion and continental travel, from eliminating high-profile threats to conducting undercover operations.
  • [[Commander Dain Verrik]] (b. 2076) - A seasoned veteran who’s seen more than his share of battles, Commander Dain Verrik commands respect both for his tactical mind and his brutal efficiency. A former soldier in the Hellhaven military, he defected after his unit was betrayed in a coup attempt. He built the Hellhaven Mercenary Company from the ground up, gathering disenfranchised soldiers, exiles, and former criminals. Verrik is a man of few words, and his reputation for decisive action has earned the company lucrative contracts. He often takes a personal hand in the most dangerous assignments, proving his mettle in combat and solidifying his role as the undisputed leader. His only weakness is his relentless ambition, which may eventually cause him to overstep his boundaries.
  • [[Lieutenant Kiera Thorne]] (b. 2092) - Thorne joined the Hellhaven Mercenary Company at the age of 18, quickly rising through the ranks due to her sharp strategic mind and adeptness at logistics. Trained in both traditional warfare and modern mercenary tactics, she serves as Verrik’s second-in-command. She’s a calm, collected strategist, known for her resourcefulness and ability to outthink opponents before they even realize they're in a losing battle. Thorne has a unique bond with her soldiers, having personally hand-picked many of them, and she takes her role as their leader and protector very seriously. Outside the battlefield, she's a meticulous planner and is known to study the patterns of Hellhaven’s political landscape, preparing for any shifts that could impact her company’s contracts.
  • [[Quinn "Ironclad" Voss]] (b. 2087) - Known as "Ironclad" for his heavily augmented body, Quinn Voss was once a simple enforcer for a minor gang. However, after a near-fatal encounter during an ambush, he had to undergo extensive arcane augmentations to survive. Now with cybernetic arms, reinforced legs, and arcane-infused lungs, Quinn is a living weapon and a terrifying presence on the battlefield. He's a quiet individual, preferring to let his actions speak for themselves, but he’s fiercely loyal to Commander Verrik, whom he considers both a leader and a friend. Despite his brutal reputation, he has a strict code of honor and never engages in unnecessary cruelty, distinguishing him from many of his mercenary peers.

docs.title: The Gilded Tribunal[[The Gilded Tribunal|*]]
docs.text:
_(Legal/Political Faction)

  • [[Archprelate of Ledgers Valeria Silvershade]] – A high-ranking official in the Gilded Tribunal, an elite legal faction tasked with interpreting and managing Hellhaven’s complex system of laws. Known for her unyielding adherence to the letter of the law, Silvershade is both revered and feared for her ability to manipulate the legal system in favor of the city's ruling class.
  • [[Archprelate of Tithes Orielle Vossin]] (b. 2080) - The locations/Settlements/Haven of Hale/Subpages/Hellhapfen Governance and Power#^8f3fff, Orielle Vossin holds immense sway over Hellhaven’s financial laws. A brilliant legal mind, she was once a young prodigy who rose through the ranks of Hellhaven’s bureaucracy before securing her place in the Tribunal. Known for her sharp wit and calculating demeanor, Vossin has become a symbol of ruthless efficiency in both the political and economic spheres. She’s made countless decisions that have cemented her as the gatekeeper of Hellhaven’s financial stability, often making tough calls that benefit the city’s elites while crushing the lower classes. While she has few true allies, her influence is unshakable, and many whisper that she holds hidden alliances with dark forces, both within and outside of the Tribunal.
  • [[Veran Duskholt]] (b. 2074) - Veran Duskholt, the head of the Merchant-Prince Syndicate, is a man of silver-tongued diplomacy and cutthroat business acumen. His syndicate controls the majority of Hellhaven’s merchant activities, including trade with foreign nations like the Locations/Settlements/Vermilion Republic/Rellavoss and Tidecourt of Vethmar. Duskholt is known for using subtle manipulation and long-term planning to secure his position, often outmaneuvering rivals without ever showing his hand. His wealth allows him to influence every major political decision in the city, and his ability to broker favorable deals for Hellhaven ensures his place among the city’s most powerful individuals. Beneath his smooth exterior, however, Duskholt has a dark reputation for getting his hands dirty when needed, even if it means removing anyone who gets in his way.
  • [[Ambassador Helia Varne]] (b. 2089) - Helia Varne serves as the official liaison between Hellhaven and its trading partners, most notably the Republic of Rellavoss. She is a gifted diplomat, known for her ability to secure mutually beneficial agreements between the city's various factions and the powerful mercantile republic. Varne’s success is rooted in her ability to balance power, charm, and ruthlessness in every negotiation. She is particularly skilled at navigating the complexities of foreign politics, where she regularly faces pressure from the Locations/Settlements/Vermilion Republic/Rellavoss merchant council. Many suspect Varne’s loyalty lies more with her ambition than with the city itself, and some even claim she is secretly working to align Hellhaven with outside powers in the gulf, to the detriment of the city’s theocratic rulers.

docs.title: Crimson Lanterns[[Crimson Lanterns|*]]
docs.text:
_(Crime Faction)

  • [[Alise "Redhand" Carrick]] – A ruthless co-leader of the Crimson Lanterns, an underground organization involved in smuggling illegal magical items and relics stolen from merchant caravans. Carrick's operations span Hellhaven’s slums and the outlying ports, making her a significant threat to the Concordat's control.
  • [[Master Sylpho "The Red Veil"]] (b. 2081) - An enigmatic leader of the Crimson Lanterns, Master Sylpho, is an individual who operates in the shadows, his true motives known only to a few. Known for his deadly elegance and sharp intellect, he controls a vast network of underground crime, including extortion, illegal arcane practices, and a series of illicit brothels. The "Red Veil" is an apt moniker, as he is rarely seen without a veil of deep crimson cloth, hiding his identity and adding to his mystique. Though he often appears calm and composed, his ruthlessness has made him one of Hellhaven’s most feared figures. Sylpho’s past is a well-guarded secret, but it’s rumored that he rose to power after orchestrating the assassination of his predecessor, the previous leader of the Lanterns.
  • [[Dante "Blackfang" Ruelle]] (b. 2094) - A notorious enforcer for the Crimson Lanterns, Dante Ruelle earned his moniker “Blackfang” after surviving a [[Creosmagi#^1d695d|Burning Veil]] assassination attempt that left him with a scarred face and a mouth full of sharp, blackened teeth. Once a soldier for the Hellhaven military, Dante was dishonorably discharged after an altercation with his superior officers. He turned to a life of crime and quickly rose through the ranks of the Lanterns, his brutal efficiency and relentless violence making him a feared figure in Hellhaven’s underworld. Known for his sadistic nature, Dante enjoys making an example of those who defy the Lanterns, whether through intimidation or outright brutality. His loyalty to Master Sylpho is absolute, and Blackfang is one of his most trusted, and feared, lieutenants.
  • [[Lyric Ambré]] (b. 2100) - Lyric Ambré is the youngest member of the Crimson Lanterns, but her rise to prominence has been swift. A former socialite turned spy, she uses her charm, wit, and beauty to infiltrate the city’s upper echelons, gathering information and manipulating powerful figures to further the Lanterns’ goals. Though her primary role is that of a spy and infiltrator, Lyric is also skilled in deception, blackmail, and covert operations. She is known for her ability to manipulate people without them ever realizing they’ve been played. Many of Hellhaven’s elites unknowingly find themselves entrapped by Lyric, whose true loyalty lies not with the rich and powerful but with the Lanterns and their agenda.

docs.title: The Forge Collective[[The Forge Collective|*]]
docs.text:
_(Industry/Faction)

  • [[Archprelate of Flame Tessa Durnford]] – Adminstrator of The Forge Collective, a powerful union of inventors, engineers, and artisans responsible for Hellhaven’s technological innovations. Durnford is an influential figure in the steampunk industry, playing a crucial role in shaping the city’s infrastructure and machinery.
  • [[Master Engineer Tavrin Kael]] (b. 2079) - Tavrin Kael is the co-head of the Forge Collective, Hellhaven's largest guild of industrial crafters and magitech engineers. A master of combining arcane power with industrial machinery, Kael is responsible for some of the most impressive and deadly weapons the city has ever produced. His work has ensured that Hellhaven maintains its technological edge in the Locations/Regions/Windbor Coast region, with magitech devices and weaponry in high demand from both local and foreign buyers. Kael is a perfectionist, obsessed with efficiency and innovation, and will stop at nothing to push the boundaries of magitech. However, his single-mindedness has alienated many of his fellow engineers, leading to growing tensions within the Collective. Despite this, Kael’s genius is undeniable, and his creations continue to reshape Hellhaven’s industrial landscape.
  • [[Saria "Redstrike" Vexen]] (b. 2095) - A rising star in the Forge Collective, Saria Vexen is a prodigy in the field of experimental weaponry. Known for her signature “Redstrike” blasters, a type of arcane-infused firearm, she is one of the Collective's most brilliant, and volatile, engineers. Saria’s work often pushes the boundaries of safety, resulting in both groundbreaking inventions and disastrous failures. She is fiercely protective of her inventions, seeing them as extensions of herself, and has a reputation for ignoring orders and working alone. Though Kael often chastises her for her reckless approach, Saria’s talent cannot be denied, and many in the Collective see her as the future of magitech warfare. She is driven by a desire to create something that will outlive her, something that will change the course of history.
  • [[Harlan "Brassfist" Dorne]] (b. 2083) - Harlan Dorne is a former mercenary who became the head of security for the Forge Collective’s vast operations. Known for his imposing size and strength, Harlan is a master of both physical combat and industrial safety. With extensive cybernetic enhancements and a brutal fighting style, he is the perfect enforcer for a guild that deals in weapons and arcane devices. Harlan is fiercely loyal to Tavrin Kael and the Collective’s cause, seeing the creation of new technologies as the path to Hellhaven’s dominance in the Locations/Regions/Windbor Coast. Though he prefers a straightforward approach to solving problems, Harlan has developed a growing interest in the political machinations of the city, leading some to suspect he may one day seek a role in governance.

docs.title: The Mnemonic Consortium[[Mnemonic Consortium|*]]
docs.text:
A hidden network of scholars, rogue casters, and outcasts seeking to reclaim lost magic and undermine the Concordat’s control.

  • [[Lorica "Lory" Vance]] (b. 2097) - Ex-Adjudicator turned rogue arcanist
    • A former Scribe who defected after realizing the truth about the memory purges. Lory now leads a small resistance cell, using her insider knowledge to free marked arcanists before they’re executed or imprisoned.
  • [[Vaelin "The Unbound" Marrow]] (b. 2083) - Notorious spellbreaker and fugitive
    • A master of counter-seal magic, Vaelin specializes in removing arcane restrictions, including the Creosmarks. His reckless nature and habit of taking dangerous risks put him at odds with the Consortium’s leadership.
  • [[Dr. Edria Moss]] (b. 2070s, exact year unknown) - Former Concordat scholar and codebreaker
    • One of the few people alive who can still read pre-Dread spell scripts. While she rarely fights, her knowledge is invaluable. Some say she has decoded fragments of [[Sylvara Morn]]’s lost teachings.

docs.title: The Concordance of the Unchained[[Concordance of the Unchained|*]]
docs.text:
A dangerous faction that believes the Dread was a moment of transcendence and seeks to complete the process by further breaking magical limits.

  • [[High Seer Kasiel Vorth]] (b. 2065) - Leader of the Concordance
    • A charismatic and unhinged visionary who claims to have witnessed the Dread firsthand and seeks to finish what it started. He is believed to have unlocked forbidden pre-Dread spells that warp reality itself.
  • [[Nyssa "Echo" Veyne]] (b. 2101) - Psionicist and voidwalker
    • A young and unstable psion who claims she can hear the voices of those lost to the Dread. Her abilities make her a powerful oracle, but at the cost of her sanity.
  • [[Orphiel Zahn, The Hollow Saint]] (b. ???, possibly pre-Dread) - Supposed immortal entity tied to the Dread
    • An elusive, possibly undead figure who some claim predates Hellhaven itself. His existence is debated, but his name appears in multiple forbidden texts.

docs.title: The Smog Barons[[The Smog Barons|*]]
docs.text:
A syndicate of wealthy merchants, corrupt officials, and black-market traders controlling Hellhaven’s underworld economy.

  • [["Duke" Valster Goldfound]] (b. 2082) - Leader of the Goldfound Syndicate
    • The self-proclaimed “Duke” of Hellhaven’s black market, Kordaine runs smuggling rings, illicit trade routes, and underground arcane deals. His interests often conflict with both [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat]] and the [[Mnemonic Consortium]].
  • [[Silva Runehart]] (b. 2090) - Chemist and alchemist dealing in contraband elixirs
    • An expert in synthetic magic enhancements, Runehart produces banned alchemical brews that grant temporary spellcasting abilities to those without innate magic.
  • [[Captain Drevan "Rust" Sorrell]] (b. 2085) - Corrupt enforcer running illegal port operations
    • An ex-naval officer who now controls Hellhaven’s black-market docks, Drevan ensures smuggled goods make it into the city undetected.

docs.title: Hellhaven's Outer Reaches & Wild Cards
docs.text:
Figures who operate outside the structured factions but still influence events.

  • [[Cassian "Cinder" Veyne]] (b. 2096) - Bounty hunter with shifting allegiances
    • Once a member of the Burning Veil, Cassian defected and now works for whoever pays best. Though skilled, he has a habit of forming personal attachments to targets.
  • [[Sister Lenora Vale]] (b. 2080s, exact year unknown) - Rogue priestess who follows an outlawed faith
    • A former Concordat priestess who preaches a heretical version of [[The Lord]]’s doctrine. Some say she heals the marked, removing the arcane chains of the Creosmark.
  • [[Gale Nox, the Phantom Dealer]] (b. ???, age unknown) - Sells dangerous artifacts to the highest bidder
    • A mysterious arms dealer who seems to appear when you need something most, for a steep price. No one knows what they look like, but their name is whispered in every black-market deal.

docs.title: Historical Figures
docs.text:
Queen Nyssa of the Hollow Veil (r. 1600s - ?)

A dark elven ruler who forged alliances between the isolated settlements of the Kagecombs, establishing trade routes that would later become crucial for resettlement on the surface. She was famed for her use of umbra-woven silk, a rare textile infused with shadow magic. Legends claim she still rules in some hidden enclave beneath the world.

Hierophant-Magus Aulmareth (d. ~1920)

An enigmatic mage-priest who prophesied the end of the elemental storms decades before they ceased. Some believe he played a secret role in stabilizing [[The Arras]], though his followers insist he ascended before he could witness the world’s return to the surface. His abandoned sanctum, buried deep in the Kagecombs, is still sought by scholars and treasure hunters.

Prophet-Admiral Sefor Jurek (fl. 1930s)

Commander of the Ark Tower and human leader in Gellhafn Led the first human fleet to Gellhafn in 1932, integrating human settlers into the city's existing power structure. His followers introduced the worship of [[The Lord]], which gradually gained traction among the city's ruling elite.

Felecia Everhart, The Last Matron (d. ~1940)

Felecia Everhart was the final Matron of the Mist Shapers, a secretive sect of mages who were once revered for their ability to manipulate the strange energies left behind by the Elemental Storm. Everhart was accused of using forbidden rituals to control the flow of mist and was executed publicly in one of Hellhaven’s grandest displays of power. Her death marked the end of the Mist Shapers and the beginning of Hellhaven's stricter stance on magic. However, whispers of her power persist, and some believe her spirit still haunts the fog-covered regions of the city.

Commander Elara Vael (d. ~1950)

One of Hellhaven's earliest military commanders, Elara led the Stormbreaker Campaign against the monstrous forces that emerged after the elemental storm. Her actions helped establish Gellhafn as a fortified city, ensuring its survival during the early years of its formation. However, her death during a ritualistic event in the Mist Veil led to the eventual ascension of the current authoritarian regime. She is a controversial figure, with some viewing her as a martyr and others as a symbol of oppressive military rule. She is survived by the collective naval force known as the [[Tempest Watch]].

Harven Norrick (fl. 1960s)

A former pirate captain who rose to prominence after the Mist Veil disaster, Harven Norrick was instrumental in organizing the The Free Enclaves of Istrecce. His initial involvement in Hellhaven's early mercantile agreements saw him broker several under-the-table deals with the clergy, providing essential supplies during the city’s rebuild. Norrick’s fortunes changed after a failed attempt to seize power during a factional civil war. His escape into the outer gulf marked the beginning of his infamous pirate career. Though labeled a traitor by the clergy, Norrick’s name is still whispered in the taverns of Hellhaven as a symbol of rebellion and freedom.

Caius Rhorn, The Merchant King (fl. 1960s-1980s)

Caius Rhorn was the wealthiest merchant in Hellhaven during the early days of its transformation into a thriving port city. He was the first to establish trade routes with the Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig, facilitating the exchange of goods that would fuel Hellhaven's growth into a metropolis. Rhorn was a master of negotiation, often playing rival factions against each other to increase his influence. His assassination remains a mystery, but his fortune and the merchant guilds he founded continue to shape Hellhaven's economy to this day.

Empress Sylvara Morn (d. ~2000)

Empress Sylvara was a visionary who sought to create alliances with the nearby gulf nations during the days of Gellhafn’s most fragile state. Known for her diplomatic grace and foresight, she expanded the city’s trade routes and helped broker peace agreements with the Republic of Rellavoss and Tidecourt of Vethmar. However, her reign was cut short when she mysteriously disappeared, leaving behind only cryptic messages about “a storm within.” While some believe she was a victim of a coup, others suggest she vanished voluntarily as part of a larger conspiracy involving powerful factions within the city.

Lord Athelius Corvenar (r. 2020s - 2030s)

One of the impactful figures of Hellhaven's theocracy, Lord Athelius was a prominent noble during the city’s early days as Hellhaven. He led the establishment of the The Creed of Binding Light after the city’s transformation into a theocracy, marking the beginning of the clergy’s dominance. Though largely remembered for his role in shaping the new religious laws, Athelius was also a shrewd political leader who consolidated power and unified the city’s factions under a single banner. Some claim he made a secret pact with arcane forces, although such rumors were never proven. His legacy remains deeply interwoven with the city's current structure.

The Phoenix Magister (fl. ~2030)

Radical arcane scholar post-Dread A revolutionary spellcaster who sees the [[The Dread|Dread]] as an opportunity to rebuild magic from the ground up. His Codex of the Unshackled challenges the [[Concordat of Chains]]’ strict arcane laws, leading to his exile.

Vera Malstrad, The First Archprelate (r. 2030s - 2050s)

Vera Malstrad was the first to hold the position of Archprelate of Godspel, an influential role in the early days of Hellhaven's judicial system. She created much of the legal framework still in place today, particularly the codification of laws regarding magical regulation and retribution. Known for her unyielding sense of justice, she personally oversaw several high-profile trials, some of which led to public executions. Though revered by many, Malstrad's strict interpretation of The Creed of Binding Light sparked fear and loathing in others, especially those accused of arcane practices. Her name became synonymous with the relentless pursuit of law and order.

Mara Vessier (b. ~2000s)

Leader of the Mnemonic Consortium A rogue arcanist who leads an underground group working to reconstruct lost magic, opposing Hellhaven’s strict regulations.

Grand Executor Thalienne Marzahn (b. ~2030)

Architect of the Creosmark system. A high-ranking bureaucrat responsible for implementing the Creosmark system, which binds Hellhaven’s citizens to their assigned roles through arcane contracts.

Commodore Edris Vahn (b. ~2050)

Navy Reformist integrating Vergrenzig tech. An ambitious naval officer pushing for the modernization of Hellhaven’s fleet with Vergrenzig aeronautical engineering, facing resistance from traditionalists.

docs.title: Trade Partners
docs.text:
• Republic of Rellavoss – A city-state with a powerful merchant council that controls much of the western gulf's trade. Locations/Settlements/Vermilion Republic/Rellavoss brokers deals between Hellhaven and less authoritarian polities.
  • Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig – An industrial powerhouse renowned for its steampunk and arcane-powered engineering. Vergrenzig provides Hellhaven with advanced machinery, steamships, and arcane-powered infrastructure, such as its engineered lighting systems.
  • [[Ironwreath Syndicate]] – A powerful cartel of industrialists operating out of the subterranean city of Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Khoz-Grimvar to the east. They export engineered arcane lighting systems, reinforced ship hulls, and steam-powered constructs to Hellhaven in exchange for processed petrolune and rare alchemical reagents.
  • [[The Pale Market of Quenhal]] – A vast trade network run by nomadic primordial merchants that controls the flow of exotic materials harvested from deep-sea trenches and the storm-touched tundras of the north. Their dealings with Hellhaven remain discreet, as they frequently sell goods considered illegal under the [[Concordat of Chains]].
  • The Commonwealth of Aexithis – A bureaucratic confederation of gnomish city-states specializing in ship automatons and arcane propulsion engines. Their relationship with Hellhaven is mutually beneficial, though fraught with tension due to their open acceptance of arcane magic.

docs.title: Allies
docs.text:
• [[Tidecourt of Vethmar]] – A submaritime kingdom ruled by a hereditary admiralty of sea elves, where noble houses are expected to contribute magically-enhanced ships that can dock underwater rather than land or wealth to maintain their status.
  • [[The Argent Bastion]] – A militarized theocracy in the northern mountains that reveres [[The Lord]] as a divine enforcer of law. They frequently supply Hellhaven with battle-hardened knights and inquisitors to aid in maintaining the city's strict social order, tolling through a trial where they cross [[The Chasm]] to reach their ally to the south.
  • [[The Caedrith Accord]] – A coalition of guilds and scholars who seek to regulate the lawful study of magic under strict theological doctrine. While they do not directly ban arcane practice like Hellhaven, they provide oversight and guidance, ensuring only sanctioned casters operate within allied territories.
  • [[The Sable Warden Conclave]] – A reclusive order of judges and executioners who travel between Hellhaven and its allies to enforce justice under the Concordat’s decrees. Their presence ensures no heretic or fugitive escapes retribution.

docs.title: Enemies
docs.text:
• [[The Umbral League]] – A network of rogue mages, anarchists, and exiled scholars who work to undermine Hellhaven’s rule and free those persecuted for forbidden magic. They operate in secret across the region, sabotaging enforcement efforts wherever possible.
  • [[The Crimson Tide]] – A notorious fleet of corsairs, privateers, and rogue merchants who directly oppose Hellhaven’s naval dominance. Their bases remain hidden within the labyrinthine inlets of Locations/Settlements/Free Isles/Istrecce, raiding trade routes and smuggling illicit goods.
  • [[The Luxborne Collective]] – A heretical sect that worships a pantheon of ancient, forgotten deities in defiance of [[The Lord]]’s singular dominion. They infiltrate the city’s lower districts, spreading their doctrine in whispers and shadows.
  • [[The Ashen Court of Luthrenne]] – An empire of necromancer-kings who reject the Concordat’s strict religious doctrine, instead ruling through legions of tireless undead servitors. Hellhaven considers their existence an abomination and has waged an undeclared war against them for decades.

docs.title: Neighbours
docs.text:
• The Free Enclaves of Istrecce – A loose confederation of island settlements and pirate holds that operate outside of official Gulf Concord law. They are frequently targeted by Hellhaven’s navy but continue to evade total suppression.
  • [[Velshyrn]] – A windswept fortress-city built into the cliffs south of Hellhaven, home to an ancient order of storm-callers and navigators. While neutral, their expertise in controlling the treacherous fjord currents is invaluable to the region’s maritime powers.
  • [[Néthivrë, the Drowned Court]] – An abandoned elven city half-submerged beneath the waves, now ruled by a cabal of deep-sea aberrations. Sailors whisper that its inhabitants were cursed for ancient crimes against [[The Lord]], and Hellhaven forbids travel to its ruins.
  • [[The Ember Holds]] – A chain of volcanic islands to the northwest, occupied by a mix of fire genasi, dwarven smith-clans, and warlike mercenary houses. While they trade raw metal and obsidian freely, their independence and refusal to kneel to the Concordat prevent closer ties.
  • [[Draeven’s Cradle]] – A floating atoll-turned-city, where exiles, debtors, and displaced communities have forged a society free from the influence of greater powers. Hellhaven keeps a wary eye on them, suspecting that they harbor fugitives and dissidents.
  • Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Irrhilm

docs.title: Language
docs.text: Hellhaven’s language has evolved over centuries of trade, religious doctrine, and technological development, leading to a dialect rich with legalistic phrasing, nautical terminology, and mechanist jargon.

docs.title: Dialects and Accents
docs.text:
• Godspel Speech – The formal dialect spoken by [[Concordat of Chains|The Concordat of Chains]] and legal authorities. It is precise, rigid, and heavily structured, filled with ritualistic phrases and references to The Creed of Binding Light.
  • Dockside Cant – A fast, clipped dialect spoken in Chainmoor Brine Yards and among the lower classes. It borrows from Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig trade lingo and often shortens words.
  • Tinker’s Tongue – A blend of Vergrenzig technical jargon and Hellhaven’s common tongue, used by artificers, mechanists, and alchemists in The Ironclad Sprawl.

docs.title: Developmental Impacts
docs.text:
Hellhaven’s culture is shaped by its history of elemental catastrophe, religious governance, and technological advancement.

  • Obedience and Regulation – Society is bound by strict legal codes, enforced from childhood. Even street slang retains legalistic phrasing, and contracts, ledgers, and bureaucratic approvals dominate daily life.
  • The Weight of Redemption – Those who fall into debt, criminal status, or heresy may enter "Redemptive Service," a form of indentured labor under the clergy’s oversight.
  • Innovation vs. Control – While Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig’s technology has advanced Hellhaven, it has also created tensions between those who seek progress and the clergy, who wish to regulate innovation to maintain authority.

docs.title: Cuisine
docs.text:
Hellhaven’s cuisine is influenced by maritime trade, coastal resources, and imported Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Vergrenzig ingredients. Common dishes include:

  • Brined Blackfish – A staple fish dish, cured in sea salt and spiced oils, often paired with sour pickled greens.
  • Chainmoor Chowder – A hearty stew of shellfish, potatoes, and smoked sausage, thickened with ground sea biscuit.
  • Steam-Baked Loaves – Bread made in geothermal ovens, producing a crisp crust and dense, warm interior.
  • Arcane-Infused Brews – Drinks such as Glowgin (a luminescent, mildly energizing spirit) and Ether-Touched Brandy (a distilled liquor rumored to heighten awareness).

docs.title: Rich/Poor Gap
docs.text:
• The High Clergy and Merchants – The wealthy elite live in opulent, towering spires with private lifts and skyferries. Their homes feature imported Vergrenzig luxuries, from self-winding automata to electric chandeliers.
  • The Industrial Class – Artificers, mechanists, and engineers earn stable incomes but remain under strict legal contracts, often forced into long-term service to their guilds.
  • The Debt-Bound and Redemptives – The lowest class lives in overcrowded, soot-choked housing, often forced into "redemptive labor," working in factories, shipyards, or clerical archives under surveillance.

docs.title: Outsiders
docs.text:
Hellhaven is suspicious of foreigners, but trade keeps the city’s gates open. How outsiders are treated depends on their background and purpose:

  • Vergrenzig Traders – Accepted as necessary trade partners, though many resent their influence. Their free-market ideals clash with Hellhaven’s controlled economy.
  • Drifters and Vagabonds – Viewed with distrust, often forced into Redemptive Service if caught without papers.
  • Religious Dissidents – Treated as heretics, often exiled or publicly condemned.
  • Innovators and Mechanists – Welcomed cautiously, but their work is heavily regulated by the clergy.

docs.title: ~ Society and Culture
docs.text: Perched between mountain shadow and sea-glow, Sauztein Geb is a fractured marvel, a city that dances on the bones of old tectonics, scavenges from the sky, and sings through spindled glass and lattice. Suspended across terraces, lifted platforms, and partially restored aerial shards, it thrives by salvaging, inventing, and reimagining. Mnemonic magic flows through its infrastructure, infusing memory with matter, craft with cognition. A haven for flight-specialists, scavenger guilds, and memorysmiths, Sauztein Geb is known as much for its ingenuity as for its volatility.

docs.title: Atmosphere
docs.text: A tang of ozone and rusted lightfract clings to the air, layered with the scent of hot stone, chemical brine, and flowering highwind moss. You hear the hum of gliders overhead, the hiss of memory distilleries venting steam, and the irregular toll of seismic stabilizers echoing from deep shafts below. There’s movement everywhere, carts, cranes, skyferries, and windwalkers on wired boots.

docs.title: Populace
docs.text: The people of Sauztein Geb move with purpose and a kind of collective half-focus, always multitasking, often mid-construction. Mages scribble glyphs into the air with silver styluses while tinkerers dangle upside-down from broken beams. Conversation is fast, technical, and oddly poetic. Memory-tattoos flicker across bare shoulders, and flight gear is common garb even among shopkeepers.

docs.title: Rapport
docs.text:
To outsiders, Hausztieners seem distracted, curt, or even paranoid, especially when discussing resource scarcity or Fabric instability. But those who stay long enough to prove they’re not saboteurs or thieves are often adopted quickly into small, fierce social circles bound by projects and shared trauma. Knowledge is traded like coin. Secrets less so.

Residents

Demonym: Hausztieners

Species Contour

While mostly elfin, Sauztein Geb is home to sky-blooded faerfolk, wind-bound elementals, and memory-born constructs known as Recallants, once-mortal minds bound to crystal bodies or mechanical frames. Goblin presence is limited post-Dreka Goro’s secession but still found in enclaves near the lower lifts.

History and Lore

Pronunciation: sow-stine gehb Meaning: Crystal's Bounty

Archaic Iterations:

  • Don Morcoux

    • Pronunciation: dohn mohr-coo

    • Meaning: The Gift of Chaos' End

    • An old name carried in prophecy-laced texts discovered in the vaults beneath the Riftglass Plateau, once believed to mark the final stabilizing node of a shattered continent. Replaced by "Sauztein Geb" after the rediscovery of the Crystal Wellspring and the establishment of mnemonic binding tech.

docs.title: Invention
docs.text:
Sauztein is one of the most innovation-forward cities in the Council due to its access to lightfract, a living crystal network that amplifies mnemonic and temporal magics. Invention here is not just mechanical, it is psycho-arcane. Artificers, scribe-smiths, and echo-forgers work in experimental harmony with memory-sourced blueprints, often creating devices that already remember how they should function.

The Chronoscribes regulate dangerous invention by locking volatile designs behind Mnemonic Seals, which require synchronized minds to access. Smuggled blueprints are often encrypted in dreamscapes.

docs.title: Distribution
docs.text:
• Lightfract Veins: Controlled by the Spirehands Guild and taxed by the Council.

  • Memory Crystals (Aetherlace): Allocated under Council permits, regulated by the Chronoscribes.

  • Filtered Echoresin: Distributed by the Hollow Choir's intermediaries to shadow-markets and low-tier inventors.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
• Nutrient Slabs & Synthmeals from Hellhaven Concord.

  • Binding Alloys & Fracture-Alloys from Winbor Coast refineries.

  • Soulglass Components from Drosvenna’s arcane salvage.

  • Fresh Minds, conscripted or “volunteered” individuals for memory-labor.

docs.title: Income
docs.text:
• Export of stabilized Lightfract Shards and temporal-laced relics.

  • Licensing Council-backed mnemonic prosthetics.

  • Illicit trade in blackmarket memory snippets and loop-sculpting art.

  • Council’s interest subsidies on experimental containment tech.

docs.title: 🏭 Key Industries
docs.text:
Mnemonic Crafting

Creation of memory-based devices, temporal stabilizers, emotion-charged tools, and recall tokens. Used in both medicine and warfare.

Lightfract Resonance Tuning

The refinement and shaping of Sauztein’s native crystal into usable infrastructure or psycho-reactive tech.

Memory Dredging & Loop Containment

Salvage and repair of timeline fractures. Recovery agents are trained to navigate nonlinear events and extract stable chrono-matter.

Echo-Engineering

Arcane-construction based on sound, harmonics, and memorywave attunement. Used to grow buildings, machines, and even sentient architectures.

Mind-Sculpting & Dreamsmithing

A luxury and blackmarket art, crafting or rewriting memories and personality shards for clients. Technically illegal unless licensed.

docs.title: 🎭 Niche Professions
docs.text:
Time-Attuner

Tunes personal devices to a user’s chronostability. Prevents unintentional duplication, collapse, or loop fragmentation.

Loop-Weaver

Designs stable microloops to preserve environments, art, or personalities in fixed-time scenarios. Sometimes hired to create haunted installations.

Shard-Daemonist

Specialist in semi-sentient crystal formations. Often bonded to a Lightfract warden-beast for urban maintenance.

Memurgeon

A surgeon who manipulates emotional and temporal scars instead of physical wounds. Used for trauma removal or espionage resets.

Echo-Sealer

Creates echo-null zones to shield areas from memory or time bleed. Common in high-security or ritual spaces.

Cognition Broker

Middlemen who trade memory-snippets, often customizing narratives for customers’ personal myths, trauma therapy, or addiction.

Dreamwright

Elite artisan hired to construct fully immersive mnemonic landscapes, often for mourning, inspiration, or rehabilitation.

docs.title: Companies
docs.text:
1. Lucid Helix Consortium Logo: A silver helix inscribed with runes around a fractured core. A semi-legal mindscaping firm that supplies high-end memory loops and fabricated lives to clients. Suspected to have ties to Dredger guild defectors.

2. Vaexial Harmonics Ltd. Logo: A tuning fork piercing a prism, radiating sound-lines. Official partner of the Spirehands Guild. Manufactures resonance tools and echo-safe materials. Funds public infrastructure projects.

3. The Sabled Guild Logo: A single blindfolded eye over a memory crystal. Elite Cognition Brokers operating in plain sight. They own parts of Shardmarket and sponsor underground artists who work with looped art or grief-vaults.

4. Synthread Corp. Logo: Interlocked memory tags forming a braid. Producers of memory prosthetics and narrative healing kits. Works with the Council in veterans’ clinics and trauma centers.

5. Choir of Iridescent Scar Logo: A cracked mirror wrapped in luminescent thorns. A front-company for the Hollow Choir’s mind-distribution wing. Officially distributes filtered lightfract and chant-infused talismans.,

docs.title: Planning
docs.text:
Sauztein Geb was not built in a traditional fashion, it grew, much like the resonant crystal that pulses through its foundations. Original settlements were small mining alcoves, later interlinked by harmonic scaffolding grown from Spirehand designs. Over centuries, neighborhoods emerged around resonance nodes, forming an uneven but reactive sprawl.

The city is semi-subterranean, tiered into crystalline hollows, shaft-cities, and resonance chambers, most of which follow the natural flow of the lightfract veins. Above ground, shattered crystal towers glimmer under dim skylight, while the true life of the city pulses deeper within.

docs.title: Districts
docs.text:
Core Districts of Sauztein Geb include:

  • Irid Vaults – The memory archive halls run by the Chronoscribes. Part library, part fortress, and part prison of unwanted pasts.

  • The Rootflumes – A living architectural region where Spirehands guide crystal-growth to house residential needs. Constantly shifting and humming with latent energy.

  • The Loamshaft – Lowest legal district before collapse zones; flooded with filtered lightfract. Home to poor laborers, smugglers, and dredgers.

  • The Upper Chime – Council-garrisoned plateau above the city. Host to administration towers and the eerie Resonance Bell, which tolls only during echoquake warnings.

  • Shardmarket – The volatile commerce center built atop cracked resonance. Street stalls sell memory-snippets, soulcrystals, dredged relics, and forged futures.

  • Hollow Choir Cloisters – Secretive, crypt-like sanctums carved into forgotten veins, used for sermons and synchrony by the Choir's followers.

docs.title: Modes of Travel
docs.text:
• Latticerails – Thin levitating tramways that “slide” via attuned harmonic pulses. Dangerous if mistuned, can trigger memory echoes.

  • Crystaspires – Vertical lifts powered by vibrational tuning forks. Sometimes fall into feedback loops during city-wide resonance flux.

  • Walkwinds – Subterranean walkways reinforced with echo-barriers to prevent cognitive spill. Many are privately guarded.

  • Chimebeasts – Semi-domesticated fauna bred for resonance navigation, used mostly in Loamshaft areas. Glimmer-skinned and eerily silent.

docs.title: Travel in the City
docs.text:
Navigating Sauztein means avoiding zones of high echo saturation, where time distorts or fractures may occur. Citizens carry memory tags, inscribed talismans tied to their current moment, to anchor their consciousness in linear flow.

Certain paths shift when the city re-harmonizes weekly, meaning maps must be updated constantly by the Spirehands and Chronoscribes.

docs.title: Entry and Reentry
docs.text:
Entry to the city requires passing through Mnemonic Clearance Points, where:

  • Your surface memory is scanned for hostile echoes or illegal grafts

  • Visitors are assigned a “Reverence Anchor,” a mind-stabilizing charm

Reentry is harder. Citizens who’ve been outside too long are subject to drift, where memory becomes misaligned. The longer you're gone, the more you may forget where you belong.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
• Resonant Crystal (lightfract, amberglas, shadestone)

  • Echo-etched Limestone

  • Boneglass (calcified, infused with sonic runes)

  • Rootmetal Filament – organic alloy grown from fungal-metal hybrid veins

Structures are partially sung into form by choir-architects or molded through vibration-sculpting.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Each building evolves with the needs of its inhabitants, walls bend subtly over time to accommodate emotional frequencies, and “echo doors” may open only when specific memories are thought of.

Districts sometimes shift their boundaries overnight during harmonic tremors. These events are called Veinbursts.

docs.title: Landmarks
docs.text:
• The Irid Archive Spindle – A shimmering monolith that spirals down 13 levels, housing centuries of recorded memory.

  • The Resonance Bell – Ancient crystal bell suspended over a fracture nexus. Its toll stabilizes the city... or shatters it further.

  • Mirror Hollow – A fault-pocket of pure mnemonic bleed, where visitors see versions of themselves that never existed.

  • The Lattice Cairn – A Spirehand memorial, pulsing gently with the death-harmonies of those who shaped the city’s veins.

  • The Nullspire Column – A condemned pillar of crystal where memory cannot exist. Used for exile or purification rituals.

docs.title: Climate
docs.text:
Sauztein Geb exists within a filtered geoluminal basin, light does not behave normally here. There is no traditional day-night cycle, but rather pulses of photonic bloom and luminous decay, both of which affect memory coherence.

Air is dry but thick with particulate resonance. Winds hum. Echostorms occasionally tear through sectors, leaving behind memory-slick surfaces and spectral afterimages.

docs.title: Flora
docs.text: Crystawheat – Edible shard-grain grown under false-light. Tough but sustaining. Glowfane Ivy – Climbs walls and lights districts at night, but may remember the voices it hears too often. Vireling Bloom – A fragile flower said to grow only where deep memory is buried. Used in mourning rites.

docs.title: Fauna
docs.text: Chimebeasts – Docile, vibration-sensitive mounts used by lower dwellers. Lurkrill – Insectoid tunnel scavengers, feast on memory-fragments. Dewdancers – Tiny glider-creatures made of silk and dust. They feed on psychic residue.

docs.title: Pests
docs.text: Shardmice – Glass-bodied rodents that gnaw through mindglass for warmth. Sometimes steal stray memories. Resonance Wasps – Aggressive creatures that inject mnemonic venom. Victims experience looping thoughts or false pasts. Nullmolds – Fungal infections that erase history from buildings and people alike. Dangerous and hard to detect.

docs.title: Symbolism
docs.text:
Emblem/Crest

A fractured prism set within a stylized eye, ringed by thirteen concentric lines (each representing a failed collapse prevented by Council intervention).

Mascot

“The Whisperwren”, a small, glass-winged bird believed to nest in harmonic flares. Its song is used to detect unstable memory pockets before they rupture.

docs.title: Settlement Leaders
docs.text:
Governance in Sauztein Geb is tripartite, but imbalanced: the Council’s presence dominates, local guild authority struggles for autonomy, and spiritual influences subtly manipulate beneath the surface.

  • [[Queen Liraenne du Virelys]] The current monarch of Sauztein Geb, descended directly from the astral elven line of Don Morcoux. Regal, inscrutable, and known for her radiant presence, she wears the Opalescent Crown with both grace and quiet dread. Rumors suggest she communes with something within the oldest ruins beneath the palace.

  • Overpréfet Cerid Banlot (Crystallis Council Spokesperson) Wields veto power over major legislation and coordinates Concord military deployment. Pragmatic, detached, and views the city as a crystalline fuse waiting to blow.

  • Guildmistress Thaerila Vennarienne (Chronoscribes Leader) Enforces memory legislation, manages the Irid Archive, and oversees the use of sanctioned mnemonic technologies.

  • High Resonant Tellun Sar (Temple of the Crystalline Veil) Spiritual authority across resonance rites and rituals; not officially part of governance, but his sermons are studied like law.

  • Magistrate Jessa Truanne (Civil Order & Mediation) Oversees court systems and inter-faction disputes; known for being both just and deeply exhausted.

Legislation

docs.title: Resonance Conduct Law (controls access to crystal harmonics, public rituals, and sound-emission technologies)
docs.text:
The Harmonic Limitation Decree (A.R. 1257)

Restricts public use of high-frequency resonance tools (like tuning-staves or harmonicscanners) due to their potential to:

  • Agitate unstable crystal networks

  • Trigger latent memory loops

  • Interfere with Concord communication nodes

Exceptions granted to certified Spirehands and Temple Chimebearers.

The Refractive Disturbance Accord

Signed between Concord enforcers and local guilds to regulate:

  • Mining methods near resonant crystal veins

  • Ritual song frequency use

  • Timing of public choral rites

Breakage leads to both fines and civic memory re-alignment (often forced reflection therapy).

Amendment 13-C: The Public Echo Curfew

Establishes a nightly curfew during which memory dredgers and resonance technicians must halt all operations. Why? Because during twilight and night hours, crystal matrices become volatile, leading to a higher chance of phantom projections (unintentional memory specters) and temporal bleed.

docs.title: Memory Regulation Doctrine (governs dredging, scribing, memory-trading, and identity preservation)
docs.text:
Directive on Mnemonic Property Rights

Defines ownership of one’s own memory. It’s illegal to: - Sell another’s memories without notarized consent - Embed false memories in mindglass without disclosure - Copy or fracture a “soul-sequence” for duplication or entertainment

Ethics Charter for Temporal Dredgers

A training and licensing document. Mandates: - Consent protocols before scanning someone’s past - Mindfield containment measures during echoquakes - Maximum allowed “temporal dip” duration before cognitive feedback risk

The Mindglass Confidentiality Mandate

Criminalizes: - Leaking memory-snippets from the Irid Archive - Using dredged memories as legal evidence without cross-verification - Storing weaponized trauma-imprints in public archives

Also enforced by the Council under civil security statutes. Violations can lead to memory erasure or exile to the Nullspires.

docs.title: Factions
docs.text:
The Chronoscribes

Time-law enforcers and memory archivists. Power centers in the Irid Archive.

The Spirehands Guild

Crystal-shapers and infrastructure builders. Control Rootflume architecture.

The Temple of the Crystalline Veil

Keepers of resonance theology. Their doctrine shapes public rituals and holidays.

The Undergleam Kin

Radical rebels, secessionists, and echo-sick outcasts. Hidden in the lower shafts.

The Lightfract Smugglers

Blackglass and resonance dealers. Control the illicit “emotional experience” market.

The Concord Representatives

External governors and military supervisors from Hellhaven. Prioritize resource security over local lives.

docs.title: Crime
docs.text:
Despite Concord surveillance, crime is rampant and often sonic, mnemonic, or metaphysical in nature.

  • Blackglass Trafficking: Illegal trade of volatile scrying crystal. Powers resonance heists and prophetic terrorism.

  • Echo Theft: Stealing identity-fragments from others, often resold to dream dens or used to forge artificial selves.

  • Fracture Poaching: Entering unstable zones without a dredging license to scavenge memory relics.

  • Resonance Sabotage: Weaponizing harmonic pulses to cause structural collapses or public auditory hallucinations.

  • Soulloop Sculpting: Creating illegal mnemonic loops for luxury reliving or torturous punishment.

docs.title: Current Threats
docs.text:
• The Echoquake Instability Fragmented temporal echoes have begun to resonate uncontrollably beneath the Rootflumes and Old Galleries, leading to localized time fractures, memory bleed, and spontaneous loopzones. Some areas have collapsed inward, pulling structures into unanchored pasts or futures.
  • The Hollow Choir A rogue sect of former Chronoscribes who worship the Echo Unformed, a theorized entity composed of untethered memories. They seek to deepen the fractures, believing full collapse will allow communion with a “pure astral self.” Hollow Choir operatives infiltrate rituals and sabotage stabilization engines.
  • Crystal Plague (“Refraction Sickness”) Caused by prolonged, unbuffered exposure to unstable lightfract crystals, this affliction leads to physical crystallization of tissue, sensory overload, and echo-induced psychosis. Though treatable if caught early, poor districts often delay care.
  • Lurkers Beneath the Gleaming Hollow Miners whisper of serpentine things glimpsed in reflective facets deep in the mines, mirror-skinned horrors that move without sound and eat memories instead of flesh. Reports increase every cycle.

docs.title: Adaptation to Threats
docs.text:
• Ward-Tuning and Echo Anchoring Civil engineers and mages specialize in pulsebound stabilization, a method of anchoring locations with rotating ley beacons and mnemonic wards. Neighborhoods pay tribute to guilds for regular re-tuning.
  • Crystal Licensing Handling of raw lightfract or “live resonance cores” requires certification. Unauthorized possession is punishable by exile or memory stripping (performed ritually by sanctioned Chronoscribes).
  • Memory Dredgers A public service caste tasked with recovering and reintegrating displaced memories caused by echo-slip. They act as emergency responders during fractures and occasionally work with lawkeeping bodies to verify testimonies through memory-stitching.
  • The Writ of Soft Treading A societal code practiced during unstable cycles, movement slows, conversations soften, and all wear non-reflective coverings. Crystals are dimmed to reduce harmonic agitation.

docs.title: Arcane Integration
docs.text:
• Architecture & City Planning Entire sectors are constructed with ley-etched foundations that “breathe”; pulsing in time with the city’s arcane lattice. Buildings are grown from crystal grafts, shaped by artisan-mages called Spirehands.
  • Everyday Magic
    • Glimmglyphs: Minor household enchantments etched in walls to create light, warmth, or sound muffling.
    • Echocharms: Worn to protect against memory slippage; usually set with a loved one's voice or a stabilized moment.
    • Public Transit: Involves short-range aether folds, which teleport passengers across fixed points via stabilized space-threading paths.
  • Chronoscript Law All official documents must be time-stamped magically, ensuring the moment of signing is stored within the page itself. Legal disputes often involve recalling and witnessing the moment of contract creation through magical replay.

docs.title: Religion
docs.text:
• The Lattice Divine (The Crystalline Veil) The dominant spiritual belief system sees divinity in interconnected patterns, not beings. Followers of the Veil believe all thought, matter, and time form an ever-shifting pattern that can be read through resonance, meditation, and prism-scrying.
  • Temples Called Vescaries, these crystal domes are tuned to amplify ley-song. Worship is often silent, focused on internal resonance rather than external veneration. Religious leaders are known as Resonants, and their status is tied to how clearly they can “hear” the universal lattice.

docs.title: Holidays
docs.text:
• Lumenwake A celebration of the year’s first full harmony pulse from the central Spire Core. Citizens hang lightfract wind-chimes and engage in ritual stillness to “catch the perfect moment.”
  • Echofall A memorial season when the veil between moments thins. People wear masks of those they've lost or were in past lives, and memory offerings (engraved on crystal shards) are sent down the Gleaming Hollow river.
  • The Silent Ring Once a century, the entire city falls quiet for three days, acknowledging the moment Sauztein Geb first heard the astral lattice. It's both a holy observance and a massive calibration of all magical infrastructure.

docs.title: The Opal Court & Council
docs.text:
• [[Queen Liraenne du Virelys]] – The current monarch of Sauztein Geb, descended directly from the astral elven line of Don Morcoux. Regal, inscrutable, and known for her radiant presence, she wears the Opalescent Crown with both grace and quiet dread. Rumors suggest she communes with something within the oldest ruins beneath the palace.

  • [[Archmagus Thévain d’Aurelac]] – Master of Arcane Conservation, responsible for studying, interpreting, and preserving the Novachron glyphs within the ancient stonework. Quiet and pale, with opal-veined eyes and a delicate touch with magic that seems to bend time.

  • [[Butler Alistelle de Lioranne]] – Noble representative of the fertile southern fiefdoms. Known for her charm, decadent salons, and politically dangerous gossip. Her allegiances shift like tides, but she always lands on her feet.

  • [[Comte Vaurien de Rochambre]] – Lord of the highland mines, his family manages the extraction of precious minerals from the crystal-laced caverns. Gruff and utilitarian, he sees the monarchy as sacred but believes in the strength of coin above all.

  • [[Seigneur Marné Vallisque]] – Merchant king of Sauztein Geb’s opal and spellglass trade. Wears rings laced with raw aural energy and speaks in glowing economic prophecy. Some suspect he’s secretly funding an arcane monopoly.

  • [[Chevalière Ylisse Dornévant]] – Commander of the royal guard, known as the Shardsworn. Stoic, battle-scarred, and unshakably loyal to the Queen, but whispered to have a personal vendetta against the swamp-dwellers of Hly’draug.

  • [[Victoire Nemevalle]] – High Priestess of the Luminous Echo, Sauztein Geb’s primary faith centered around ancestral resonance and starlight memory. Gentle in tone but utterly ruthless in rooting out corruption or false divination.

  • [[Maître Cerelune Briavell]] – Representative of the artisan caste and guild leader of the Weavers of Prismatic Craft. Wields enormous influence through enchanted fashion, memory-infused sculpture, and dream-distilled perfumes.

  • [[Warden Thrannic Delmarr]] - Grey dwarven Prince of Dwelreach, heir to the Delricht throne, and sole reason for the end of the Auroral Vein Dispute. Spends most of his time under soft guard in the Crystalseal Pavilion, but is present during public-facing events as a reminder to the Opal Court's power and influence.

docs.title: The Chronoscribes (Arcane archivists of memory and time)
docs.text:
• [[Archivist Elenvoir Morchaude]] – Stoic and prismatic-eyed, she leads the Chronoscribes from the Irid Archive. Known for her emotionless clarity and capacity to recall exact seconds from centuries ago.

  • [[Scribe-Lieutenant Jome Aethern'e]] – Oversees Echoquake containment; rumored to be experimenting with illegal mnemonic grafting tech to predict future fractures.

  • [[Memorist Vel Curneaux]] – A low-ranking scribe who illegally sells memory-snippets to black market artisans and memory dens. He seeks redemption, or at least escape.

docs.title: The Undergleam Kin (Tunnel-dwelling rebels and outcast communities)
docs.text:
• [[Rin "Coalcut" Marrev]] – A former Spirehand who turned revolutionary after her brother succumbed to Refraction Sickness due to poor zone management in the lower shafts.

  • [[Tahlin "Le Langue'eclat"]] – Prophet of the Hollow Choir’s fringe sect; his body is laced with growing, living crystal. Preaches a coming moment when “all time shall hum in one note.”

  • [[Maedren Skellieu]] – Smuggler of filtered lightfract for poor districts. Hates the Council for its exploitative mining practices and sabotage of memory dredgers.

docs.title: Spirehands Guild (Arcane builders and crystal-shapers)
docs.text:
• [[Maitre-Tailleur Alvix Dorneux]] – Oversees structural reshaping of the Rootflumes. Respected for his architectural genius, but slowly losing cohesion due to prolonged exposure to raw harmonics.

  • [[Apprentice Lurelle Vauxl'e]] – A prodigy who hears the lattice’s “whispers.” Secretly being courted by both the Council’s elite and the Hollow Choir.

  • [[Ruthen Bexot]] – Overseer of residential Spire-growth. Blunt, practical, deeply concerned about unstable districts, and suspected of passing info to the Undergleam Kin.

docs.title: The Crystallis Council Representatives (Governors, diplomats, and enforcers from the Hellhaven Concord)
docs.text:
• [[Overpref'et Cerid Banlot]] – Political liaison from Hellhaven. Believes Sauztein Geb is expendable if the crystal instability spreads.

  • [[Magistrate Jessa Truanne]] – A Council enforcer sympathetic to the city’s citizens. Maintains order with minimal violence, but her leash is shortening.

  • [[Dainhardt Glimmerung]] – Secretly part of the Ironwreath Syndicate. Posing as a Concordist official while mining influence, literal and metaphorical.

docs.title: Memory Dredgers (Recovery agents and first responders for echo-fractures)
docs.text:
• [[Draguer Ilim Myrthe]] – Famous for rescuing a whole district from loop-collapse. Carries dozens of stored memories not his own, and it's wearing thin.

  • [[Tessari Drahme]] – Works in the poor rings, often for free. Was once a scribe but now refuses to speak except in mnemonic glyphs.

  • [[Rokk Denlire]] – Veteran dredger with a mechanical arm fitted with tuning forks and harmonizers. Hates the Spirehands for abandoning his collapsed family zone.

docs.title: Lightfract Smugglers & Blackglass Dealers
docs.text:
• [[Vain "Mirrorcut" Solen]] – Dandy-like thief and rogue scholar of resonance. Collects rare reflections and forgotten timelines like trophies.

  • [[Casseth Orlun]] – Runs an illegal “memory bar” where clients relive curated emotional experiences. Ex-scribe with a price on her head.

  • [[Yvette Farv]] – Imports blackglass (unstable crystal used for scrying), and distributes it across unstable sectors to “accelerate the truth.”

docs.title: Temple of the Crystalline Veil
docs.text:
• [[High Resonant Tellun Sartre]] – Beloved spiritual leader who once sang a resonance so pure it stalled an entire collapse. Now fading, literally, phasing in and out of the moment.

  • [[Echo Sister Pryll]] – Enforces doctrine with unsettling serenity. Believes silence is sacred and often speaks through lightfract-script or gesture.

  • [[Vicar Jonrith Daiveux]] – A rising priest-artist who “paints with sound,” creating audible mosaics in public prayer domes.

docs.title: Historical Figures
docs.text:
Elvar'e “The Aegistone” Threnne

The first to stabilize a resonance fracture using only her voice and a cracked staff of lightfract. Died singing into the Gleaming Hollow.

Marnak Voleux

Founder of the Spirehands Guild, built the original Rootflumes by shaping them mid-collapse. Vanished into a prismatic fold; supposedly still alive in a pocket second.

The Marbled Prophet

An ancient Hollow Choir visionary whose body calcified into flawless crystal during a ritual. Her skull still hums under specific frequencies.

General Cassan Derrielle

Led the city's defenses during the Veilfire Uprising. Slaughtered echo-mutated Opalguard troops and then erased the memory of it citywide.

Raevaine Calloush

The Council-appointed arbiter who once ordered the memory-wipe of an entire caste. Sparked the schism that formed the Undergleam Kin.

docs.title: Trade Partners
docs.text:
• [[Drosvenna]] – A floating market city of scavengers, aerial tinkerers, and skybound mages. Trades in flight tech, scavenged relics, and modular skycraft parts.

  • Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Dreka Goro – A coastal enclave shaped by goblin culture. Exports strange sea-bound spices, jury-rigged devices, and salt-dried reagents.

  • Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Bo Renn – A rugged mining town at the base of the western mountains. Offers refined minerals, raw ore, and low-cost labor contracts.

  • Locations/Settlements/TO BE FLESHED/Cuirefyn – A northern roadside village nestled in the hilly plains. Renowned for herbal remedies, rare medicinal plants, and eco-alchemy supplies.

docs.title: Allies
docs.text:
• The Skywake Accord: An alliance of aerial trade pilots and mercantile dirigibles who favor Sauztein Geb for repairs and enhancements.

  • Vraekholdt: A high-perched cliffside settlement once nearly buried in a Fabric quake. Hausztiene engineers helped stabilize the cliff lattice, forging a bond of gratitude and joint seismic research.

  • Mirequay: A fortified, fog-wreathed town along the southern coast. Their reliance on modified Hausztiene filtration tech to cleanse their salt marshes led to lasting cooperation.

  • Tasselreed: A lowland agrarian commune where Hausztiene alchemists once helped contain a crop rot plague with memory-infusion techniques. Now a reliable source of raw alchemic staples.

  • Brasshearth Bastion: An isolated forge-city with deep volcanic roots. Shares experimental metallurgy secrets with Sauztein Geb in return for heat-resistant latticework and energy stabilizers.

docs.title: Enemies
docs.text:
• The Hollow Choir (Fringe Sect): Particularly the crystal-obsessed zealots who wish to dissolve Sauztein Geb into resonance.

  • The Ironwreath Syndicate: Criminal infiltrators aiming to siphon resources, sabotage governance, and weaponize mnemonic magic.

  • The Ravine Corsairs: Sea-raiders who occasionally make inland runs for lightfract and memory graft tech.

  • The Gleamscour: A radical eco-purist faction who blames Sauztein Geb’s existence for unbalancing the Fabric and unleashing Echoquakes.

  • Locations/Settlements/Ironbound Dynasty/Dwelreach: An underground empire of miners who blame Sauztein Geb's deep-lattice projects for a series of devastating echoquakes that collapsed half their mines, and blocked them off from extracting their ancestral birthright: the lightfract veins.

docs.title: Neighbours
docs.text:
• Yennoc’s Spine: A vertical settlement clinging to a rift in the southern cliffs; trades in smoked fish, oil-glass, and fissure-grown gems.

  • Klev’Sorn: A nomadic plain-fair town that migrates across the northern hills with great wheeled platforms, bartering seasonal produce and crafts.

  • Xereth Vale: A distant, isolationist society nestled deep in the western mountain fold. Rarely interacts, but tales speak of ancient resonance stabilizers and forgotten lattice scripts.

  • [[Harrowfen]]: A mist-laden village at the fjord's eastern bend, known for prophetic mushroom cults and soft diplomacy. Maintains a wary but non-hostile distance. One of the main southern Kagekunan entrances.

  • Nauzeret Strand: A coastal fishing settlement to the southeast with drifting trade barges and a superstition-laced view of Sauztein Geb's skytech as omens.

  • Fenbramble Reach: A northern marshbound commune using earth-speech and vinecraft; often called upon to assist with botanical anomalies in Hausztiene infrastructure.

docs.title: Dialect and Accents
docs.text:
• High Eltheric (Eltherai Valucien): The formal, ceremonial language used in law, academia, and governance. Rooted in astral phonetics, High Eltheric is spoken with elongated vowels, harmonic inflections, and rhythmic patterns that mirror the cadence of leyline pulses. Words may contain silent pauses, intentional gaps meant to reflect "lightbreath" (a tradition of respectful silence).
  • Low Eltheric / Crystal Cant: A more conversational dialect blended with miner's shorthand, artisan lingo, and borrowed dwarvish terms (especially among tradesfolk and the crystal-guild caste). It carries clipped consonants and occasional tonal shifts, developed for clear speech in echo-chambers and under ambient resonance from crystal structures.
  • Accents:
    • Corelight Accent: The elite nobility of the upper towers speak with a fluid, almost musical cadence, softened consonants, vowel glides, and astral harmonics threaded into daily speech.
    • Hollowtone: Those living closer to the deep roots or echo-choked quarters have speech patterns that emphasize guttural stops and echo-dampened syllables, reflecting environmental necessity.
    • Ridgecracked Drawl: A rugged tone common among boundary rangers and tradefolk along the Shiverpath, infused with dwarvish diphthongs and harsh cadence for overland or tunnel shouting.

docs.title: Developmental Impacts
docs.text:
• Magic as Infrastructure: The widespread use of lightfract crystals and ley conductors has created a city where even the poor enjoy some ambient luxuries, like warmth from lumenveins or crystallight in common thoroughfares. However, education in arcana is highly stratified, limiting who can truly wield or understand the deeper workings of the city.
  • Time Perception: Due to astral echoes and the cultural respect for fragmented memory, many inhabitants adopt a non-linear view of time. The past isn’t "gone", it’s present, accessible, even dangerous. This affects planning, emotional development, and historical education. Children are taught to interpret and not fear echo-anomalies.
  • Echobound Professions: Citizens often choose vocations based on family “echoline,” studying recorded memories or echo-glimpses of ancestors to “inherit” skills. Some trades rely entirely on this, particularly Glasswrights, Opalbinders, and Chronoscribes.

docs.title: Cuisine
docs.text:
• Crystal-Grown Produce: Underground gardens nourished by lightfract channels yield bioluminescent fungi, vine-fruits like telari pearls, and root-honey tubers.
  • Meat & Protein: Predominantly insectoid protein (from shimmercrabs and ley-burrowers), riverfish, and imported herding beasts from upland elfholds. Sauztein cuisine avoids heavy seasoning, instead highlighting textures and luminosity, a dish should glow, sing, or fracture in the mouth.
  • Common Delicacies:
    • Shattermoss Soup: A clear broth with crystal-flecked algae that pops and fizzes softly.
    • Auroral Caviar: From dreamfish caught near the Gleaming Hollow.
    • Whispercake: A dessert made from spun sugarroot and essence-capture, traditionally eaten in silence.

docs.title: Rich/Poor Gap
docs.text:
• Subtle Stratification: The wealth divide is reflected in elevation. The higher one lives in Sauztein Geb, the more access they have to stable echoes, clean crystal resonance, and ambient aether. The poor live in the Rootflumes, a district near unstable echo zones and sediment buildup.
    • Upper Castes: Fluent in High Eltheric, taught crystalcraft, often wear lightwoven garments that shimmer in tune with their heartbeats.
    • Lower Castes: Work as Refractors (echo stabilizers), Wickrunners (crystal maintainers), or Siltbearers (transporting unstable crystal runoff). They dress in grounding fabrics threaded with lead-pins or damping rings to avoid echo sickness.
  • Notably: Basic living standards are still relatively high due to crystalline infrastructure, no one starves, but opportunity is tightly controlled by caste and access to sanctioned arcana.

docs.title: Outsiders
docs.text:
• Dwarves of the Kagecombs: Viewed with tense respect. Dwarves are often seen as blunt and “too rooted,” but their mineral knowledge is unmatched. Many elves quietly envy the dwarves' resistance to echo influence.
  • Humans: Treated as dangerously fast-living and culturally reckless. Their short lifespans and rapid development cycles disturb the city’s measured pace. A human’s presence often signals trade, war, or theological confusion.
  • Drifters & Echoborn: Individuals with unknown origins who wandered in from unstable time fissures. Treated with suspicion, sometimes reverence. Many echo-priests believe them to be testaments from the Astral Collapse, living prophecies, or dangerous paradoxes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Description

Located in the fallen ruins of a draconic city from the Age of Arcanum, this mountain-road outpost in the [[Drakonspyre Mountain]] range is filled with all sorts of refugees from the law and ne're-do-wells. there is definitely a thieves guild. The leader is the person who last stole a coveted [[Gnosichron|Gnosichronian]] artifact. Thus, the leader changes often in a city of thieves and conniving merchants. Because of the nature of its populace, the city has outlawed the mapping of the layout to safeguard the residents, and has become known as The Uncharted City. However, these two verdicts are the only legislation limiting its residents, leaving them to their own desires.
